title: I Chronicles 18:13
text: The preservation of the people of God amidst the dangers to which they are exposed, and all the successes with which they are favored, come from him; and lay them under new obligations to love and obey him.

title: I Chronicles 19:2
text: Gratitude should ever be manifested for favors; and if it cannot be shown towards the benefactors themselves, it should be towards their children or others who were connected with them.

title: I Chronicles 19:3
text: Our best intentions may be misunderstood and misrepresented; evil may be returned for good, and that which should have been the means of forming and cementing friendship, may be made the occasion of enmity and strife.

title: I Chronicles 19:13
text: In a good cause, men should be of good courage; and while they use with fidelity all appointed means, they should feel their dependence on God, and commit the result of their efforts to him.

title: I Chronicles 19:16
text: The river; Euphrates.

title: I Chronicles 19:18
text: All efforts of the wicked to prevail against God and his people will in the end prove ineffectual, and be the means of hastening and aggravating their own ruin.

title: I Chronicles 20:1
text:
Rabbah; the capital of the Ammonites. 
 
  Tarried at Jerusalem; that is, as explained in  II Samuel 12:27-28 , till Joab sent for him, when he had nearly completed the conquest of the Ammonites. 
 
Reference to the sin of David in the matter of Uriah, which took place while Joab was besieging Rabbah, is here entirely omitted; and it is always proper to be silent about the sins of other, unless the cause of God and of truth requires the mention of them.

title: I Chronicles 20:3
text: Brought out the people; see note on  II Samuel 12:31 .

title: I Chronicles 20:4
text:
Gezer; a city in the western part of the tribe of Ephraim, bordering upon the Philistines. 
 
This is a world of trial, and one trouble will succeed another through the whole journey of life.  But to those who honor God in their trials, he will at last grant a complete and glorious deliverance.

title: I Chronicles 20:6
text: Gath; a city of the Philistines.

title: I Chronicles 21:1
text:
Stood up; presented himself as an accuser. 
 
  Provoked; moved, excited. 
 
Whenever the people of God are left to themselves, Satan stands ready to tempt them to the commission of sins which will bring distress, if not ruin, on themselves and others.

title: I Chronicles 21:2
text: Beer-sheba--to Dan; one end of the land to the other.

title: I Chronicles 21:3
text: A cause of trespass to Israel; a means of leading them into sin, and of thus bringing judgments upon them.  Joab seems to have understood that David was influenced by foolish pride in requiring this thing.

title: I Chronicles 21:5
text:
A thousand thousand and a hundred thousand; this sum differs from that given in  II Samuel 24:9 .  For some reason not explained, a portion of the armed men--perhaps those already enrolled for military service before this numbering--seem to be included in one account, and not in the other. 
 
  Four hundred threescore and ten thousand; for which we have, in  II Samuel 24:9 , the round number of five hundred thousand.

title: I Chronicles 21:8
text: Though the people of God may discover their sins, be deeply humbled on account of them, and be forgiven, yet if their sins have been open and brought scandal upon the cause of religion, the Lord will manifest his displeasure against them.

title: I Chronicles 21:12
text: Three years' famine; in  II Samuel 24:13 , we read, seven years of famine, which may be an error of the transcribers.  This might the more easily happen, as numbers were often indicated by letters.

title: I Chronicles 21:13
text: The penitent soul in all its difficulties will submit to the Lord, and commit itself and its interests to his merciful care and disposal.

title: I Chronicles 21:15
text: Repented him of the evil; he changed his course of conduct.

title: I Chronicles 21:17
text:
These sheep; the children of Israel, the people generally. 
 
The ingenuous soul mourns deeply, not only on account of its sins and the sufferings they bring upon itself, but for the evils they bring upon others whom they love, and whom they wish to benefit.

title: I Chronicles 21:25
text: Six hundred shekels; see note to  II Samuel 24:24 .

title: I Chronicles 21:26
text:
By fire; the fire descended from God and burnt up the sacrifice, in token of his acceptance of David and his offering. 
 
When the soul is duly penitent for its sins, submits to the judgments of God, and is ready to follow his directions, he is ready to forgive and grant manifestations of his mercy and love.

title: I Chronicles 21:28
text: He sacrificed there; continued to make that a place of sacrifice.

title: I Chronicles 21:29
text: In the high place at Gibeon; compare  I Chronicles 16:39-40 .

title: I Chronicles 21:30
text: Could not go before it; he feared to do so in the circumstances mentioned previously in this chapter.   I Chronicles 21:1-30

title: I Chronicles 22:1
text:
This is the house--this is the altar; that is, here on the threshing-floor which I have bought, and where I have sacrificed, shall the house of the Lord be built and the altar of burnt-offering established.  The tabernacle and altar which Moses built were yet at Gibeon, and there the daily sacrifices were offered.   I Chronicles 21:29  
 
The people of God, when delivered from the sad effects of their sins, will become more engaged than before in doing his work; and if they cannot honor him in one way they will attempt to do it in another, and thus to fill up life with fidelity and usefulness.

title: I Chronicles 22:3
text: Joinings; clamps of iron used to fasten work together.

title: I Chronicles 22:5
text: Good men live and labor not merely for themselves and their own generation, but for posterity and for all coming time; and their efforts will be felt not only to the end of the world, but to eternity.

title: I Chronicles 22:9
text: Solomon; meaning, peaceable.

title: I Chronicles 22:10
text:
For ever; so long as he should continue to obey God.  I Chronicles 22:12-13 I Chronicles 22:19  
 
The promises of God to individuals, are made on condition that they hearken to his voice and continue to obey his commandments.  If they forsake him, he will cast them off.

title: I Chronicles 22:16
text: If men would avail themselves of the blessings of Jehovah, enjoy his presence, and experience the benefit of his promises, they must be found doing his will.

title: I Chronicles 22:19
text: Bring the ark; from Zion, to which place David had already transferred it from Gibeon.

title: I Chronicles 23:1
text: The present and the four following chapters are occupied with an account of the orderly arrangements made by David for the service of the sanctuary and the administration of the affairs of his kingdom.  To the writer of the books of Chronicles, who lived after the Babylonish captivity, these were matters of deep interest, as they furnished a general model for the reestablishment of the state and the public worship of God.

title: I Chronicles 23:3
text:
From the age of thirty years and upward; in  I Chronicles 23:24 I Chronicles 23:27 , we read, "from the age of twenty years and upward."  The two statements may be thus reconciled: the Levites were distributed for the different services by thousands,  I Chronicles 23:4-5 .  Of these the great body, upon whom full service was laid, was from thirty years old and upward.  But to fill out the thousands a portion of younger men was taken, who discharged the lighter and less responsible duties. 
 
Nothing is more important to the interests of true religion than the increase of faithful ministers; and good men at the close of life, will be peculiarly anxious that a sufficient number may be provided and rightly employed for the good of coming generations.

title: I Chronicles 23:4
text: The work of the house of the Lord; all the service connected with the sanctuary, its revenues, and the ordering of the public worship of God.                                                       d

title: I Chronicles 23:7
text: Of the Gershonites; before giving the heads of the courses into which the priests and Levites were divided, the writer gives a partial list of the fathers' houses among the sons of Levi, embracing only such as belonged to the twenty-four thousand assigned for "the work of the house of the Lord."

title: I Chronicles 23:9
text: Shimei; not the Shimei mentioned in  I Chronicles 23:7 I Chronicles 23:10 , who was a brother of Laadan, but a descendant of Laadan.

title: I Chronicles 23:13
text: For ever; continually, to the end of the Jewish dispensation.

title: I Chronicles 23:26
text: Carry the tabernacle; from place to place, as in the wilderness, and afterwards in the land of Canaan.

title: I Chronicles 23:30
text: Religion is a daily duty; morning and evening offerings of prayer, thanksgiving, and praise should be presented to God, and such special seasons of devotion from time to time be observed, as he has appointed.

title: I Chronicles 24:1
text:
The divisions of the sons of Aaron; these divisions, it is supposed, were made by David according to divine appointment.  By them the priests were distributed into twenty-four courses, sixteen of the sons of Eleazar, and eight of the sons of Ithamar.  These served at the sanctuary, each course in its turn, from Sabbath to Sabbath, according to the testimony of Josephus, which agrees with the words of the sacred writer,  II Kings 11:5 II Kings 11:7 . 
 
Order and regularity are important in all concerns, especially in those of religion; and its ministers should all, in the place which God assigns them, attend with punctuality and perseverance to the duties of their office.

title: I Chronicles 24:5
text: One sort with another; the two sorts were those of Eleazar's sons, and those of Ithamar's.

title: I Chronicles 24:6
text: One--taken for Eleazar, and one--for Ithamar; one course of the house of Eleazar was drawn, and one of the house of Ithamar alternately, till the latter house was exhausted, when the remaining eight of Eleazar were drawn.  But some think that the original text implies that a double lot was drawn for Eleazar to a single lot for Ithamar.

title: I Chronicles 24:19
text: Under Aaron their father; all the priests were considered as successors of Aaron, and he is spoken of as their father.

title: I Chronicles 24:20
text: The rest of the sons of Levi; that is, who were not priests.

title: I Chronicles 24:31
text:
Over against their brethren; that is, as the original seems to imply, so that course answered to course, there being twenty-four courses of the Levites, corresponding with the twenty-four of the priests. 
 
  The principal fathers over against their younger brethren; so that no preference was given in casting the lots, to one division above another.

title: I Chronicles 25:1
text:
Asaph; he was descended from Gershon or Gershom, the eldest son of Levi.   I Chronicles 6:39-43  
 
  Heman; the grandson of Samuel, and a descendant of Kohath, Levi's second son.   I Chronicles 6:33-38  
 
  Jeduthun; supposed to be the same as Ethan, a descendant of Merari, the youngest of Levi's sons.   I Chronicles 6:44-47   Jeduthun signifies "praising," or "celebrating," and seems to have been a name given him from his office. 
 
  Prophesy with harps--cymbals; they not only sung inspired songs, accompanying them with instrumental music, but themselves received, at times at least, the spirit of prophecy.  To Asaph, twelve psalms--  Psalms 50:1-23 Psalms 73:1-83:18 --are all in probability to be ascribed. Heman is called "the king's seer,"  I Chronicles 25:5 ; and both Heman and Ethan (Jeduthun) were celebrated for their wisdom.   I Kings 4:31  
 
To praise God is one of the noblest services in which men can engage; and where it is done from the heart it is acceptable to God, and raises the affections to him.

title: I Chronicles 25:5
text:
Lift up the horn; blow it loudly. 
 
Children are the gift of God; and whether they be sons or daughters, the great object of parents should be to train them up for his service.

title: I Chronicles 25:7
text: All that were cunning; these two hundred and eighty-eight--twelve times twenty-four--were the teachers mentioned in the following verse. The remainder of the four thousand were the scholars.

title: I Chronicles 25:8
text: Ward; here put for a course of singers.

title: I Chronicles 26:1
text: The porters; these had charge of the gates leading to the temple. The temple was not yet built in David's day, but the porters were assigned in anticipation of it; and their offices are here described as they existed under Solomon and onward.

title: I Chronicles 26:4
text:
Obed-edom; who took charge of the ark after the death of Uzzah.  II Samuel 6:10-12  
 
Those who treat the ordinances of God with reverence, and are faithful in his service, may expect that he will prosper them and their children after them, and make them blessings to mankind.

title: I Chronicles 26:13
text: In the service of God, each one should stand in his lot, and be ready to perform his portion of labor.

title: I Chronicles 26:20
text:
Of the Levites; these seem to have been Levites who were neither singers nor porters, but belonged to the twenty-four thousand who had charge of the work of the house of the Lord, having special services assigned to them connected with the sacred treasures.  This will explain the fact that so many of the names here mentioned are those contained in the list in  I Chronicles 23:12-23 , while no name belonging to the singers or porters appears here. 
 
The treasures with which any one is intrusted should be guarded with care, and faithfully appropriated to the objects for which they are given.

title: I Chronicles 26:24
text: The son of Gershom; that is, his descendant.

title: I Chronicles 26:25
text: His brethren by Eliezer; Shebuel's brethren descended from Eliezer, who was also a son of Moses.

title: I Chronicles 26:27
text: As all our treasures come from God, a suitable portion of them should be devoted to the support of his worship, and the spread of a knowledge of his truth and will throughout the world.

title: I Chronicles 26:28
text: Whosoever had dedicated any thing; it had been customary for those who had property to dedicate a portion of it to the Lord.

title: I Chronicles 26:29
text: Of the Izharites; the sacred writer comes, in the last place, to notice the six thousand Levites who were officers and judges.  I Chronicles 23:4

title: I Chronicles 27:1
text:
Twenty and four thousand; these were kept constantly under military discipline, and were changed for as many others once a month. 
 
In those services which are needful for the public safety, all should be willing to take part; and as far as consistent, these services should be so divided as to bear equally upon all according to their ability.

title: I Chronicles 27:3
text: Of the children of Perez was the chief; or, Of the children ofPerez was he, being chief, etc.  Perez is, in the Hebrew, the same as Pharez the son of Judah, from whom also David descended.   Genesis 38:29   I Chronicles 2:3-12

title: I Chronicles 27:4
text: The ruler; a subordinate ruler under Dodai.

title: I Chronicles 27:7
text: Asahel--Zebadiah his son after him; Asahel had been slain at the beginning of David's reign, but his son Zebadiah seems to have succeeded him in the command of his division, which retained the name of Asahel's division.  When David--how early in his reign we are not informed--divided the army into the twelve divisions here mentioned, Asahel's came in as the fourth.

title: I Chronicles 27:23
text:
From twenty years old and under; these being unfit for military service, and exceedingly numerous, he did not attempt the labor of numbering them. 
 
It may sometimes be expedient and useful for the people of a country to be numbered; but this should be done for useful purposes and not to gratify pride, or lead men to glory in their numbers, prosperity or strength.

title: I Chronicles 27:24
text: Began to number; that is, to number the men of war who were twenty years old and upward.

title: I Chronicles 27:25
text: The division of labor, and the appointment of suitable persons to superintend every department of business, are essential to that regularity, diligence, and dispatch, which the highest prosperity and usefulness indispensibly require.

title: I Chronicles 28:1
text: As men draw near the close of life, they should endeavor to communicate such instruction from the word and providence of God, as may be most useful to survivors.

title: I Chronicles 28:4
text: For ever; that is, in his posterity.  David here refers to the promise, "Thy throne shall be established for ever,"  II Samuel 7:16 , which has its perfect fulfilment in Christ.  See notes on  II Samuel 12:16 .

title: I Chronicles 28:7
text:
If he be constant; had Solomon and his successors been constant in God's service, he would have established the earthly kingdom of David without interruption till it should have been merged in Christ, of whom the angel Gabriel said, "The Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David: and he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end."   Luke 1:32-33   But for their unfaithfulness the earthly successors of David were rejected for many centuries before the advent of the Messiah. 
 
Fidelity to God is essential to the reception of those blessings which, to the faithful, he has engaged to impart.

title: I Chronicles 28:8
text: In the sight of all Israel--in the audience of our God; supply, "I charge you."

title: I Chronicles 28:9
text: To be accepted of God, what men do they must do heartily as unto him, with a willing mind, for his glory and the best good of men.

title: I Chronicles 28:12
text: By the Spirit; as divinely directed.

title: I Chronicles 28:15
text: The candlesticks of gold; of these there were ten,  II Chronicles 4:7 . The candlesticks of silver were for uses less sacred, but which are not stated by the inspired writer.

title: I Chronicles 28:16
text: Tables of show-bread; here, and in  II Chronicles 4:19 , the writer speaks of the tables of show-bread as more than one.  Elsewhere one table for show-bread is mentioned:  I Kings 7:48 II Chronicles 29:18 .  Perhaps the writer means the table of show-bread and the other golden tables connected with it.  In  II Chronicles 4:8 , ten tables are mentioned.

title: I Chronicles 28:18
text: Of the chariot of the cherubim; or, "the chariot, the cherubim;" that is, the chariot of God consisting of the cherubim.  Compare  Psalms 18:10 .  The reference is to the two cherubim of olive-wood overlaid with gold, which Solomon placed in the holy of holies, and under the shadow of whose wings the ark was placed.  II Chronicles 3:10-13 II Chronicles 5:7-8

title: I Chronicles 28:19
text:
In writing; what God showed David with regard to the temple and its furniture, as related from  I Chronicles 28:11 , it is supposed he wrote down and delivered to Solomon for his guidance. 
 
The Lord will show his believing people all that they need to know; and in folowing his directions, however great or difficult their work, they may undertake it with resolution and go forward with cheerfulness, expecting that in due time he will give them success.

title: I Chronicles 29:1
text: The Lord chooses such as he sees fit, to possess power and exercise authority among men; on him they are dependent, and to him they must give account for the manner in which they use the blessings with which they are favored.

title: I Chronicles 29:3
text: If a man's affections are set on God and his service, he will willingly offer a portion of what God has given him to establish and maintain his worship among men.

title: I Chronicles 29:7
text: Drams; or, as some prefer, daries, a Persian coin estimated at about three dollars.  It was not in use among the Israelites in David's time, but is employed by the author of the books of Chronicles, as a coin well known to the Jews of his day.

title: I Chronicles 29:9
text:
Perfect heart; sincere, upright, for the purpose of honoring God.  I Chronicles 29:17  
 
Such is the nature of the human soul, that in offering its best affections and choicest treasures to the Lord, it is filled with gladness and exceeding joy.

title: I Chronicles 29:11
text: None can offer any thing good and acceptable to God, except what they have first received from him.  For all blessings, and for a disposition rightly to use them, men are indebted to his grace.  To him belongs, and to him, so far as they feel right, they will give, all the glory.

title: I Chronicles 29:17
text: Sensible that God looks upon the heart, and that nothing is acceptable to him except what is done in sincerity and truth, good men will seek from him a preparation of heart not only for themselves, but for their children and all who come after them.

title: I Chronicles 29:18
text: Keep this; this same disposition to offer willingly of their substance to the Lord.

title: I Chronicles 29:20
text:
The king; before whom they bowed, and thus paid civil obeisance. 
 
However greatly men may be honored in being instrumental of good to others, the glory they will give to the Lord, whose is the greatness, and the power, and the victory, for ever.  Amen.

title: I Chronicles 29:22
text: King the second time; his first anointing to the kingly office was on the occasion of Adonijah's attempt to usurp the throne.  I Kings 1:39

title: I Chronicles 29:25
text: Magnified Solomon; caused him to appear great in the eyes of the people.

title: II Chronicles 1:1
text: When the Lord is with his people they will be strong, and by his word, Spirit, and providence be furnished for every good work.

title: II Chronicles 1:3
text: There was the tabernacle; the tabernacle and brazen altar of burnt-offering made under the direction of Moses in the wilderness remained at Gibeon, though the ark had been carried to Jerusalem.  See notes to  I Chronicles 16:37 I Chronicles 22:1 .

title: II Chronicles 1:6
text: Communion with God and supreme devotion to him, are a good preparation for the reception of all needed blessings.

title: II Chronicles 1:10
text: Go out and come in; discharge aright his public duties.

title: II Chronicles 1:11
text: When men desire that wisdom which is from above more than they desire wealth, power, or influence, they may expect to receive it; and with it all things necessary for their spiritual and everlasting good.

title: II Chronicles 1:16
text: Linen yarn; or, as some render, caravans or companies of horses.

title: II Chronicles 2:2
text: Threescore and ten thousand men--three thousand and six hundred; see notes to  I Kings 5:15-16 .

title: II Chronicles 2:3
text: The establishment and support of the worship of God according to his appointment, and the spread of a knowledge of his salvation, is the most honorable and noble work in which the kings of the earth can engage; by it they not only honor God, but promote their own highest good and the good of the people over whom they are placed.

title: II Chronicles 2:6
text:
Should build him a house; that is, a house that can contain him. 
 
  Save only to burn sacrifice before him; he wishes Hiram to understand that he does not propose to build a house that shall contain God's majesty and glory, according to the notions of the heathen respecting their gods, but only a house that shall serve as a suitable place for his public worship, which the burning of sacrifices and incense here stands to represent. 
 
The more exalted a good man's views of God, and the more abundant his labors and offerings for Him, the more humble will be his views of himself, and the more entire his sense of dependence on the riches of divine grace.

title: II Chronicles 2:8
text: Algum-trees; these came in the ships that went to Ophir under the joint management of Hiram's and Solomon's servants, so that Hiram had a share in the work of procuring them.   I Kings 9:26-28 I Kings 10:11-12   II Chronicles 8:17-18 II Chronicles 9:10-11   They seem to be mentioned here along with the trees of Lebanon, because they were used in common with them in the work of the temple.

title: II Chronicles 2:10
text: Not only the mutual exchange of kind offices, but the exchange of the labor and productions of different countries, may be of service to all.

title: II Chronicles 2:13
text: Of Huram my father's; or, as some propose to render, Huram Abi; Abi, my father, being an honorary title borne by this artificer, whose name was Huram or Hiram,  I Kings 7:13 .

title: II Chronicles 2:14
text: Of the daughters of Dan; in  I Kings 7:14 , this man is called "a widow's son of the tribe of Naphtali."  Probably his mother was by birth of the tribe of Dan, but had married into the tribe of Naphtali.

title: II Chronicles 2:16
text: Joppa; the nearest seaport on the Mediterranean, about forty miles west of Jerusalem.

title: II Chronicles 2:17
text: With a proper division of labor and union of effort, and with the blessing of God on well-directed diligence and perseverance, the most difficult undertakings may in due time be accomplished.

title: II Chronicles 3:1
text:
Mount Moriah; an elevation in the eastern part of Jerusalem. 
 
However great or difficult the work to which God calls men, in his name and strength they should undertake it, with confidence that he will give them all needed aid.

title: II Chronicles 3:3
text: To those who are disposed to learn and do their whole duty, God will grant all needful instruction; so that they will see not only what to do, but also how to do it in order to meet his approbation, secure his blessing, and be made benefactors to mankind.

title: II Chronicles 3:6
text: Parvaim; perhaps a general name for the eastern regions whence the gold came.

title: II Chronicles 3:14
text: The veil; between the holy and the most holy place.

title: II Chronicles 3:15
text:
Thirty and five cubits; in  I Kings 7:15 Jeremiah 52:21 , the height of these pillars is stated at eighteen cubits.  Some have supposed that the height of each pillar was seventeen cubits and a half, with a base of half a cubit, making eighteen in all; and that here the joint height of both pillars is given. 
 
  Five cubits; in  II Kings 25:17 the height of the chapiters is given at three cubits.  In  Jeremiah 52:22 , it is stated at "five cubits, with net-work and pomegranates upon the chapiters round about."  It has been supposed that, in Kings, only the three cubits below the net-work are reckoned.

title: II Chronicles 4:2
text: The ordinances of divine appointment have ever been such as to impress upon men a conviction of their moral pollution, and the necessity of being washed in that fountain which Jesus Christ has opened to purify them from sin and all uncleanness.

title: II Chronicles 4:3
text: The similitude of oxen; small figures like oxen running around the brim of the sea in two rows.  In  I Kings 7:24 , they are called "knops."  They must not be confounded with the twelve oxen on which the sea stood.

title: II Chronicles 4:7
text: Men are naturally in spiritual darkness; and will never view things aright, unless the Holy Spirit shine into their minds and give them the light of the knowledge of his glory in the face of Jesus Christ.

title: II Chronicles 4:9
text: The court of the priests; called, in  I Kings 6:36 , "the inner court," as being next to the sanctuary.  The great court was for the Israelitish people.

title: II Chronicles 4:16
text: Huram his father; see note to  II Chronicles 2:13 .

title: II Chronicles 4:21
text: Treasures devoted to the service of God are by no means lost, but are safely invested where they will yield thirty, sixty, and a hundred fold.

title: II Chronicles 5:2
text:
Zion; in the south-west part of Jerusalem, and south-west from Moriah, the site of the temple. 
 
When a whole people assemble, and with united hearts engage sincerely in the worship of God, they may expect that their service will be acceptable to him and greatly beneficial to themselves.

title: II Chronicles 5:3
text: The feast which was in the seventh month; the feast of tabernacles, which was celebrated in the month of Tishri, corresponding to the last part of September and the first part of October.   Leviticus 23:34-43

title: II Chronicles 5:7
text: The cherubim; the two cherubim of olive-wood over laid with gold.  II Chronicles 3:10-13

title: II Chronicles 5:9
text: Unto this day; see note to  I Kings 8:8 .

title: II Chronicles 5:10
text:
The two tables; on which were engraved the ten commandments. 
 
The ten commandments express the will of God, and are the measure and the rule of human duty, under all dispensations, and in all ages.

title: II Chronicles 5:13
text: When the ministers of religion heartily unite in praising and adoring God for his mercies, he will accept their offerings, and give evidence of his approbation by delightful manifestations of his presence and favor.

title: II Chronicles 6:2
text: Thy dwelling for ever; the place where he would perpetually manifest his special presence.

title: II Chronicles 6:4
text: What God promises in his word, he will in his providence and by his Spirit faithfully perform.

title: II Chronicles 6:5
text: Neither chose I any man; to establish in him and his posterity a hereditary authority, as he chose David.

title: II Chronicles 6:8
text: Those who wish to do good, may in such wishes be accepted of God, when it is not his will that they should accomplish the particular object on which their hearts are set.

title: II Chronicles 6:12
text: When we have finished a work, we should in earnest believing prayer commend it to the blessing of God, without which it will not accomplish any good.

title: II Chronicles 6:16
text: The promises of God are often so connected with the faithfulness of his people, that their conditions must be fulfilled, in order to obtain their blessings.   II Chronicles 7:17-22

title: II Chronicles 6:20
text: Prayer is a chief means of obtaining that forgiveness of sin, without which there can be no deliverance from its power.

title: II Chronicles 6:24
text: Sin is the cause of all sorrow; and unless it is confessed and forsaken, it will cause sorrow eternal.

title: II Chronicles 6:28
text: Temporal calamities are God's servants; and are sent to remind men of their sins, and lead them to repentance, that they may escape everlasting punishment.

title: II Chronicles 6:32
text: God is no respecter of persons; but the prayer of the penitent, of whatever nation, kindred, or tribe, offered in faith, he will hear and answer according to the riches of his grace.

title: II Chronicles 6:34
text: The event of wars is in the hands of God: when his people rebel against him, he often suffers the wicked to prevail against them; but if they become penitent, and turn heartily to him, he will deliver them and grant them his salvation.

title: II Chronicles 6:41
text: When the ministers of God faithfully proclaim his salvation, and show its living power in their example, they may expect that many will embrace it, and rejoice in it with exceeding joy.

title: II Chronicles 7:1
text:
Fire came down from heaven; this was evidence that Solomon and the people were accepted in their offerings. 
 
The manner in which God shows his acceptance of his people is such as to fill them with awe of his justice, as well as adoring gratitude for his mercy, and bind them in willing obedience to his service.

title: II Chronicles 7:6
text: Praise is the spontaneous expression of truly grateful hearts; and is well-pleasing to God, and most useful to men.

title: II Chronicles 7:8
text: From the entering in of Hamath unto the river of Egypt; from the north to the south part of the land.

title: II Chronicles 7:9
text: The dedication of the altar seven days, and the feast seven days; the feast here referred to is the feast of tabernacles, which began on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, and lasted seven days,  Leviticus 23:34-36 .  The seven days of the dedication of the altar preceded the seven days' feast of tabernacles.  Compare  I Kings 8:62 .

title: II Chronicles 7:10
text: True devotion of heart to God, manifested in such acts of public religious worship as he has appointed, is a source of great joy to his people, and prepares them to return to their families and engage in the duties of life with new cheerfulness and success.

title: II Chronicles 7:13
text: No evil comes upon individuals or nations without the permission and control of God; and he is able and ready, when they are duly humbled, to remove it and manifest towards them new tokens of his favor.

title: II Chronicles 7:16
text: Sanctified this house; devoted it to a holy use.

title: II Chronicles 8:3
text: Hamath-zobah; Zobah was a country north and east of Palestine. Hamath was a city on the river Orontes, apparently belonging to Zobath.

title: II Chronicles 8:4
text:
Tadmor; a city in the great Syrian desert, between Damascus and the Euphrates.  It was afterwards called Palmyra, and has long been in ruins. 
 
So fading and transitory are all earthly things, the the most splendid cities may become a heap of ruins.  This should lead all to seek a city that hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.

title: II Chronicles 8:5
text: Beth-horon the upper, and--the nether; on the border of Ephraim and Benjamin.

title: II Chronicles 8:6
text: Baalath; a city within the territory of the tribe of Dan.

title: II Chronicles 8:8
text:
Tribute; a tribute of bondservice.   I Kings 9:21  
 
  Unto this day; see note to  I Kings 8:8 .

title: II Chronicles 8:11
text:
The city of David; Zion, the south-western hill of Jerusalem. 
 
  Shall not dwell in the house of David; he seems to have regarded this as too sacred a place for the residence of one who was a foreigner, not of Israelitish descent. 
 
A man's wife has a great influence upon him, and through him upon others; let him be careful that this influence does not mislead him into sinful practice.

title: II Chronicles 8:14
text: The commands of parents, so far as they accord with the commands of God, should be remembered and carefully followed by their children.

title: II Chronicles 8:17
text: Ezion-geber, and--Eloth; on the eastern branch of the Red sea.

title: II Chronicles 8:18
text: Ophir; a distant place visited by ships from the Red sea, the location of which is not known with certainty.  It is generally supposed to have been in either Arabia or India.

title: II Chronicles 9:1
text:
Sheba; supposed to have been a country of southern Arabia bordering on the Red sea. 
 
Those who know the value of true wisdom will seek to obtain it; and one means of this is, familiar conversation with those who possess it.  He that walketh with wise men shall be wise.

title: II Chronicles 9:8
text: All true wisdom comes from God, and habitual communion with him is the best means of obtaining it.

title: II Chronicles 9:12
text: A truly wise man will delight not only in receiving, but in imparting knowledge; and by doing it will become a benefactor to those around him.

title: II Chronicles 9:14
text: Chapmen; sellers, market-men.

title: II Chronicles 9:20
text: Silver and gold are a blessing or a curse according to the use that is made of them.  A wise man, therefore, will not be so anxious to obtain more, as he will be to use what he has to the glory of the Giver.

title: II Chronicles 9:21
text: The king's ships went to Tarshish; see note to  I Kings 10:22 .

title: II Chronicles 9:24
text: Harness; that is, armor.

title: II Chronicles 9:29
text: Book of Nathan--of Ahijah--of Iddo; books of Jewish history, not now extant.

title: II Chronicles 10:4
text: Expensive undertakings of rulers necessarily bring heavy burdens on the people, under which they become uneasy, and from which they wish to be delivered.

title: II Chronicles 10:7
text: Kindness in rulers often does more to secure obedience from the people, than force; and the longer men live, and the more they see of their fellow men, the deeper is their conviction of this truth.

title: II Chronicles 10:10
text: Youth are reckless, and often plunge into courses which bring distress and ruin upon themselves and others.

title: II Chronicles 10:15
text: The hand of God is never to be overlooked in the events of his providence, but is to be acknowledged even in those calamities which the folly and wickedness of men bring upon themselves.

title: II Chronicles 10:17
text: Rehoboam reigned over them; and also over the tribe of Benjamin, which was joined to that of Judah.

title: II Chronicles 11:4
text: Things which take place under the directing and controlling providence of God, are spoken of in the Bible as done by him.

title: II Chronicles 11:15
text:
Devils; demons, to which idolaters rendered religious worship. Compare  I Corinthians 10:20 . 
 
The worship of images is treated in the Bible as worship offered to devils.   I Corinthians 10:20

title: II Chronicles 11:17
text: As long as nations walk in the way of the Lord, they may expect that he will give them prosperity; but when they forsake him, they take a course adapted to bring ruin on themselves.

title: II Chronicles 11:23
text: He dealt wisely; in placing his children in different parts of the country, so that they should not unite against Abijah, whom he appointed as ruler over them.

title: II Chronicles 12:1
text: Great prosperity is dangerous; when it is granted men are increasingly prone to rebel against God, and thus to bring ruin upon themselves and those who join with them.

title: II Chronicles 12:3
text: Lubim--Sukkiim--Ethiopians; people living in countries bordering upon Egypt.

title: II Chronicles 12:6
text: When men become sensible of their sins, ascribe righteousness unto God, and humble themselves before him, he is ready to forgive and save them from that destruction which their sins deserve.

title: II Chronicles 12:12
text: Things went well; there were yet some good men, and things went well compared with what they had done.

title: II Chronicles 12:14
text:
He prepared not his heart; his reformation was merely external. 
 
Reformations which are merely external and in which the heart is not engaged, will not avail to the permanent removal of calamities in this world, or save the soul from destruction in the world to come.

title: II Chronicles 12:15
text: Of Iddo the seer concerning genealogies; that is, the book of Iddo the seer, which has for its object to give genealogical registers. These registers also contained notices of the acts of the persons whose genealogy was given.

title: II Chronicles 13:3
text: The frequency, prevalence, and devastation of war, show the wickedness of the human heart and the power of the great adversary in leading men in such vast numbers to murder one another.

title: II Chronicles 13:5
text: By a covenant of salt; all the sacrifices and oblations required by God's covenant with Israel were to be sprinkled with salt.  Hence it is called the salt of God's covenant.   Leviticus 2:13 Ezekiel 43:24   Thus salt became a symbol of the perpetuity of God's covenant with men, and "a covenant of salt" is a covenant that can never be changed or destroyed.

title: II Chronicles 13:9
text: When men cast off the true ministers of religion, and choose those who connive at and encourage them in their sins, they are ripening for ruin.

title: II Chronicles 13:13
text: None can contend against God and prosper.  However numerous or thoroughly disciplined their armies, and however skilfully devised their plans, they will be broken in pieces and flee before those who have the Lord for their helper and trust in him for defence.

title: II Chronicles 13:20
text: Life and death are in the hand of the Lord; and when he smites, the most mighty fall before him.  However numerous their attandants, they can give them no respite and afford them no relief.

title: II Chronicles 13:22
text: Story; or, commentary, that is, in the Latin sense, book of memoirs.

title: II Chronicles 14:2
text: Pious rulers are a great blessing to a nation; and by their efforts to reform the people and lead them to obey God, they prepare the way for him to bless them will all needed earthly good.

title: II Chronicles 14:3
text: The groves; or images of Astarte.  See note to  Deuteronomy 16:21 .

title: II Chronicles 14:9
text:
Zerah the Ethiopian; in the Hebrew, Zerah the Cushite.  It has been doubted whether he was a king of the Arabian Cushites or of the African Cushites, that is, the Ethopians properly so called in Africa, south of Egypt.  But since he came from the direction of Egypt and fled towards Egypt and had the Lubim, that is, Libyans, in his service,  II Chronicles 16:8 , it seems more probable that he was an Egyptian king of an Ethopian dynasty, and had also Ethiopians, as well as Egyptians and Libyans in his service. 
 
  Mareshah; in the south western part of Judah, near the Philistines. 
 
Although it is our duty in times of trouble to use all suitable means to help ourselves, yet our dependence for deliverance should be upon God.  He can save by few or by many, and is ready to help all who truly trust in him.

title: II Chronicles 14:13
text: Gerar; a city of the Philistines near the southern border of Palestine.

title: II Chronicles 14:14
text: They smote all the cities round about Gerar; probably as being confederates with Zerah, as would naturally be the case if he was an Egyptian king.

title: II Chronicles 15:2
text: The Lord encourages those who seek him, with special manifestations of his presence and favor; while he warns those who forsake him, that he will forsake them, and leave them to that ruin which they deserve.

title: II Chronicles 15:3
text: Israel hath been without the true God; the exact reference of this verse and the three following is doubtful.  Some suppose that the prophet is giving a general description of the unsettled times of the judges: "Now for a long season Israel was without the true God," etc. According to this interpretation, the third verse would describe the general ignorance of the people.  The mass of them were without the true knowledge of God and his law; and, though there were regular priests, few resorted to them for instruction.  Others suppose the reference to be to the kingdom of Israel after its separation from that of Judah: "Now for a long season Israel hath been without the true God," etc.  The fourth verse will then refer to the pious remnant among the ten tribes.  Compare  II Chronicles 15:9 .

title: II Chronicles 15:7
text:
Be ye strong therefore; he applies the past history of God's people to the case of Asa and his kingdom.  If they will believe in God and serve him steadfastly they shall be delivered, as their fathers have been. 
 
The certainty that if men engage and persevere in well-doing they shall be graciously and abundantly rewarded, should make them steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord.

title: II Chronicles 15:8
text: Oded the prophet; or, as in  II Chronicles 15:1 , Azariah the son of Oded.

title: II Chronicles 15:9
text: Evidence of the presence and favor of God will draw together multitudes, of all classes who love him, to acknowledge his goodness and render united thanks to his holy name.

title: II Chronicles 15:16
text:
Because she had made an idol in a grove; rather, Because she had made an image of Astarte. 
 
  Kidron; a torrent-bed between Jerusalem and the mount of Olives, which ran through the valley of Jehoshaphat into the Dead sea. 
 
No natural affection, or regard to relatives and friends, should lead us to connive at their sins, or prevent us from taking decided measures to resist their evil influence.

title: II Chronicles 15:17
text: But the high places were not taken away; see note to  I Kings 15:14 .

title: II Chronicles 15:19
text: Unto the five and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa; see note to  II Chronicles 16:1 .

title: II Chronicles 16:1
text:
In the six and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa; Baasha began to reign in the third year of Asa, and he reigned twenty-four years.  I Kings 15:33   Thus he died in the twenty-seventh year of Asa's reign. It has been supposed that an error has occurred in the number here given.  Numbers were anciently indicated by letters, whence mistakes in transcribing them might more readily occur. 
 
  Baasha--built Ramah; see note on  I Kings 15:17 .

title: II Chronicles 16:2
text: When men in trouble rely upon their own efforts merely, or look for help to thier fellow men instead of trusting in the Lord, they dishonor him, and may expect that he will visit them with tokens of his displeasure.

title: II Chronicles 16:10
text: Men, when reminded of their sins, instead of forsaking them, are sometimes angry with him who reminds them, and persecute him for his fidelity.  But this increases their guilt, and ripens them for the just judgments of God.

title: II Chronicles 16:14
text: A very great burning; of sweet spices.

title: II Chronicles 17:3
text: A succession of pious rulers is a great blessing to a people, and opens the way for permanent peace and prosperity.

title: II Chronicles 17:6
text: Lifted up; encouraged, strengthened.

title: II Chronicles 17:7
text:
To teach; teach the people the will of God. 
 
The teaching of the word and will of God to all the people, is the grand means of leading them to obey him, and thus securing his favor.

title: II Chronicles 17:10
text:
The fear of the Lord; a great dread, so that they did not dare to war against his servant. 
 
When a man's ways please the Lord, he maketh his enemies to be at peace with him; and they who seek Jehovah as their chief good, will not want any good thing.

title: II Chronicles 17:19
text: Fenced; fortified.

title: II Chronicles 18:1
text:
vv 1-34. 
 
See notes to  I Kings 22:1-36 . 
 
Great wealth is a source of great temptations, and among them is that of forming intimate connections with the rich and great, though they are enemies to the truth and will of God.

title: II Chronicles 18:3
text: When good men yield to the enticements of the wicked, and unite in their plans, without inquiring as to the will of God, or in opposition to it when known, they are preparing for trouble.

title: II Chronicles 18:5
text: False teachers are numerous; and those who reject the testimony of God, are suffered to be deceived by them to their ruin.

title: II Chronicles 18:7
text: Faithful ministers promise no good to the wicked, and on this account are often hated and rejected by them; while the friends of God desire to know his will.

title: II Chronicles 18:12
text: Worldly minded men think those the best preachers who best please their hearers; and that no message can be good which they dislike and reject.

title: II Chronicles 18:20
text: Satan is the father of lies, and will, if suffered, be a lying spirit in the mouth of all false teachers, and deceive those who follow them to their destruction.   Genesis 2:17 Genesis 3:4 Genesis 3:5 John 8:44

title: II Chronicles 18:27
text: Though men may by falsehood be deceived for a time, the final event, as all faithful teachers know, will effectually undeceive them.

title: II Chronicles 18:31
text: Though good men by their own folly and wickedness may bring themselves into great trouble, yet if they turn heartily to God he will so order events in his providence that they shall escape.

title: II Chronicles 18:33
text: A bow drawn at a venture, and an arrow sent at random, so far as the agency of man is concerned, may be so guided by God as to fulfil his predictions and manifest to all the truth of his word.

title: II Chronicles 19:2
text: Intimate connections with the openly ungodly are displeasing to God, and dangerous to men.

title: II Chronicles 19:3
text: The groves; or, images of Astarte.

title: II Chronicles 19:4
text: He went out again through the people; the reference is to  II Chronicles 17:7-9 , where it is related how Jehoshaphat sent teachers throughout his kingdom.  As these teachers went under his direction, he may be said to have gone forth on this mission, whether he personally accompanied them or not.

title: II Chronicles 19:6
text:
But for the Lord; because judges are appointed to administer justice in God's name, and must render an account to him of the manner in which they fulfil the duties of their office. 
 
Magistrates are God's ministers, and should by impartial and just decisions approve themselves to him, and guard the rights of all their fellow men.

title: II Chronicles 19:7
text: Gifts; bribes to pervert judgment.

title: II Chronicles 19:10
text:
Between blood and blood; where the question is who is guilty of shedding blood. 
 
  Between law and commandment--judgments; where the question is as to the right understanding or application of any of the Mosaic ordinances.

title: II Chronicles 19:11
text:
Matters of the Lord; pertaining to the service of the Lord; and so, "the judgment of the Lord,"  II Chronicles 19:8 . 
 
  The king's matters; pertaining to the civil administration of the government under the king. 
 
True courage is essential to obedience to God; and none who do not regard him more than men, will ever be accepted of him.

title: II Chronicles 20:2
text:
The sea; the Dead sea. 
 
  Engedi; on the western shore of the Dead sea.

title: II Chronicles 20:3
text: This is a world of trials, and none in passing through it can escape them; but if they, in despair of all human help, look to the Lord and depend upon him, he will in due time appear for them and grant them relief.

title: II Chronicles 20:7
text: The past mercies of God should be remembered with gratitude, and may be pleaded as reasons for the continuance of his favors and for the bestowment of future blessings.

title: II Chronicles 20:10
text: Mount Seir; a mountainous country south of the Dead sea, inhabited by the Edomites.

title: II Chronicles 20:12
text: The less we depend upon ourselves or creatures, and the more entire our dependence is on God, the more certainly will help come from him.

title: II Chronicles 20:15
text: When God undertakes to fight for his people, however numerous or powerful their foes, he will give his people the victory, and in such a manner as to manifest his own glory.

title: II Chronicles 20:16
text:
Ziz; a pass at Engedi, by which the enemy would go up to the interior of Judah. 
 
  Brook; or ravine.

title: II Chronicles 20:20
text:
Tekoa; a place south of Bethlehem, on the border of the desert. It lay on the route from Jerusalem to Engedi, and appears to have been connected with "the wilderness of Jeruel,"  II Chronicles 20:16 . 
 
Faith in God is an earnest of success, and prepares the soul to hail his interposition with gladness and joy.

title: II Chronicles 20:22
text:
The Lord set ambushments; the nature of these ambushments cannot be clearly determined.  Some have supposed that they consisted of bands of angels; others, that through the influence of a spirit of jealousy and discord, one portion of the allied forces set ambushments against the rest; others still, that, by a delusion sent upon them from God, the ambushments which they had set for Judah fell upon their own allies. 
 
  Were smitten; rather, "smote one another."

title: II Chronicles 20:23
text: God can grant deliverance to his people, by leaving their enemies to fight against and destroy one another; so that while his people stand still, they see the salvation of God.

title: II Chronicles 20:26
text: Berachah; that is, blessing.

title: II Chronicles 20:29
text: The fear of the Lord is the best security of his people, and when he gives them rest and quietness none shall make them afraid.

title: II Chronicles 20:34
text: Who is mentioned; or, who is brought into; that is, whose writings are inserted.

title: II Chronicles 20:35
text: Good men who unite with the wicked, dishonor God, injure his cause, and bring disappointment, trouble, and distress upon themselves.

title: II Chronicles 20:36
text: Ships to go to Tarshish; in  I Kings 22:48 , it is said that Jehoshaphat "made ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold."  The ships were made at Ezion-geber, on the eastern arm of the Red sea, which was the port for Ophir.  It has been supposed that by "ships of Tarshish" are meant ships of a particular construction fitted for navigating the open sea, such as those originally employed in the trade with Tarshish; and that in process of time all ships of this form and size were called "ships of Tarshish," without regard to their destination.  But in the present passage the ships are made "to go to Tarshish."  How this statement is to be reconciled with that in Kings is not agreed.  Some have assumed the existence of a second Tarshish in the direction of Ophir; others, that the fleet was expected to circumnavigate Africa, taking Ophir on its way, and returning by Tarshish in Spain.  It is possible, however, that, in the days of the author of the Chronicles, "Tarshish" had come to be an indefinite term for remote regions that must be approached by sea.

title: II Chronicles 21:1
text: The city of David; the hill of Zion,  II Chronicles 5:2 .

title: II Chronicles 21:3
text: Divine grace is not inherited; and no parent can know what will be the state of his children after he is dead.

title: II Chronicles 21:4
text: Slew all his brethren; lest they should rebel against his authority.

title: II Chronicles 21:6
text: Intimate connections with the openly wicked tend to corrupt the heart, debase the character, and ripen the soul for the vengeance of God.

title: II Chronicles 21:10
text: Libnah; in the south-western part of Judah.

title: II Chronicles 21:12
text:
A writing; it is commonly supposed that Elijah prepared this awful message before his death by God's direction, and left it to be communicated to Jehoram at the proper time; just as he fulfilled the command to anoint Jehu king over Israel and Hazael king over Syria, not in his own person, but by the ministry of others. 
 
The wickedness of the wicked is all known to Jehovah, and in due time he will punish it as it deserves.

title: II Chronicles 21:18
text: The effects of sin are often terrible in this world, and dreadful warnings of the misery which awaits it in the world to come.

title: II Chronicles 21:19
text: No burning; of sweet spices, as a mark of honor.

title: II Chronicles 21:20
text: Without being desired; the people did not desire that he should live, nor did they mourn his death.

title: II Chronicles 22:2
text: Forty and two; in  II Kings 8:26 , we find "twenty and two," which must be the right reading, since Jehoram his father was but forty years old when he died.  See  II Chronicles 21:20 .

title: II Chronicles 22:3
text: Those parents who counsel their children to do wrong, are often the means of their destruction, temporal and eternal.

title: II Chronicles 22:5
text: Those who knowingly do wrong are not unfrequently given up of God to pursue such courses as involve themselves and their connections in irretrievable ruin.

title: II Chronicles 22:9
text: He was hid in Samaria; see note to  II Kings 9:27 .

title: II Chronicles 22:10
text:
Destroyed all the seed royal; that they might not disturb her in reigning over the people. 
 
The judgments of God upon the wicked, instead of being improved as a warning against sin, are sometimes made the occasion of greater transgressions, which bring down heavier divine judgments.

title: II Chronicles 23:1
text:
vv 1-21. 
 
Compare  II Kings 11:1-21 . 
 
Revolutions in human governments are sometimes needful; and those who are most distinguished by wisdom, integrity, and influence, are the best fitted to take the direction of them, and to conduct them to successful results.

title: II Chronicles 23:3
text: The king's son; Joash the son of Ahaziah.

title: II Chronicles 23:8
text: Power to select rulers is with the people, and in doing it they should regard the word and will of God; selecting such persons and conducting in such a manner as will meet his approbation.

title: II Chronicles 23:13
text: Usurpers and those who have been guilty of treason themselves, are among the first to cry out against it in others.  But not every revolution is wrong, nor should the cry of "Treason!" hinder those who have power, from placing the government in the hands of such as will use it for the glory of God and the good of mankind.

title: II Chronicles 23:14
text: Ranges; ranks of guards around the temple.

title: II Chronicles 23:18
text: Whatever be the form of government, and whoever is called to administer it, it should be carried on in accordance with the revealed will of God; and should protect all in their just rights, especially the right to worship their Maker according to the dictates of conscience.

title: II Chronicles 24:2
text: It is a great blessing for men, especially when young, to be surrounded with wise and pious counsellors; and in following their advice they will find the ways of wisdom to be ways of pleasantness and her paths to be paths of peace.

title: II Chronicles 24:4
text: Mnay are zealous in the externals of religion who have no real piety; and who, when left to the flattery of the wicked, will cast off the appearance of religion and be guilty of the most abominable iniquity.

title: II Chronicles 24:6
text: The commandment of Moses;

title: II Chronicles 24:7
text: Wicked rulers, by their profane treatment of sacred things, corrupt the hearts of the people and bring down upon them the just judgments of God.

title: II Chronicles 24:10
text: When rulers, by their profane treatment of sacred things, corrupt the hearts of the people and bring down upon them the just judgments of God.

title: II Chronicles 24:14
text: Continually; the daily burnt-offering prescribed in the law of Moses is referred to.

title: II Chronicles 24:17
text:
Made obeisance to the king; rendered him homage, and made entreaty unto him for the restoration of idolatry in Judah. 
 
When pious persons who have been instrumental in keeping up public worship are removed by death, survivors who have no love for it often renounce it, and show by their conduct that their appearance of religion sprung from regard to men, not to God.

title: II Chronicles 24:18
text: Groves; or images of Astarte.

title: II Chronicles 24:19
text: Apostates who have cast off the fear of the Lord, are exceedingly averse to being reproved for their sins, and often hate, persecute, and even kill those who reprove them.

title: II Chronicles 24:22
text:
Require; that is, punish it. 
 
Though God sometimes suffers the wicked to kill his servants, and their punishment may be for a while delayed, it will, unless they repent, in due time overtake them.

title: II Chronicles 24:24
text:
Executed judgement; the just judgments of God against Joash for his sins. 
 
With a very small company God can easily overcome and desolate the country of those who rebel against him, and show them, by their punishment, his wrath against their iniquity.

title: II Chronicles 24:27
text: Burdens; either burdens in the sense of heavy judgments from God, or as the same word is rendered in  II Chronicles 17:11 , burdens of tribute imposed on him by the conquerors.

title: II Chronicles 25:2
text:
He did that which was right; externally, and for a time. 
 
Many for a time do that externally which is right, who have no supreme regard to God, and whose services for this reason are not accepted of him.

title: II Chronicles 25:5
text: When men engage in projects without asking counsel of the Lord, they may expect them to be sources of trouble, if not of ruin.

title: II Chronicles 25:6
text: He hired also a hundred thousand mighty men; to assist him in a war which he proposed against the Edomites.

title: II Chronicles 25:7
text: Men, out of regard to their own interests merely, sometimes do externally as the Lord directs, and thus save themselves from many of the evils which would otherwise come upon them.

title: II Chronicles 25:9
text: Men are often very reluctant to do what is right, on account of the pecuniary sacrifice it may involve; but whatever be the sacrifice it may involve; but whatever be the sacrifice which obedience to God may occasion, it is wise to make it, for God can give us much more than we lose for his sake.

title: II Chronicles 25:11
text: Children of Seir; Edomites.

title: II Chronicles 25:12
text:
Unto the top of the rock; the word in the original for rock is Sela, the same as that used in  II Kings 14:7 .  Sela is generally considered to have been the same as Petra, (rock,) a celebrated city of Edom lying in a valley surrounded by precipices of rock, from which it received its name. 
 
Apostasy and cruelty are often united.  War tends to the production and increase of both, and is a source of innumerable evils to mankind.

title: II Chronicles 25:14
text: That men who know the true God and have received special blessings from him, should renounce his service, bow down to idols, and expect to be gainers by it, shows that the heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked.

title: II Chronicles 25:16
text: When men persevere in rejecting the counsel of God, it is evidence that he intends to destroy them.

title: II Chronicles 25:17
text:
Let us see one another; let us try our strength together in battle. On this whole narrative,  II Chronicles 25:17-24 , see  II Kings 14:8-14 , and the notes upon that passage. 
 
As a punishment for their sins, God often suffers the wicked, in gratification of their pride, to engage in projects which occasion their ruin.

title: II Chronicles 25:27

II Kings 16:5 Isaiah 7:1-2   Of the three different accounts which we have of this war-- II Kings 16:5-9 Isaiah 7:1-9 , and the present passage--no one contains a full history of all the events that took place. title: Ezra 2:1
text:
The children of the province; those who had been carried away from Judea--here spoken of as a province of the Persian empire--and their descendants, who now returned.  This catalogue is repeated in  Nehemiah 7:6-69 , with various differences, however, in respect to names and numbers.  The differences of names may be easily explained from the fact that it was common for men to bear different titles, particularly if they were persons of distinction; as, for example, Daniel and Belteshazzar, Zerubbabel and Sheshbazzar.  It is not certain upon what principle the differences in numbers are to be explained.  The sum total of both catalogues is the same, namely, forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty; from which it is plain that the lists are in both cases partial, since neither of them amounts to this sum.  "The sum of the numbers, as separately detailed, will correspond, if to the twenty-nine thousand eight hundred and sixty-five persons reckoned by Nehemiah which Ezra has omitted; and, on the other hand, to the thirty-one thousand and eighty-nine enumerated by Nehemiah, add the four hundred and ninety-four, which is an overplus in Ezra, not noticed by Nehemiah; both writers including in the sum total ten thousand seven hundred and seventy-seven of the mixed multitude, not particularized in the individual detail."

title: Ezra 7:21
text: Rulers who not only favor the cause of God, but use their influence to gain the cooperation of others, may expect a blessing on themselves and their fellow men.

title: Ezra 7:27
text: Blessed be the Lord God; the exclamation of Ezra in view of what God had done for him and the Jews, especially in inclining the king to favor them.

title: Ezra 8:15
text:
Ahava; in Assyria, on a river of the same name, which emptied into the Euphrates.   Ezra 8:21  
 
Ministers are sometimes backward to engage in difficult and perilous services, and need, by the exhortation of their more zealous brethren, to be stirred up to their duty.

title: Ezra 8:17
text: Casiphia; supposed to have been not far from Ahava.

title: Ezra 8:21
text: We should never undertake a journey, or any enterprise, without first seeking the guidance and blessing of God; which is a better security against evils than any assistance that can be rendered by men.

title: Ezra 8:24
text: Those should be especially holy, who are intrusted with holy things; and should carefully preserve and faithfully appropriate what is committed to them.

title: Ezra 8:31
text: Those who secure the protection and blessing of God, may pass through the greatest dangers and prosecute the most difficult enterprises with safety and success.

title: Ezra 9:1
text: However great the judgments of God on men for their sins, or his mercy in their deliverance, they are prone to forget him, and even to repeat the sins for which they have been called to suffer.

title: Ezra 9:2
text: Marriages with the openly wicked have ever been a powerful means of public corruption, and a fruitful source of calamity to both rulers and people.

title: Ezra 9:3
text: I rent my garment; a token of great consternation and sorrow at the transgression of the people, in mingling by marriage with the idolatous nations around them.

title: Ezra 9:5
text: At the evening sacrifice; when the people assembled for evening worship.

title: Ezra 9:6
text:
Grown up unto the heavens; become exceedingly great. 
 
Ingenuous confession of sin, with hearty supplication to God for pardon, is a more sure means of relief than any application which can be made to creatures.

title: Ezra 9:8
text: A little space; from the time Zerubbabel with his company arrived at Jerusalem, to the arrival of Ezra.

title: Ezra 9:9
text: A wall in Judah; the means of defence from their enemies.

title: Ezra 9:13
text: However great the calamities which God inflicts on his people, they feel that he is righteous, and that he punishes them less than their sins deserve.

title: Ezra 9:15
text: Thou art righteous; in the punishment he had inflicted on them for their sins; and their deliverance was all of grace.

title: Ezra 10:1
text: Those who would lead others to repentance, must show that they are deeply affected with their sins, and earnestly desire their good.

title: Ezra 10:3
text: True repentance will always be accompanied with thorough reformation; and no sin is repented of, that is not heartily forsaken.

title: Ezra 10:7
text: Those who undertake public reformations need encouragement from their brethren, and the cooperation of many will effect what no one can accomplish alone.

title: Ezra 10:9
text: If men would forsake their sins and turn to the Lord, they must not only resolve to do it, but with his help must carry their resolutions into effect; actually doing what they know and acknowledge to be their duty.

title: Ezra 10:14
text: Come at appointed times; to have their cases duly investigated and decided according to the truth.

title: Ezra 10:17
text: Courage, resolution, activity, and perseverance, with dependence on God, will enable his people, for the good of his church, to accomplish objects otherwise impossible.

title: Nehemiah 1:1
text:
Chisleu; the ninth month, answering to apart of November and December. 
 
  In the twentieth year; of Artaxerxes' reign.   Nehemiah 2:1  
 
  Shushan; a city in Persia, and the winter residence of the kings.

title: Nehemiah 1:2
text:
Came; from Jerusalem. 
 
True piety is sometimes found among those who are high in civil office; and it leads them to take a deep interest in the welfare of the people and cause of God, in all parts of the world, especially in the home of their ancestors and brethren.

title: Nehemiah 1:5
text: Prayer to the God of heaven froms the best preparation for great and difficult undertakings, and is the surest means of securing complete and final success.  Compare  Nehemiah 2:4-8 Ezra 7:6 .

title: Nehemiah 1:7
text: Hearty confession of sin, and an expression of firm confidence in the promises of God, are traits of acceptable prayer, and open the way for answers of peace.

title: Nehemiah 1:9
text: The place that I have chosen; Jerusalem.

title: Nehemiah 1:10
text: These are thy servants; the Israelites who had returned to Judea.

title: Nehemiah 1:11
text:
This man; the king of Persia. 
 
As teh hearts of all men are in the hand of the Lord, application to him is the surest way of obtaining favors from them.

title: Nehemiah 2:1
text: In the month Nisan; the first month of the Jewish year; consequently about four months after Nehemiah had inquired about the Jews and engaged in special prayer in their behalf.  The months Chisleu and Nisan both fell in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes.   Nehemiah 1:1

title: Nehemiah 2:4
text:
So I prayed to the God of heaven; in silent prayer that he might be directed, and the king be led to favor him. 
 
Silent vehement prayer should be intermingled with all our employments; and the habit of asking the guidance and blessing of God in all ouir concerns, is honorable to him and highly useful to ourselves.

title: Nehemiah 2:7
text: While we first seek the blessing of God on our endeavors to do good, we should use all suitable means to secure the aid and cooperation of men; especially of those in authority, and such as have influence with others.

title: Nehemiah 2:10
text: The wicked are often grieved when the cause of God prospers and they cannot prevent it.

title: Nehemiah 2:17
text: Jerusalem lieth waste; this was more than ninety years after the decree of Cyrus giving the Jews permission to return to their own land, and about seventy years after the completion of the second temple.  The feebleness and poverty of the Jews, and the strong opposition of their enemies, had thus far prevented them from rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem.  It is from the decree of Artaxerxes, empowering Nehemiah to perform this long-neglected work, that the seventy years of Daniel,  Daniel 9:25 , are to be reckoned.  This decree is placed by some chronologists 454, by others, 449 years before Christ.  See notes on  Daniel 9:25-26 .

title: Nehemiah 2:18
text:
The hand of my God; how God had favored him. 
 
The history of God's dealings with his people affords them encouragement to engage unitedly and heartily in his work.

title: Nehemiah 2:19
text: Sanballat--Tobiah--Geshem; these men, so often mentioned in the book of Nehemiah, were the chief men among the opponents of the Jews in the provinces west of the Euphrates.

title: Nehemiah 3:1
text:
The sheep-gate; n the eastern part of the city near the temple, where sheep were sold for the sacrifices.  Compare  Nehemiah 3:32 Nehemiah 12:39   John 5:2 . 
 
In works of public reformation and such as are required for the protection and prosperity of the church, ministers of religion should take the lead, and set an example which may be safely and usefully followed.

title: Nehemiah 3:5
text:
Put not their necks; did not assist Nehemiah in the building of the wall. 
 
Men of rank often excuse themselves from the performance of those labors which the public good requires, and in which others are engaged; and thus neglect the talents with which they are intrusted, and set an example mischievous to all within their influence.

title: Nehemiah 3:7
text: The throne of the governor; the place where he administered justice.

title: Nehemiah 3:8
text: Persons of all trades and professions may assist in promoting the cause of God, and each should endeavor faithfully to perform that which belongs to him, and which his condition fits him to accomplish.

title: Nehemiah 3:12
text: When rulers and people of both sexes engage in works of beneficence, all doing what is appropriate to their condition, the work of the Lord will prosper and the highest good be effectually advance.

title: Nehemiah 3:14
text: The dung-gate; on the south-west side.

title: Nehemiah 3:15
text: The gate of the fountain; near the pool of Siloam, at the south-east part of the city.

title: Nehemiah 3:26
text: Ophel; an elevation with a tower, south of Moriah.

title: Nehemiah 3:28
text: Division of labor, and assigning to each one that which peculiarly belongs to him, and which he can most readily perform, prevents confusion, promotes dispatch, and tends to the most speedy and thorough accomplishment of every good work.

title: Nehemiah 3:32
text: The sheep-gate; the place where they began to build.  Thus they had surrounded the whole city.

title: Nehemiah 4:2
text:
Will they fortify themselves? or, "Will they leave it to them?" that is, will the Persian governors permit them to go on with the work? 
 
  Sacrifice--make an end in a day? will they, by worshipping their God through sacrifices, obtain such help from him as to finish the work in a single day?  But we may, perhaps, better render, "Shall they sacrifice? Shall they at this time make an end?" that is, shall they be allowed to go on sacrificing to their God, and building the walls, till they are completed? 
 
Opposers of religion often attempt to hinder its progress by ridicule; but if this excites the people of God to increased prayer, it will further, rather than hinder their work.

title: Nehemiah 4:6
text:
Unto the half thereof; that is, the half of its intended height. 
 
Where there is a will there is a way.  Whenever the people of God are disposed to work for him, he will open a way for them to be employed in his cause with success.

title: Nehemiah 4:9
text: Prayer to God, and a diligent use of all appropriate means, will defend his people from the rage of their enemies, and carry them forward in their appropriate work till it be accomplished.

title: Nehemiah 4:12
text: From all places whence ye shall return unto us; apparently meaning that the enemy are ready to assail them from all the roads which they employ in returning from Jerusalem to their several homes.  The passage is difficult, and has been variously interpreted.

title: Nehemiah 4:14
text: It is sometimes right to fight for the protection of our wives, children, property, and religious privileges, rather than to have them taken away by our enemies.

title: Nehemiah 4:20
text: When men who are at work for God are called to contend with enemies, they may expect that he will fight for them; and with God on their side they may both work and fight without fear, till their work is done.

title: Nehemiah 5:1
text: The rich, instead of relieving the poor, often take advantage of their necessities to obtain their property, and sometimes to bring them and their children into bondage; thus violating the duty of doing to others as they should wish others to do to them.

title: Nehemiah 5:2
text: Take up corn; that is, upon usury, having no money with which to purchase it.  Thus they brought themsleves into the power of their creditors.

title: Nehemiah 5:4
text: The king's tribute; the taxes which they were obliged to pay to the king of Persia.

title: Nehemiah 5:5
text: We bring into bondage our sons; by the sore exactions to which they were subjected in their poverty.

title: Nehemiah 5:6
text: "Oppression maketh a wise man mad," and he will without delay, as far as may be in his power, devise and execute means to bring it to a speedy and perpetual end.

title: Nehemiah 5:7
text: Usury; interest.

title: Nehemiah 5:8
text: Those who oppress their brethren will have nothing to answer when God shall call them to account.

title: Nehemiah 5:11
text:
The hundredth part of the money; this is generaly understood to mean a hundredth part per month, or twelve percent interest per annum. 
 
Those who have wrongfully taken any thing from others are bound to make full restitution, and always to do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with God.

title: Nehemiah 5:14
text:
From the twentieth year--unto the two and thirtieth year; these twelve years include the period of his first administration.  He then returned to the Persian court, and afterwards came back to Jerusalem and assumed the administration of the affairs of the Jews a second time.   Nehemiah 13:6-7  
 
  The bread of the governor; the maintenance which the people whom he governed might, according to established usage, have been required to furnish him.  He had not required the people to support him, but had supported himself.

title: Nehemiah 5:15
text: The fear of God will often lead the rich to relinquish what is justly due to them, especially when those from whom it is due are poor, and unable to pay their honest debts without distressing themselves.

title: Nehemiah 5:19
text: Those who from love to God and to men have made pecuniary sacrifices for his cause, will not in the end be losers; but will receive from God a gracious and an abundant reward.

title: Nehemiah 6:2
text:
The plain of Ono; in the tribe of Benjamin. 
 
When the efforts of wicked men to hinder the work of God are disappointed in one way, they are often tempted to try another.

title: Nehemiah 6:6
text: Gashmu; the same as Geshem.

title: Nehemiah 6:7
text: The king; the king of Persia.

title: Nehemiah 6:9
text:
Made us afraid; attempted to make us afraid. 
 
Fear of men is unbecoming in the people of God, and when threatened, they should look up to him for the courage, wisdom, adn strength which they need, go forward in duty, and let nothing hinder them from learning and doing his will, committing themselves and their cause to his wise and gracious disposal.

title: Nehemiah 6:11
text:
Being as I am; having a good conscience, and being engaged in the work of the Lord. 
 
Sometimes, if need be, it is proper in a good cause to endanger one's own life, but it is never proper to do wrong in order to save it; for he who thus saves his life shall lose it, and he who loses his life in doing right shall keep it to life eternal.

title: Nehemiah 6:15
text: Sometimes God so manifestly appears in support of his cause, that even its enemies see his hand, and are convinced that their efforts to stop it will be unavailing.

title: Nehemiah 6:16
text: Was wrought of our God; that he was with the people and blessed them in their work.

title: Nehemiah 6:18
text: Shechaniah--and--Meshullam; foreigners whose daughters Tobiah and Johanan had married.

title: Nehemiah 7:2
text:
For he; Hananiah. 
 
Power and authority should be committed to those who fear God, and will employ their talents for his cause.

title: Nehemiah 7:3
text:
Let not the gates of Jerusalem be opened; this was designed to guard against enemies. 
 
We should show our trust in God by the proper use of means, and not tempt him by the neglect of them.

title: Nehemiah 7:4
text: The city was large; the walls, having been built on the old foundations, enclosed more than was inhabited.

title: Nehemiah 7:5
text:
A register; containing the names of those who came up from Babylon to Judea. 
 
For the remainder of this chapter see the notes on  Ezra 2:1 Ezra 2:4 Ezra 2:17-19  
 
Every good thought is from above; and while we diligently improve it to the best advantage, God should be acknowledged as the giver of all good, and the glory of all be rendered to him.

title: Nehemiah 7:70
text: When God, in addition to all his other mercies, gives men a disposition to employ what they have to his glory, it is evidence of his peculiar favor, and should be acknowledged with peculiar gratitude and joy.

title: Nehemiah 8:1
text: The reading and explanation of the Scriptures is one of the most powerful means of reviving true religion; and when men desire to hear, ministers should ever be ready to communicate to them a knowledge of the word and will of God.

title: Nehemiah 8:2
text: The seventh month; Tishri, answering to a part of September and October.  On the first day of this month was kept the feast of trumpets.   Leviticus 23:23-25

title: Nehemiah 8:3
