  For vanity; here the word describes the wicked man's reward as empty; that is, disappointing his hope.  He reaps what he sowed.

title: Job 15:32
text:
It shall be accomplished; his recompense, which consists in his destruction. 
 
  Before his time; he shall be cut off by an untimely end.

title: Job 15:35
text: They conceive mischief--prepareth deceit; the same as, they trust in vanity; and vanity is their recompense,  Job 15:31 .  All their plans and works are ruinous to others, and they end in the ruin of themselves.

title: Job 16:5
text: Those who have themselves suffered great afflictions, are most disposed and best prepared to sympathize with the afflictions and assuage the grief of others.

title: Job 16:7
text: He; God.

title: Job 16:9
text: In the depths of distress, even good men, if left to themselves, will have hard thoughts, and complain not only of men but of God, and speak as if he not only were the author of their afflictions, but had become their enemy.

title: Job 16:10
text:
They; Job's pretended friends. 
 
  Smitten me; they had opposed and reproached him.

title: Job 16:11
text: Whoever may be the instruments of affliction to the people of God, they should not overlook his all-controlling hand, or feel that without his permission others could have any power over them.

title: Job 16:12
text: Was at ease; before his afflictions came.

title: Job 16:13
text: He poureth out my gall; an expression denoting the most intense anguish.

title: Job 16:15
text: Defiled my horn; the horn was an emblem of power, authority, and influence; and the meaning is, he was shorn of his power, his authority was gone.

title: Job 16:17
text: Pure; free from hypocrisy.  Of this Satan had accused him before God, and his friends had insinuated against him the same charge.

title: Job 16:18
text:
Cover not thou my blood; he speaks of himself as an innocent man appointed to die, and asks the earth to leave his blood uncovered that it may cry aloud for redress. 
 
  Let my cry have no place; that is, the cry of my blood: let it have no place where it shall be hid in silence.  According to others the meaning is, that if he had been guilty of heaven-daring crimes as his enemies charged, he did not ask that his crime should be hid; nor could he expect that God would hear his cry for deliverance from punishment.

title: Job 16:19
text: My witness is in heaven; God knows that I am sincere, though here I am charged with hypocrisy.

title: Job 16:20
text: When the soul pours out its complaints to God, and looks to him for help, though he may not at once seem to hear, in due time he will answer and grant a glorious deliverance.

title: Job 16:22
text: When a few years are come; if he is to have any deliverance in this life, it must come speedily, for death is near.

title: Job 17:1
text: We should not conclude that our work in this world is done, so long as we are continued in it; or forget that we may be useful by patient suffering, as well as by active benevolent labors.

title: Job 17:2
text: Mine eye continue; to be intently fixed on their provocations.

title: Job 17:3
text:
Lay down now; that is, a pledge, as was the custom with men when about to contend in law before the judge. 
 
  Put me in a surety with thee; be my surety that justice shall be done me. 
 
  Will strike hands with me; as was done in becoming surety for another.  These expressions are borrowed from the usages of legal tribunals in Job's day.  From his friends, whom God has deprived of understanding,  Job 17:4 , he passionately appeals to God.  The reader will notice that in this proposed trial of his cause God is both his adversary, and his patron and judge.

title: Job 17:4
text: When God leaves men to the wickedness and folly of sin, it is evidence that they are on the way to destruction, and that unless they change their course and turn their feet into the path of life, they will sink into unavailing sorrow.

title: Job 17:5
text:
Speaketh flattery to his friends; others render, betrays his friends to plunder, a figurative expression for unfaithfulness to them in the time of their calamity. 
 
  The eyes of his children shall fail; they shall suffer great calamities.

title: Job 17:8
text:
At this; the afflictions of Job; and that his friends should so far take part with Satan, as to contend that they were sent on account of his peculiar wickedness; whereas the fact was, they were sent, or permitted, to show the reality and genuineness of his religion, and that those who accused him of hypocrisy were in the wrong. 
 
  Stir up himself; be excited to greater fidelity in avoiding hypocrisy, and be guarded against considering peculiar trials as proofs of peculiar wickedness. 
 
The dealings of Providence with the righteous will render them more and more watchful, and lead them more carefully to distinguish between good and evil, and more diligently and perseveringly to pursue the one and avoid the other.

title: Job 17:9
text: Shall hold on; instead of being induced to give up his religion on account of his trials, or because others consider them as proofs of his hypocrisy, he who has true religion will persevere in it to the end; and whatever his condition here, will grow stronger and stronger in faith, patience, experience, hope, and all the graces of the Spirit.

title: Job 17:10
text: Return; return to the argument, and say something that is to the purpose and that is worth hearing.

title: Job 17:13
text:
The grave is my house; the place which I shall occupy, and where I shall remain till these heavens and earth pass away.   II Peter 3:13-14  
 
As the grave is the house appointed for all the living, and the one which they will shortly occupy, it should be the great object of each one so to live, labor, and if need be suffer, that when the body shall sleep in the grave the soul shall be with God till the morning of the resurrection; and that when the body shall be redeemed from the power of the grave, it may dwell in the new Jerusalem for ever.

title: Job 17:16
text: They shall go down; all my hopes.

title: Job 18:2
text: Ye make an end; the words are addressed to Job, and seem to mean, thou and others that think and speak like thee.  So  Job 18:3 , "in your sight."

title: Job 18:3
text:
We; Bildad and his two friends. 
 
Those who abuse or say hard things of others, are the persons who are most likely to be irritated and complain when others abuse or say hard things of them.

title: Job 18:4
text: He teareth himself; spoken of Job.

title: Job 18:5
text:
Shall be put out; his prosperity shall cease. 
 
Though evils greater than can be described are before the wicked, they may not come upon them in this life; and the idea of Bildad and his friends, that a man's character can be determined by his present outward condition, is false.  Their conclusion, therefore, concerning Job, that he must be a very wicked man, was utterly wrong.

title: Job 18:7
text: Be straitened; he shall become feeble.

title: Job 18:9
text:
Gin; a snare, or trap.   Job 18:10  
 
  The robber shall prevail against him; or, as some render, the snare shall seize upon him.

title: Job 18:12
text:
Be hunger-bitten; fail through hunger. 
 
The righteous and the wicked may both in this world be visited by trials; and a just discrimination between them may never fully appear till they enter the world of spirits.

title: Job 18:13
text:
The strength of his skin; or the members of his skin; that is, his body. 
 
  The first-born of death; death in the most terrible form.

title: Job 18:14
text: It shall bring him to the king of terrors; the calamity sent upon him from God shall bring him down to death.

title: Job 18:15
text:
It is none of his; it is no longer his secure resting-place, being taken from him and desolated by God's judgments. 
 
  Brimstone shall be scattered; possibly with allusion to the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah.   Genesis 19:24

title: Job 18:17
text:
No name in the street; there shall be none to speak of him, or keep him in remembrance after he is dead. 
 
The memory of the wicked shall rot, but the righteous shall be had in everlasting remembrance.

title: Job 18:19
text: Neither have son nor nephew; he shall leave no posterity.

title: Job 18:20
text:
They that come after him; men of a later day, who hear of his terrible overthrow. 
 
  His day; the day of his destruction. 
 
  They that went before; that lived with him; his contemporaries. 
 
  Were affrighted; at the greatness of his calamities.

title: Job 19:3
text:
Ten times; many times, very often. 
 
The afflictions with which God visits us are greatly lessened, or increased, by the conduct of our friends.  If they are kind, and ready to assist us, they help us bear our burdens; but if unkind, negligent, and reproachful, they greatly increase our sorrows.

title: Job 19:4
text: Remaineth with myself; I must bear the consequences.

title: Job 19:11
text: No permanent or safe dependence can be placed upon the most intimate and endeared earthly friends.  For the continuance of their affection and care, we are dependent upon God; and if they are forsaken of him, they may forsake us.

title: Job 19:14
text: Have forgotten me; they neglected him, as if he were not remembered.

title: Job 19:20
text: With the skin of my teeth; but just escaped from death, or utter ruin.

title: Job 19:22
text: Are not satisfied with my flesh? he compares them to beasts of prey.

title: Job 19:23
text:
My words; those that follow,  Job 19:25-27 . 
 
  Printed; that is, inscribed, as the original word signifies.

title: Job 19:24
text:
With an iron pen; a sharp-pointed instrument of steel, such as was used to cut letters into metallic plates, or, as here, into stones. 
 
  And lead; after the letters had been cut deep into the stone, it was customary to fill them with lead.  The language of  Job 19:23-24 , implies that what he is now about to utter is no common maxim, but a momentous truth, worthy to be perpetuated to the end of time.  By placing his words in the volume of inspiration, God has made them more permanent, and infinitely better known, than if they had been graven with a pen of iron and lead on the rocks of Arabia.

title: Job 19:25
text: Strong confidence in an almighty, ever-living Redeemer, and the expectation of meeting him as a friend and portion, support the soul in the deepest affliction, and cause it to rejoice in hope of the glory of God.

title: Job 19:26
text:
After my skin; after my skin shall have been destroyed by the force of my disease.   Job 7:5  
 
  Worms destroy this body; the words "worms" and "body" are not in the original, as the italic letters indicate.  The literal rendering is, "they destroy this," or, this be destroyed, meaning this body. 
 
  In my flesh; the literal rendering is, "from my flesh," or, "out of my flesh".  This is taken by some to mean, looking forth upon God from my body of flesh, that is, after its resurrection, which is the idea given by our version, "Yet in my flesh shall I see God."  Others understand the words to mean, seeing God when out of my flesh, or separated from my flesh, that is, in a disembodied state.

title: Job 19:27
text: Though my reins be consumed within me; "My reins within me are consumed with earnest desire for that day," is to be preferred.

title: Job 19:29
text:
The sword; of divine justice, for your unjust treatment of me. 
 
  Wrath; such unrighteous wrath as yours towards me. 
 
  A judgment; when God will reward all according to their works.

title: Job 20:2
text:
Therefore; because of thy impiety in justifying thyself against God. 
 
Those are often most in haste to speak, who are least able to speak to the purpose, or with any good effect.   James 1:19

title: Job 20:3
text:
The check of my reproach; the reproachful rebuke administered to me and my friends by thee. 
 
  To answer; to reply to what Job had said in opposition to his doctrine and that of his friends.

title: Job 20:5
text: The triumphing--is short; short compared with his whole existence, though it may sometimes continue through life, and life be continued till old age.

title: Job 20:10
text:
Please the poor; on whom they shall be dependent, or to whom they shall apply for help. 
 
  Restore their goods; those which they had wrongfully taken away.

title: Job 20:11
text:
The sin of his youth; he shall carry the effects of it to the grave. 
 
Sins committed in youth may produce consequences which shall be felt in old age, and which shall follow transgressors to the grave and onward to eternity.

title: Job 20:14
text: The gall of asps; his pleasures are all turned to bitterness.

title: Job 20:17
text: The brooks of honey and butter; emblems of worldly abundance.

title: Job 20:18
text:
According to his substance; his substance wrongfully gotten by oppressing the poor. 
 
Whatever may be the pleasures of sin for a season, in the end they shall be turned to bitterness and death.   Proverbs 23:32

title: Job 20:21
text: Therefore shall no man look for his goods; because they are perished, and looking for them will be in vain.  But we may better render, "Therefore shall his prosperity not abide."

title: Job 20:26
text:
All darkness shall be hid in his secret places; or, all darkness shall be laid up for his treasures.  All darkness means calamities of all kinds. 
 
  Not blown; not kindled or kept alive by man, but by God.

title: Job 20:29
text:
The portion of a wicked man; what, as Zophar and his friends contended, always came upon the wicked in this life.  In the next chapter, Job shows by facts that their doctrine was false. 
 
The evils consequent upon sin are the appointment of God; and no one can continue in it, and escape them.  They may not, in all cases, be seen or felt in this world; but they will overwhelm all continued transgressors, in the world to come.

title: Job 21:2
text: Let this be your consolations; if you will candidly listen to me, I will accept this in place of the consolations I might have so reasonably expected of you.

title: Job 21:4
text:
Is my complaint to man? merely, or principally. 
 
  And if it were so, why should not my spirit be troubled? better, omitting the italics, which are not in the original, to read, "And why should not my spirit be troubled?" that is, in view of the mighty afflictions laid upon me by God's hand. 
 
In our trials and distresses we should look not so much to men for help, as to God; and feel that whoever or whatever may be the instrument, he is the only source of relief.

title: Job 21:5
text:
Mark me; behold my affliction. 
 
  Lay your hand upon your mouth; be silent.

title: Job 21:7
text:
The wicked live, become old, yea, are mighty; this, in opposition to the doctrine of Job's friends, is often the case.   Psalms 73:3-17  
 
The wicked are sometimes prospered in this world, and receive more outward blessings than their pious neighbors.  They may live longer, and die in less distress.  The reason of this is to men not known, and it sometimes occasions them great perplexity.   Psalms 73:2-17

title: Job 21:13
text: In a moment; without long, lingering illness.

title: Job 21:14
text: Therefore;  Ecclesiastes 8:1

title: Job 21:16
text: Not in their hand; not in their own power.  It comes from God, and they are wholly dependent on him.

title: Job 21:17
text:
How oft; many understand this question as extending to the following verses  Job 21:18-20 , which may then be read interrogatively thus: How oft doth God distribute?  how oft are they as stubble? etc.; and as meaning to affirm that such a thing seldom happens, or rather, does not happen to the wicked more than to the righteous.  But see note to  Job 27:13 . 
 
However prosperous may be the condition of the wicked in this world, or however adverse that of the righteous, in the future world it will be reversed; the righteous will be comforted, and the wicked tormented.  Luke 16:24-25

title: Job 21:21
text: What pleasure hath he in his house after him; when the wicked man's days are ended, he can have no more interest in the lot of his children.  If they be cut off, that does not affect him.

title: Job 21:26
text: They shall lie down alike; God does not deal with them here according to their character, but treats them in many respects alike.

title: Job 21:28
text: Where is the house of the prince? meaning, of me, Job, who once lived as a prince.

title: Job 21:29
text:
Them that go by the way? travellers, who have had the opportunity of extended observation. 
 
  Their tokens; the indications which they give of the course of God's providence.

title: Job 21:30
text:
Is reserved to the day of destruction; now he is suffered to prosper, being reserved for destruction hereafter. 
 
The fact that men are not treated according to their character in this world, is evidence of a coming judgment, when a just discrimination will be made, and each one receive according to his works.

title: Job 21:31
text: Who shall repay him; no one in this world; but God shall reward him in the world to come.

title: Job 21:32
text: And shall remain in the tomb; literally, and shall watch over the mound, meaning the sepulchral mound.  Some render this clause impersonally: "and one shall watch over the mound;" that is, the sepulchral mound of this powerful and prosperous sinner shall be carefully guarded.  Others understand it as a poetical descrition, by which he is represented as watching, through his monumental inscription, over his grave.

title: Job 21:33
text: Every man; shall in like manner go to the grave.

title: Job 22:3
text: Any pleasure--that thou art righteous? that is, any pleasure in view of the profit he shall derive from thy righteousness.

title: Job 22:4
text: For fear of thee? lest thy sin should bring damage to him.  The meaning of Eliphaz is, that God has no private interests to be promoted by our righteousness, or damaged by our wickedness.  He is therefore infinitely above all those influences which among men produce partial and unjust conduct.

title: Job 22:8
text: He had the earth; Eliphaz here falsely charges Job with favoring the mighty and honorable, and oppressing the poor and needy.

title: Job 22:15
text: The history of past generations, both of the righteous and the wicked, is full of instruction to the children of men.

title: Job 22:16
text:
Out of time; before their time; in the prime of life, when they had not lived out the ordinary period of human life.   Psalms 55:23  
 
  With a flood; the reference seems to be to the deluge of Noah.

title: Job 22:20
text: Whereas--fire consumeth; this verse may be thus rendered: "Has not our adversary been cut off? and their excellency [that of the ungodly] the fire has consumed."  It is then the language of "the righteous" and "the innocent," mentioned in the preceding verse.

title: Job 22:21
text:
Acquaint now thyself with him; Eliphaz speaks as if Job were unacquainted with God, and at enmity with him. 
 
All men who have the Bible may become acquainted with God, and by cordial reconciliation to him may have that peace which passeth all understanding, which the world can neither give nor take away.

title: Job 22:24
text: Lay up gold; a man's piety, in the estimation of Job's friends, might be measured by the amount of his worldly prosperity, and his guilt by his calamities.

title: Job 22:26
text: Delight in the character of God and in the keeping of his commands will secure all needful good to those who exercise it, and make them great blessings both to themselves and their fellow men.

title: Job 22:29
text:
When men are cast down; when wicked men are cast down for their impiety. 
 
  There is lifting up; that is, of the righteous.

title: Job 22:30
text: The innocent; the innocent shall deliver or save the island or country for which they intercede.

title: Job 23:3
text:
Him; God. 
 
In our distress, we should look away from man and seek that help which cometh from God only.  If we cannot at once find him, we should still wait upon him in humble, believing, affectionate prayer, till he arise and have mercy upon us.

title: Job 23:6
text: Put strength in me; or, as some render, attend to me; that is, graciously listen to my words.

title: Job 23:7
text: From my judge; from God, who would not condemn me.

title: Job 23:10
text:
Come forth as gold; be justified as righteous, and accepted. 
 
Though God may not at once give relief to his distressed people, he is never unmindful of their sorrows; nor will he continue them a moment longer than his glory, their good, and the good of his kingdom require.

title: Job 23:15
text:
Troubled at his presence; because instead of allowing me to plead with him, as a man with his friend, he comes with terrible majesty, and overwhelms me with continually new calamities.  These, as Job maintains, come from his unsearchable and unalterable decree, the grounds of which no man can understand or explain.   Job 9:34-35  
 
Even the children of God sometimes exercise that fear of him which hath torment; and which nothing but the manifestation of his grace and an increase of faith and love can cast out.

title: Job 23:17
text: Because I was not cut off before the darkness; because I was not taken away by death before these calamities came upon me.

title: Job 24:1
text: See his days; of righteous retribution on the just and unjust.

title: Job 24:2
text: Though God sometimes bears long with atrocious offenders, and continues to pour blessings upon them to the end of life, yet he marks all their transgressions, and will in due time treat them according to their works.

title: Job 24:6
text: The wicked; gather the vintage of the poor.

title: Job 24:8
text: They; those whom they have robbed.

title: Job 24:9
text:
They; the freebooters or robbers. 
 
  Pluck the fatherless; seize little children to use them as slaves.

title: Job 24:11
text:
Which make oil; the oppressed and hungry, spoken of in the preceding verse, make oil and wine for their rich oppressors. 
 
  Within their walls; within the inclosure of their houses. 
 
  And suffer thirst; they compel the poor to tread their wine-presses without compensation, or suffering them to drink of the wine.

title: Job 24:12
text: Layeth not folly; doth not punish them.

title: Job 24:13
text:
Rebel against the light; the light they have; they shun the light of day, and perform their deeds in darkness.   John 3:20  
 
The wicked rebel against the light of their own minds, as well as the light of day and the light of divine truth; they seek darkness as a covering for their evil deeds, and hasten on to the time when they will sink self-condemned into the blackness of darkness for ever.

title: Job 24:16
text:
Which they had marked for themselves in the daytime; or, as some render, "They shut themselves up in the daytime," being afraid of the light. 
 
  Know not the light; carefully avoid it.

title: Job 24:18
text:
He is swift as the waters; literally, "he is swift upon the face of the waters."  The whole verse is variously interpreted.  Some understand it as a description of the wicked man's life.  He glides away with his booty, as a swift boat on the surface of a stream, or as a floating body is carried off by the current; his portion is cursed, because gotten by rapine and wickedness. 
 
  He beholdeth not the way of the vineyards; that is, hath nothing to do with the way of industry and diligence in lawful business.  Others understand the verse as describing the wicked man's end.  After he has enjoyed his day of prosperity, he passes away suddenly from his ill-gotten portion on which God's curse rests, to see his former possessions no more.  See  Job 21:13 , and note to the following verse.

title: Job 24:19
text: So doth the grave; these notoriously wicked persons die and are buried and forgotten like others; there are no judgments here in the course of providence to distinguish them from the rest of mankind.

title: Job 24:23
text: His eyes; the eyes of God.  He sees all their iniquities, if he does not now punish them.

title: Job 24:24
text:
As all; men in this life, whatever be their character, are in many respects treated alike; and you cannot from their present condition determine their character. This was the doctrine which Job contended was taught by facts. 
 
Though the difference between the righteous and the wicked may not be seen in their condition in this life, the time is at hand when all will discern between them; and the difference of condition between him that served God and him that served him not, will then be as great as that between heaven and hell.

title: Job 24:25
text: Who will make me a liar; disprove the facts, and the truth which I have maintained.

title: Job 25:2
text: In his high places; among the heavenly hosts, the "armies" mentioned in  Job 25:3 .

title: Job 25:4
text: None who have just views of the holiness of God and the sinfulness of men, will attempt to justify themselves in his sight, or expect acceptance and salvation except through his rich grace in Jesus Christ.

title: Job 26:2
text: Helped him that is without power? spoken ironically, implying that what Bildad had said was not to the point, and of no avail.

title: Job 26:5
text: Dead things--the inhabitants thereof; rather, the dead tremble; the waters underneath and their inhabitants.  The dead are, as the original word implies, the spirits of the dead in Sheol, or the world of spirits.  These, as well as the inhabitants of the deep, feel God's almighty power and tremble before it.  The world of spirits and the deep abysses of the sea are named as the places farthest removed from human vision.

title: Job 26:6
text: All things are naked and open to the all seeing eye of God; and the kingdoms of nature, providence, and grace are entirely under his control.

title: Job 26:8
text: Bindeth up the waters; the clouds convey vast masses of waters through the heavens, as if treasured up in bottles,  Job 38:37 , without being rent by their weight.

title: Job 26:9
text: Holdeth back; covereth, or rendereth invisible.

title: Job 26:13
text:
Garnished the heavens; with sun, moon, and stars. 
 
  The crooked serpent; generally understood of the northern constellation, which has been known from remote antiquity by the name of the serpent or dragon.  The book of Job contains other references to the heavenly constellations,  Job 9:9 Job 38:31-32 .

title: Job 26:14
text:
Parts of his ways; the ways of God; only a small part of which are known by men. 
 
What we know or can know of the ways of God is but little, very little, compared with what remains to be known, and which will be unfolded with greater and greater clearness and glory for ever.

title: Job 27:1
text: Parable; a representation from which moral instruction may be drawn.

title: Job 27:2
text: Taken away my judgment; refused to justify him, or appear to do so, by removing his calamities.

title: Job 27:4
text: Not speak wickedness; by condemning himself as a hypocrite, or approving the doctrine of his friends.

title: Job 27:5
text:
Will not remove mine integrity; the same as, I will hold fast my righteousness,  Job 27:6 .  Job means that, as he is conscious of having led an upright life, and of being still determined to do so, he will never acknowledge the justice of the accusations which his friends bring against him. 
 
Conscious integrity will give confidence in God, and support the soul under the sorest trials; but the want of it will deprive one of rest and peace.   I John 3:20-21

title: Job 27:7
text: As the wicked--as the unrighteous; Job by no means approved of the wicked; though he contended, in opposition to his friends, that they were sometimes prosperous in this world.

title: Job 27:8
text: Though he hath gained; the reputation of being pious, or ever so much worldly good.  But some render, "when he shall be cut off," which agrees with the following clause, "when God taketh away his soul."

title: Job 27:10
text: Delight in the Almighty will be manifested by habitual communion with him; while neglect of communion with God, is evidence of want of love to him and to his ways.

title: Job 27:11
text:
I will teach you; teach you the true doctrine concerning the wicked. 
 
  By the hand of God; or, concerning the hand of God.

title: Job 27:12
text: Seen it; seen illustrations of the truth in the facts of divine Providence.

title: Job 27:13
text: This is the portion of a wicked man; at first sight, the description of Job,  Job 27:13-22 , seems to agree altogether with that of the three friends.  Hence many interpreters have understood it as spoken in their name, thus: "Why then are ye thus altogether vain, [saying,] 'This is the portion of a wicked man,'" etc.  But Job undertakes,  Job 27:11 , to teach his friends concerning God's providence, and these verses appear to contain his doctrine.  It differs from that of his friends in this important respect, that according to them, calamity always speedily overtakes the wicked, and is sent only as a punishment for wickedness; while Job's position is, that good and bad men are both alike subject to calamities; and yet the final end of the ungodly must be destruction, while the good man, after he is tried, shall come forth as gold,  Job 23:10 .  If at times he speaks as if he were sinking down under his sorrows, without the hope of ever again seeing good, we must remember that this is the language of impatience and unbelief, to which all believers are liable in the hour of severe trial.

title: Job 27:19
text:
Shall lie down; in death. 
 
  Be gathered; by an honorable funeral.  It is of a man who has gained his riches by wickedness that he speaks. 
 
  Openeth his eyes, and he is not; perishes in the twinkling of an eye.  This seems to be a proverbial expression.

title: Job 27:22
text: God shall cast upon him, and not spare; visit him with calamities. this is often the case in this world, and always in the world to come.

title: Job 28:1
text:
The train of thought in this chapter is the following:  Man can penetrate the dark recesses of the earth, as the miner dies, and bring out to light its hidden treasures.  But wisdom, that wisdom which consists in the knowledge of God's secret counsels and the reasons of his providential dealings with men, is hid from the eyes of all living. God alone understands such wisdom.  The wisdom which he proposes to men lies not in their searching into the mysteries of his dealings with them, but in their fearing and obeying him. 
 
The goodness of God in storing the earth with all needful treasures, which may be obtained by human skill, industry, and perseverance, should be devoutly acknowledged by all, and lead them gratefully to adore and serve him.

title: Job 28:3
text: Setteth an end to darkness; the miner with his lamp enlightens the dark places underground.

title: Job 28:4
text: The flood breadeth out--gone away from men; this obscure and difficult verse has been variously interpreted.  The following rendering gives its probable meaning: "He [the miner] breaketh a channel [down] from the inhabitant [of the surface;] they [the miners] who are forgotten of the foot [above,] dwindle [from view,] they wander [far] from man."  They are said to be forgotten of the foot, because they who walk over the earth's surface above them perceive nothing of them.

title: Job 28:5
text:
Bread; grain, of which bread is made. 
 
  Fire; sparkling stones resembling fire.

title: Job 28:7
text: A path; that which is made by miners deep under ground.

title: Job 28:9
text:
The rock; he cuts it through, undermines, breaks, and removes it, in search of gold and precious stones. 
 
Should men seek for heavenly wisdom as sincerely, earnestly, and perseveringly as miners do for silver, and search for it as they do for hidden treasures, they might all possess that fear of the Lord which is true wisdom, and that knowledge of God and of his ways which is life to the soul.

title: Job 28:11
text:
From overflowing; weeping or dripping down, so as to annoy him in working his mine. 
 
  The thing that is hid; the precious treasure.

title: Job 28:12
text: Wisdom; the reasons of God's dispensations; or the wisdom which he exercises in the government of the world.

title: Job 28:13
text:
The price; value, or way to obtain it. 
 
True wisdom is to be found neither in searching the recesses of the earth and ransacking the bowels of nature, nor in vain endeavors to penetrate the mysteries of God's being and providence.  It consists rather in humbly receiving the revelation of his will which he has been pleased to make known to us, and conforming our lives to it.

title: Job 28:16
text:
Gold of Ophir; the most valuable kind. 
 
  Onyx; a precious gem.

title: Job 28:18
text: Coral--rubies; precious stones.

title: Job 28:19
text: Topaz of Ethiopia; a most precious gem.

title: Job 28:23
text: God, who understands all wisdom, will communicate to the humble and teachable, who look to him by hearty prayer in connection with the diligent study of his word, the wisdom which they need to make them blessed here, and to prepare them for everlasting blessedness in his presence hereafter.

title: Job 28:25
text:
vv 25-26. 
 
  To make the weight for the winds--weigheth the waters--a decree for the rain--a way for the lightning; the argument is, that He who made the world, and established all its laws, must know how to administer its affairs.

title: Job 28:27
text: See it; that high wisdom by which he governs the world.

title: Job 28:28
text:
That is wisdom; wisdom for man, in distinction from the divine wisdom which belongs to God alone. 
 
Heavenly wisdom if it prevails will lead a person, so far as he understands what is right, to make it his great object heartily to do it as unto the Lord; and so far as he understands what is wrong, to avoid it, and thus strive habitually to perfect holiness in the fear of God.

title: Job 29:2
text:
In months past; in the time of his prosperity. 
 
Prosperity is the gift of God.  He grants as much of it to his people, and continues it as long, as he sees best; but no one should feel that it will certainly be continued to the end of life, or forget that it may soon and suddenly be taken away.

title: Job 29:6
text: Butter, and--oil; the symbols of great prosperity and abundance.

title: Job 29:7
text: I prepared my seat; as a magistrate or judge.

title: Job 29:8
text: Stood up; as a token of respect.

title: Job 29:10
text: And their tongue cleaved to the roof of their mouth; they were overawed and held their peace.

title: Job 29:11
text: Gave witness to me; to his integrity and usefulness.

title: Job 29:14
text: It clothed me; uprightness was that by which he was known.  It was his covering and ornament.

title: Job 29:16
text: I searched out; he inquired into and examined with impartiality the cause of the stranger, as well as that of his acquaintance.

title: Job 29:17
text: Brake the jaws; overcame the oppressors, and delivered the oppressed.

title: Job 29:18
text:
Die in my nest; not meet with reverses, but live long, and go to the grave in peace. 
 
Confidence in the continuance of peace and prosperity is dangerous, and often followed by disappointment and sorrow.  If the Lord will, we shall live; and we shall be in this condition or that, in prosperity or adversity, as seemeth good in his sight.

title: Job 29:19
text: My root was spread out; he flourished like a tree by a fountain of water.

title: Job 29:20
text: My bow was renewed; the bow is an emblem of strength, and a means of defence.  The meaning is, he was kept constantly strong.

title: Job 29:22
text: They spake not again; men were satisfied with his decisions.

title: Job 29:23
text: They waited for me; to speak and settle their difficulties.

title: Job 29:24
text:
Laughed; smiled kindly. 
 
  Believed it not; for joy.   Psalms 126:1

title: Job 30:1
text: Great prosperity may speedily be followed by great afflictions.  None, therefore, should be unduly lifted up by the one, or cast down by the other.  Both are under the control of God; and in both, the great object of all should be to known him.

title: Job 30:2
text: Old age was perished; they were prematurely old and feeble on account of their poverty.

title: Job 30:3
text: Fleeing into the wilderness; they were vagabonds, shunning the society of their fellow-men.

title: Job 30:4
text:
Mallows; a plant like spinach, the leaves of which are used by the poor, both cooked and raw, as a relish for their bread. 
 
  Juniper-roots; the Hebrew word denotes a species of broom, the roots of which are very bitter, and are used for making charcoal. Compare  Psalms 120:4 . 
 
  For their meat; that is, for their living or sustenance.  The roots were probably not eaten, but either used for cooking their food, or sold to obtain food.

title: Job 30:5
text: They were driven forth; on account of their crimes.

title: Job 30:7
text: Brayed; uttered their cries.

title: Job 30:8
text: Viler than the earth; or driven out from the earth; that is, from the habitable earth into the desert.

title: Job 30:9
text: To be the song of the drunkard and the jest of the vilest of mankind has often been the lot of the virtuous; especially of those who have been active in bringing punishment upon the vicious.

title: Job 30:11
text:
He; God. 
 
  Loosed my cord; taken away my former authority, by which they were overawed and restrained. 
 
  Let loose the bridle; cast off all restraint in afflicting me.

title: Job 30:12
text:
Raise up against me; this is a figure taken from military operations.  They cast up their mounds against me as a besieging army against a fortress. 
 
  The ways of their destruction; ways, that is, embankments, that have for their object to destroy me.

title: Job 30:13
text: They have no helper; they need no one either to incite them, or help them complete their work of destruction.

title: Job 30:17
text:
My bones are pierced; expressive of the keenest and most aggressive pain. 
 
Bodily diseases are often more distressing, and the pains which they occasion are harder to bear, than any can realize, except those who endure them; and when such are neglected and reviled by those who ought to pity and relieve them, the evil is greatly increased.  Job 16:1-5 Job 19:20-21

title: Job 30:18
text: My garment changed; defiled and made stiff from my running sores. But some understand the word garment to refer to his skin, which is disfigured and made stiff by his sores.

title: Job 30:20
text:
Thee; God. 
 
  Dost not hear; dost not remove my distress. 
 
When good men in distress cry unto God, though he hears and will eventually answer, and do exceeding abundantly above all that they ask, yet he may not, and often does not, at once relieve them; but calls them to let patience have its perfect work, that thus they may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.

title: Job 30:23
text: The nearness and certainty of death should lead all to be habitually prepared for it; and though deeds of mercy for Christ's sake will not secure uninterrupted prosperity in this world, not even the giving of a cup of cold water to his disciples will fail of an abundnat reward in the life to come.

title: Job 30:24
text: Howbeit--in his destruction; the meaning of this verse is uncertain.  Some propose to render it thus: Surely there can be no prayer [prayer can avail nothing] when he [God] stretcheth out his hand: in his calamity [when God sends calamity upon a man] shall there then be a cry? [can a cry to God avail any thing?]

title: Job 30:25
text: Did not I weep; at the calamities of others, when he was in prosperity.

title: Job 30:26
text: I looked for good; in connection with his charitable deeds.

title: Job 30:27
text: Prevented; went before, came upon me.

title: Job 30:29
text:
Dragons; the original word means beasts of the desert, like jackals, that are noted for their mournful cry. 
 
  Owls; or ostriches, also well known as raising a loud cry, which much resembles the roar of the lion.

title: Job 31:1
text: Made a covenant with mine eyes; that they should look upon nothing that could excite impure desire.

title: Job 31:2
text:
What portion of God; what portion to one who transgresses his law. 
 
True religion leads those who have it to feel that the eye of God is upon them, and strive to regulate their appetites and passions, and all their thoughts and feelings, as well as their outward conduct, according to his will.

title: Job 31:4
text: He; God.

title: Job 31:5
text:
Hasted to deceit; to execute a deceitful or fraudulent purpose. 
 
Piety towards God will lead to justice, impartiality, and kindness towards men; to honesty, chastity, diligence, sobriety, and all those virtues which promote the welfare of individuals and of the community.

title: Job 31:6
text: Let me be weighed in an even balance; be righteously judged.

title: Job 31:7
text: If any blot hath cleaved to my hands; if he had committed any crime.

title: Job 31:9
text: Laid wait; to commit adultery with his neighbor's wife.

title: Job 31:11
text:
Punished by the judges; it is an offence not only against individuals but against society, and as such to be punished by the magistrates. 
 
Infidelity to the marriage covenant is a great crime, and those who are guilty of it are among the basest and most mischievous of men.

title: Job 31:13
text:
If I did despise the cause of my man-servant or--maid-servant; if he had not been strictly impartial and just towards them, as well as towards his equals. 
 
Servants and masters have the same heavenly Parent, and are brethren; and they are bound to treat each other as such, doing, each to the other, as they ought to wish that the other should do to them.

title: Job 31:14
text: Riseth up; to judgment.

title: Job 31:15
text: Make him; we had one common Creator, have one common nature, and are brethren.

title: Job 31:16
text:
Their desire; what they ought to desire and might reasonably expect. 
 
True religion is compassionate, and leads those who have it to assist the widow and the fatherless, the poor, the sick, and the destitute, and in various ways, as they have opportunity and ability, to help the needy.

title: Job 31:18
text:
Her; the widow. 
 
  From my mother's womb; from his earliest years.

title: Job 31:21
text:
Saw my help in the gate; saw those ready to aid and abet me before the magistrate in any course I might take.  The gate is mentioned as the place where courts were held. 
 
Piety in magistrates will lead to fidelity in the discharge of official duties; will secure the weak and helpless against the encroachments of the strong and overbearing; and will afford protection to the just rights of all.

title: Job 31:23
text: Could not endure; to oppress the fatherless; he was kept from it by the fear of God.

title: Job 31:24
text: The increase of riches increases the danger of setting the heart on them; and men are often secretly idolaters, without publicly bowing down to idols.  They deny to God the homage of their hearts, and live without loving or obeying him.

title: Job 31:27
text:
Secretly enticed; to worship any of the heavenly bodies. 
 
  Kissed my hand; a form of idolatrous worship.

title: Job 31:29
text: Lifted up myself; been elated, and rejoiced when evil came upon his enemy.

title: Job 31:31
text: Oh that we had of his flesh!--cannot be satisfied; or, as some render, "Where is one who was not satisfied from his flesh?"

title: Job 31:32
text: It is exceedingly difficult for a man to recount his virtues and not be elated, and it is ordinarily not best to attempt it; yet sometimes it is proper, and if done with a right spirit, may be useful; but much grace is needful to prevent being so lifted up with pride as to fall into the condemnation of the devil.

title: Job 31:33
text: Hiding mine iniquity; from men, and trying to hide it from God.

title: Job 31:34
text:
That I kept silence; when he should have spoken. 
 
  Went not out; from fear of the contempt of his neighbors.  Some have supposed the meaning of this verse to be, Let me be confounded before the multitude, let the contempt of families follow me, let me be silent and not go abroad, if I have covered my transgressions, or committed any of the crimes above-mentioned.

title: Job 31:35
text: Written a book; written out the charges against him, that he might understand and answer them; have a fair trial, and be acquitted.

title: Job 31:36
text: Take it upon my shoulder; sustain his innocence, and in such a manner that all might see it.  He would even wear the disproved accusation as an ornament.

title: Job 31:37
text: As a prince would I go; with confidence to be acquitted and approved; not as a criminal to be condemned.

title: Job 31:38
text: If my land cry against me; for having wrongfully obtained it, or not justly rewarding those who have cultivated it.

title: Job 31:39
text:
Without money; without fully paying for it, or for the labor bestowed upon it. 
 
  Caused--to lose their life; by taking away their means of support. 
 
To withhold a just reward from the laborer, or eat the fruit of his toil without compensation, is a heinous sin; and though it may be hidden from men, it will be brought to light by God, and be visited with his sore displeasure.

title: Job 31:40
text:
Thistles--and cockle; noisome weeds. 
 
  The words of Job are ended; his discussion with his friends.  He speaks afterwards only in two short prayers and confessions to God.

title: Job 32:1
text: Was righteous in his own eyes; maintained that he was no hypocrite, but a pious and benevolent man.

title: Job 32:2
text: In earnest controversies, an impartial bystander may often see much to disapprove and condemn in both parties; and when they have finished their arguments, he may to advantage, in a plain, kind, and friendly manner, attempt this, till the heat of the controversy is over, and they are prepared to receive his suggestions with attention and candor.

title: Job 32:8
text:
A spirit in man; that is, not in old men alone, but in all men. They are enlightened by God to discern between what is right and what is wrong.  Elihu uses this as an argument why he, a young man, should speak. 
 
All true wisdom is from above, and comes down from the Father of lights; and he sometimes imparts more of it to the young than to the aged, and makes those who are taught wiser than their teachers.

title: Job 32:13
text:
Lest ye should say; they had not been permitted to convince Job or settle the controversy, lest they should attribute it to their own wisdom and be lifted up with pride.  God, and not man, must convince Job of his errors. 
 
Sometimes the errors of men are such that none but God can convince them, or lead them to embrace the truth; and in our attempts to do it we should look up to him without whose influence all human efforts will fail.

title: Job 32:14
text: With your speeches; in the manner which they attempted.

title: Job 32:15
text: They; Job's three friends.

title: Job 32:19
text:
Is as wine which hath no vent; he was so full of the subject that he could not refrain from speaking. 
 
  New bottles; leathern bottles filled with new wine in a state of fermentation.  Compare  Matthew 9:17 .

title: Job 32:21
text:
Accept any man's person; use any partiality. 
 
Impartiality in the treatment of disputants is essential to mutual conviction; and a deep sense of accountability to God, before whom all must shortly appear, should ever pervade our minds when we undertake to point out the errors and correct the mistakes of our fellow men.

title: Job 32:22
text: I know not; it was not his character, or habit.

title: Job 33:3
text: Clearly; purely, with sincerity, as the original word implies.

title: Job 33:4
text: Hath made--given me life; hath made me a man endowed with reason. See note to  Job 32:8 .

title: Job 33:5
text: If we cannot justify ourselves before frail sinful men like ourselves, much less can we before the omniscient, heart-searching, rein-trying God; and we should not attempt it, but confess and forsake our sins and turn heartily to him that we may find mercy.

title: Job 33:6
text: In God's stead; he would speak for God, and attempt to justify him in his dealings with Job.

title: Job 33:7
text: My terror--my hand; he refers to Job's words,  Job 9:32-35 Job 13:20-22 .

title: Job 33:9
text: I am innocent; Job meant, that he was innocent of the crimes with which his friends charged him; but Elihu interpreted what he had said, to mean that he was free from all sin.

title: Job 33:10
text:
He; God. 
 
Great care should be taken, that in our distresses we do not seem to reflect upon the righteousness, wisdom, or goodness of God; or attribute to him, even in thought or feeling, any thing derogatory to his holy and perfect character.

title: Job 33:11
text: He putteth my feet in the stocks; shuts me up to great calamities.

title: Job 33:12
text: Thou art not just; in thus speaking of God as if he were unjust and cruel.

title: Job 33:14
text: For God speaketh; though God will not allow himself to be arraigned for his dealings at any human tribunal, yet he graciously reveals his will to the humble and teachable, by night visions,  Job 33:15-18 ; and by fatherly chastisement,  Job 33:19-22 .  They who will attend to these admonitions shall be restored to God's favor and their former prosperity,  Job 33:23-30 .  Such is the course of Elihu's argument.

title: Job 33:16
text: Sealeth their instruction; impresses instruction upon their minds and hearts, as to the consequences of virtue and vice.

title: Job 33:17
text:
His purpose; his purpose of committing iniquity. 
 
  Hide pride from man; make him humble. 
 
God addresses men in a great variety of ways, sometimes in mercies and sometimes in trials; but his object is to humble them for their sins, lead them to repentance, and thus prepare them for his everlasting love.

title: Job 33:18
text: He keepeth back; or, that he may keep back; for this verse expresses the end for which God instructs men in visions of the night.

title: Job 33:19
text: He is chastened; Elihu here names the second way in which God impresses instruction upon man, namely, by visiting him with sickness, and in various ways afflicting him, not for his destruction, but for his profit.

title: Job 33:22
text: To the destroyers; the ministers of death, whether in the form of diseases or of destroying angels.

title: Job 33:23
text:
A messenger--an interpreter; a messenger sent to the man in his affliction to interpret to him its meaning, and show him his duty in regard to it.  Some understand here a heavenly messenger, that is, an angel; others, an earthly messenger.  The last interpretation is favored by the words, "one among a thousand," which imply that among men such a wise expounder of God's will is rarely to be found. 
 
  To show unto man his uprightness; to show him the uprightness or righteousness of God in his afflictions, that they are designed to lead him to repentance, and thus prepare him for a renewal and increase of blessings. 
 
The great and effectual teacher as to the righteousness of God in all his dispensations, and the sinfulness of men, is the Holy Spirit; and if a man receives his teaching and obeys it, God will be gracious to him, overrule his trials for his good, and through the ransom which He has provided, save him with an everlasting salvation.

title: Job 33:24
text: Then he is gracious; then, when he repents and acknowledges God's uprightness, God will be gracious to  the penitent, and deliver him from death through the ransom or atonement he has provided.

title: Job 33:25
text: His flesh shall be fresher than a child's; he shall be restored to perfect health, and put on again the freshness and vigor of youth.

title: Job 33:26
text: The humble and penitent soul has access to God by prayer and supplication; and he receives gracious answers of peace, and is ripening, under all the dispensations of Providence, for complete deliverance from sin, and an entrance into that rest which remaineth for the people of God.

title: Job 33:27
text:
vv 27-28. 
 
  He looketh upon men--shall see the light; of this passage there are two readings, one given by our translators in the text, the other thus: "He [the restored penitent] shall look upon men, and say, I have sinned, and perverted right, and it profited me not.  He hath delivered my soul from going into the pit, and my life sees the light." 
 
  If any say, I have sinned; repent of and forsake his sins. 
 
  See the light; be visited with prosperity.

title: Job 33:30
text: To bring back his soul from the pit; the general doctrine of Elihu was, that the Lord sends afflictions to bring men to repentance, and thus to save them from death and fit them for the blessings of his grace.

title: Job 34:2
text: It is wise to address respectfully, and attempt to conciliate those whom we would convince of their errors and led to embrace the truth.

title: Job 34:4
text: Judgment; that which is right.

title: Job 34:5
text: Taken away my judgment; afflicts me without cause.

title: Job 34:7
text: Men in controversy are apt to put the worst construction upon the language of their opponents, and to charge them with what they do not admit, and with consequences which they deny.

title: Job 34:8
text: Walketh with wicked men; pursues the same course of argument as they do in reasoning about the government of God.

title: Job 34:13
text:
Who hath given him a charge; He is independent and reigns of right over all.  Here, again, the argument is, that He who made the world has a right to govern it according to the counsel of his own will. 
 
God is independent, and will govern the world according to his pleasure.  All men are dependent on him for life and its enjoyments, and when he sees fit they instantly die.

title: Job 34:14
text:
If he set his heart upon man; if God direct his thoughts towards man in anger, for his destruction. 
 
  Gather unto himself his spirit; recall the breath of life which he has given him.   Genesis 2:7   The argument is, that man is absolutely dependent on God for life and breath and all things, and should not presume to call in question the rectitude of his ways.

title: Job 34:16
text: Thou; Job.

title: Job 34:17
text:
Shall even he that hateth right govern? that God is the absolute and independent governor of the world, all must admit.  Can it then be reasonable to charge him with hatred of right?  The argument is the same as that used by Abraham: "Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?"  Genesis 18:25  
 
  Him that is most just? or, "the just mighty One."

title: Job 34:20
text:
Shall they die; rich men and princes, if God so wills it. 
 
The great and the mighty are equally dependent on God with the small and the feeble, and all their interests are equally at his disposal.

title: Job 34:27
text: Want of consideration is a fruitful reason why men often turn from the ways of the Lord, and by oppression and cruelty draw down his judgments upon themselves and their fellow men.

title: Job 34:33
text:
Should it be according to thy mind? God will not change his plans to meet the views of men. 
 
  He will recompense; treat every man in the end according to his character. 
 
  Whether thou refuse, or--choose; to submit to, and obey him.

title: Job 34:36
text: His answers for wicked men; because he had seemed to justify them.

title: Job 34:37
text: Multiplieth his words against God; in seeming to speak of him as if he were unjust.

title: Job 35:3
text:
Thou saidst; Job had said that from which Elihu drew the conclusion which he here states. 
 
Men in great trials should be careful not only that they do not say what is not true, but also that they do not so express themselves as shall be misunderstood and do mischief to their fellow men.

title: Job 35:6
text:
What doest thou against him? for the meaning of this and the two following verses, see note to  Job 22:3-4 . 
 
The conduct of men may injure or benefit themselves, but cannot add to or diminish the essential glory of God.

title: Job 35:9
text: They; the oppressors.

title: Job 35:10
text:
But none saith; none of those who cry out by reason of oppressions. They do not look to God for deliverance from their troubles, and therefore these are not removed.  It is a prominent thought with Elihu that trouble is sent upon men as a discipline to bring them to repentance, and that when they repent and call upon God, he saves them. 
 
  Giveth songs in the night; giveth deliverance, and thus songs of praise in the night of sorrow. 
 
Many continue in affliction because they do not in a proper manner, and with a right spirit, cry unto God for relief.

title: Job 35:12
text:
They cry; the oppressed cry out in their calamity, but not in a proper manner, and therefore they are not heard. 
 
  Because of the pride of evil men; these words are probably to be connected with the first clause, "There they cry."  Compare  Job 35:9 .

title: Job 35:13
text: Not hear vanity; not heed vain, empty, formal, hypocritical prayers.

title: Job 35:14
text:
Judgment is before him; he will do only what is right. 
 
Though God is invisible, yet he is perfectly acquainted with the wants of all the children of men, and gives them the most abundant reason at all times to trust in him.

title: Job 35:15
text:
Because it is not so; Elihu says, that because Job did not so trust in God, his afflictions were continued. 
 
  He knoweth it not; he says, Job did not know the cause of his calamities, nor did he take the right way to remove them.

title: Job 36:3
text: From afar; from without and beyond the range of common thought.

title: Job 36:4
text: Perfect in knowledge; this Elihu applies to himself.  He uses the word perfect in the sense of upright or sincere, meaning that his is one who will utter what he knows in sincerity, avoiding all sophistry and false reasoning.

title: Job 36:9
text:
He showeth them their work; their evil work: this Elihu states as the object of their affliction. 
 
  Exceeded; that their transgressions have been great. 
 
In speaking for God, men should be careful to declare only his truth, and in such a manner as shall honor him and be useful to their fellow men.

title: Job 36:10
text: The design of God in afflictions, is to lead men to forsake their sins and obey him.  If they do this, he will in due time remove their trials and bestow upon them the riches of his mercy; if they do not, they will treasure up wrath and perish without hope.

title: Job 36:12
text: Without knowledge; that is, from want of knowledge.  Because they did not understand and make a right use of God's discipline.

title: Job 36:13
text: They cry not; they do not call upon God in affliction.

title: Job 36:14
text: Their life is among the unclean; their life perishes by a premature and base death, like that of the unclean.  The word rendered "unclean" means Sodomites.

title: Job 36:15
text:
Openeth their ears; to the instructions which his dealings are suited to impart. 
 
  In oppression; in a time of affliction and by means of it.

title: Job 36:17
text: Fulfilled the judgment of the wicked; had acted as they do, and been afflicted accordingly.  Elihu does not mean to charge Job with having been a hypocrite addicted to gross sins, as his three friends had done, but rather with behaving like the wicked under his afflictions, and therefore failing to receive deliverance.

title: Job 36:18
text: When men have once passed the boundaries of probation, they are unalterably fixed in their final unchanging state.

title: Job 36:20
text:
The night; the night of death.   Job 3:20-23  
 
  When people are cut off in their place; when the successive generations of men vanish each from their place.

title: Job 36:21
text:
Regard not iniquity; indulge not thyself in it.  It is the iniquity of impatience and rebellion against God's dealings with him, that Elihu charges upon Job. 
 
  This; iniquity. 
 
  Rather than affliction; thou preferrest to spend thy time in murmuring against God, rather than in patient submission to his rod.

title: Job 36:23
text: Who hath enjoined him; pointed out to God what he should do.

title: Job 36:24
text: Which men behold; or, which men celebrate; namely, all righteous men.

title: Job 36:26
text: The character and ways of God are in many respects unsearchable, past finding out.  It is our wisdom and duty to bow submissively before him, feeling that though clouds and darkness are round about him, justice and judgment, righteousness and truth are the habitation of his throne.

title: Job 36:27
text:
Maketh small; or draweth up, that is, in vapor, that he may pour them down again in rain. 
 
  Vapor; this word here signifies the mass of clouds out of which the rain falls.

title: Job 36:29
text:
The spreadings of the clouds; the way in which God spreads forth his clouds in the firmament above. 
 
  The noise of his tabernacle; the thunder that comes from his tabernacle in the clouds.

title: Job 36:30
text:
His light; lightning. 
 
  Upon it; the cloud. 
 
  The bottom of the sea; he covereth with water.

title: Job 36:31
text: By them; clouds, rain, thunder, and lightning.

title: Job 36:32
text: With clouds--cometh betwixt; this verse may be thus rendered: He covereth his hands with light, [lightning;] and gives it a charge upon its mark, [the object it shall strike;] or, as some prefer, gives it a charge against the opposer; that is, the man that is rebellious against God.

title: Job 36:33
text:
The noise thereof showeth concerning it; or, his noise [thunder] shows concerning him; that is, announces his approach in a tempest. 
 
  The cattle also; the cattle also, by their actions, give signs. 
 
  The vapor; the mass of rising clouds.

title: Job 37:1
text: At this; the tempest mentioned in the preceding and following verses.

title: Job 37:2
text: The noise of his voice; the thunder.

title: Job 37:4
text:
After it; after the lightning. 
 
  He will not stay them; he will not hold back his lightnings; or, as others prefer, his treasures of rain, hail, and wind.

title: Job 37:5
text: All the operations of nature are under the control of God.  He orders the seasons and all things with regard to them as seemeth good in his sight; as is best suited to promote his glory and the good of those who trust in him.

title: Job 37:7
text: He sealeth up the hand; by the approach of the storm he stops the laborer in his work.

title: Job 37:9
text: The north; the original word seems to mean scattering winds; that is, winds coming from the north, scattering the clouds, and bringing cold weather.

title: Job 37:10
text: The breadth of the waters is straitened; by being frozen up.

title: Job 37:11
text: He wearieth the thick cloud; exhausts it, by causing it to pour out its contents of rain upon the earth.  Some prefer to render, Also he ladeth his thick cloud with moisture.

title: Job 37:13
text:
It; the rain, or storm. 
 
Storms are sometimes sent, and property to a great amount swept away or destroyed, for the correction of those who have sought it as their chief good; to show them the uncertainty of earthly things, and lead them to seek durable riches and righteousness, a treasure in heaven which will never be taken away.

title: Job 37:15
text: Disposed them; the clouds, rain, thunder, etc.

title: Job 37:16
text:
The balancings of the clouds; see note to  Job 36:33 . 
 
As me by doing their duty may enjoy all the benefits of the seasons without being able to explain the reasons of them, so the believer in revelation may have all its benefits without being able to explain its mysteries, or understand the reasons of divine dispensations.

title: Job 37:17
text: Quieteth the earth by the south wind; by the sultry sirocco, which overpowers every thing by its heat, and produces universal languor.

title: Job 37:19
text: Him; God, when we think to arraign him for his doings.

title: Job 37:20
text:
Swallowed up; overwhelmed with the greatness, majesty, and glory of God. 
 
Suitable views of God will always inspire reverence and awe, humility and holy fear, as well as affection, confidence, and joy.

title: Job 37:21
text: And now--cleanseth them; the meaning, according to our version, is that the bright light of the sun is hid from men's view by the clouds, till the wind cleanses them away.  Some propose to render thus: "And now men cannot look upon the bright light which is in the clouds, when the wind passeth and cleanseth them;" that is, it is too dazzling to behold.

title: Job 37:23
text: He will not afflict; improperly, or without good reasons.

title: Job 37:24
text:
Wise of heart; He receives no assistance from the most intelligent; but forms and preserves his own plans, without asking counsel or receiving aid from any of his creatures. 
 
From  Job 36:27-37:24 , Elihu is occupied with the description of God's majesty and power as manifested in "fire and hail, snow and vapor; stormy wind, fulfilling his word."  Psalms 148:8   Many suppose that the tempest out of which God soon spoke,  Job 38:1 , was seen approaching, and that this gave to Elihu's words their peculiar turn.

title: Job 38:2
text: When men undertake to sit in judgment on the works and ways of God, or to explain the reasons of all his dealings, they generally darken their own minds and the minds of others by words without knowledge.

title: Job 38:3
text: Gird up now thy loins; summon up all thy courage, resolution, and wisdom.

title: Job 38:5
text: Stretched the line upon it? as a carpenter in building a house.

title: Job 38:6
text: The works and ways of God in creating and governing the world, though ordered in infinite wisdom and goodness, are far above and beyond the most enlarged and exalted conceptions of men, and call for adoring gratitude, admiration, and praise.

title: Job 38:7
text: Sons of God; the angelic hosts.

title: Job 38:8
text: Shut up the sea; set bounds to it, that it cannot pass over.

title: Job 38:12
text: The regularity of day and night, and the benefits they impart to the human family, are constant evidences of the goodness of God; and lay men under ever new obligations to acknowledge, trust in, and obey him.

title: Job 38:13
text:
Take hold of the ends of the earth; shine upon every part of it. 
 
  Might be shaken out of it; driven away by the light from their deeds of darkness.

title: Job 38:14
text:
It is turned; the whole earth assumes a fresh, new form; like the wax under the seal. 
 
  And they stand as a garment; all things on the earth's surface stand forth like a new and beauteous robe.

title: Job 38:15
text:
From the wicked their light is withholden; because the darkness of night is their light; that is, it furnishes their opportunity to do evil deeds: the coming of the morning is to them the shadow of death.  Job 24:17  
 
  The high arm shall be broken; their power to do mischief is prevented by the approaching light of day.

title: Job 38:16
text: The greatness, wisdom, power, and goodness of God, are seen in the sea, in the inexhaustible treasures it contains, and in the facilities it affords for the conversation, health, prosperity, and happiness of man.

title: Job 38:17
text: The gates of death; the passage to the invisible world, the world of spirits.

title: Job 38:19
text: Light--and--darkness; could Job explain their origin, nature, and effects?--things which existed and operated long before he was born.

title: Job 38:22
text: The snow and the hail, the storm and the tempest, the lightning, thunder, rain, dew, and sunshine--all governed by exact and immutable laws, which no man can cntrol or evade--proclaim the omnipotence, and show forth the presence of an all-surrounding God.

title: Job 38:23
text: Against the time of trouble--battle and war?; against the day when I come forth as a warrior to fight against my enemies with great hail-stones.  Exodus 9:22-25 Joshua 10:11 Isaiah 30:30 , etc.

title: Job 38:24
text: Which scattereth the east wind; or, By what way is the east wind scattered?

title: Job 38:25
text: Divided a watercourse for the overflowing of waters; distributed the overflowing waters of the clouds into their proper channels.  This is a figurative description of the distributions of rain, borrowed from the manner in which the eastern husbandman irrigates his land by distributing the water through it in proper channels.

title: Job 38:30
text: Are hid; beneath their icy covering.

title: Job 38:31
text:
The sweet influences of Pleiades; the sweet infuences of Spring which accompany the rising of Pleiades.  Pleiades is the seven stars which rise in the spring of the year.  Some render this clause, "Canst thou bind the hands of Pleiades?"  Loosing and binding the constellations means making their movements and influences subject to our will. 
 
  Orion; a constellation of stars on the equinoctial. 
 
The nature, number, courses, and influences of the stars, though perfectly known to Him who calleth them all by their names and employs them to accomplish his purposes, can be but very imperfectly comprehended by the most intelligent and wisest of the children of men.

title: Job 38:32
text:
Mazzaroth; the twelve signs of the zodiac. 
 
  Arcturus with his sons; a constellation of stars now called the Great Bear, and revolving around the North star.

title: Job 38:33
text:
The ordinances of heaven? the laws which govern the heavenly bodies. 
 
  The dominion; the influence they have upon the earth.

title: Job 38:36
text: All the knowledge and wisdom which men possess, above the beasts of the field, or the fowls of the air, come from God.  Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might; let not the rich man glory in his riches; but let him that glorieth, glory in the Lord.

title: Job 38:37
text: Stay the bottles of heaven; or, cause to lie down as a bottle, in emptying it; that is, pour forth rain from the clouds.

title: Job 38:38
text: When the dust--cleave fast together; as in a time of drought. Another rendering: "When the dust is melted into mire, and the clods cleave fast together;" that is, are reduced by rain to a mass of cohering clay.  This is then to be regarded as the effect of emptying the bottles of heaven.

title: Job 39:1
text: Wild goats of the rock--hinds; those that live in the mountains, far away from the abodes of men.

title: Job 39:3
text:
They bring forth their young; dependent only on the care of God. 
 
Creatures that are dependent only on the providence of God, are by him provided for, as really as those whose wants are supplied by human instrumentality; while in both he equally shows his wisdom, power, and love.

title: Job 39:4
text: With corn; or, in the open field; that is, far away from all human care.

title: Job 39:7
text: Neither regardeth; literally, heareth not.  He is far removed from the driver.

title: Job 39:9
text:
Unicorn; according to some, the eastern buffalo; according to others, the rhinoceros, an immensely strong animal with one horn a little above its nose, or some other wild animal of great strength. See note to  Numbers 23:22 . 
 
It is not enough for usefulness to have great strength, or superior natural qualities; there must also be the ability and the disposition rightly to use them.

title: Job 39:13
text: Gavest thou--the ostrich? the exact rendering of this verse is difficult.  Some propose to translate as follows: "The wing of the ostriches exulteth: are its plumage and feathers those of the stork?" meaning, does the ostrich have the tender dispositon of a stork towards its young?

title: Job 39:16
text:
She is hardened against her young; treats her young as if she had no natural affection. 
 
To all classes of creatures God gives just the kind and degree of wisdom which they need to accomplish the ends for which he made them; what would only be a useless annoyance to them, he has wisely and mercifully withheld.

title: Job 39:18
text: She lifteth up herself; to escape her pursuers, running by the help of her wings with great swiftness.

title: Job 39:19
text: The courage, agility, and strength of the horse, his affection and docility, his readiness to labor, his patience even under hardship and abuse, and his subserviency to the various wants of men, are all evidence of the goodness of God, in which his hand should be gratefully recognized.

title: Job 39:20
text: Canst thou make him afraid? or, cause him to leap.  Is it from thee that he receives the agility of a locust in leaping?

title: Job 39:24
text: Neither believeth he; that is, for joy.  But many prefer to render, "neither will he stand still when there is the sound of the trumpet."

title: Job 39:30
text: The most rapacious and savage of the feathered tribes, who teach their young to revel in blood, do not take the life of their own species; this is the sin of the abused understandings and depraved hearts and bloody hands of men.

title: Job 40:2
text: Complaining of the ways of God is finding fault with him, as if we were wiser than he, and could instruct him as to the best way of governing the world; and all must one day answer to him for all the hard speeches which they have uttered against him.

title: Job 40:4
text:
Lay my hand upon my mouth; be silent. 
 
Right views of God will silence objections to his providence,a nd lead us humbly to submit to all his dispensations; saying, It is the Lord; let him do as seemeth good in his sight.

title: Job 40:8
text: Disannul; make void, or reverse.

title: Job 40:9
text: The character, works, and ways of God, show that he alone is fitted to govern the world; and that all creatures are, and for ever must be, at his disposal.

title: Job 40:13
text: Bind their faces in secret; thrust them bound into dungeons, where they shall no more be seen nor heard of.

title: Job 40:15
text:
Behemoth; supposed by some to be the elephant; by others, the hippopotamus. 
 
The greatest and most formidable of creatures on the land or in the water, are dependent on God; and he can control them with as much ease as he does the smallest and weakest, and dispose of them at his pleasure.

title: Job 40:19
text: The chief; one of the most wonderful beasts that God has made.

title: Job 40:24
text: He taketh it with his eyes; or, Can one take him in his sight, or pierce his nose with a hook or ring?

title: Job 41:1
text:
Levithan; supposed by some to be the whale, by others, the crocodile, with which latter animal the description best agrees. 
 
The principal superiority of man above many of the beasts consists not in his sizer or strength of body, but in the faculties and powers of his mind; and the cultivation and right use of these should be his chief concern.   Genesis 1:26-29 Acts 17:26-29

title: Job 41:6
text: The companions; the companies of fishermen.

title: Job 41:7
text: Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons?--with fish-spears? the bony armor or scales of the crocodile's skin make it impenetrable to spears, or even musket-balls, except in particular parts.

title: Job 41:8
text: Remember the battle; think of the conflict that would ensue should you attempt to take him, and refrain from it.

title: Job 41:9
text: The hope of him; the hope of taking him; or, the hope of him who would take him.

title: Job 41:11
text:
Prevented me; gone before me in the bestowment of favors, and laid me under obligation to repay them. 
 
None can devote any thing to God which He has not first given to them, or lay him under obligations to bestow any good upon them; but all must depend on his goodness, mercy, and grace.

title: Job 41:13
text:
Discover the face of his garment? strip off his skin. 
 
  Come to him with his double bridle? or, Come within his double bridle, a figurative expresson for his two rows of teeth.

title: Job 41:14
text: The doors of his face? his jaws.

title: Job 41:18
text:
Neesings; sneezing, or violent breathing, as when he comes to the surface after being some time under the water. 
 
  A light doth shine; the reference here, and in the following verses, seems to be to the white spray glittering in the sun, which he throws with violence from his mouth and nostrils.

title: Job 41:22
text: Sorrow is turned into joy; this some have translated, terror danceth before him.

title: Job 41:25
text:
By reason of breakings they purify themselves; or, they lose themselves with terror. 
 
The fear of man which is impressed upon most of the animal tribes, and which adds so much to his safety and comfort, is a striking evidence of the goodness of God; and lays men under obligations to employ the influence he has given for the good of all.

title: Job 41:26
text:
Cannot hold; see note to  Job 41:7 . 
 
  Habergeon; coat of mail.

title: Job 41:30
text: Sharp stones; rather, sharp pieces of potsherd.  These, and the "sharp pointed things," refer to the sharp protuberances on his belly.

title: Job 41:32
text: He maketh a path to shine after him; makes the deep white with foam.

title: Job 41:34
text: The children of pride; the most strong and courageous of the animal creation.

title: Job 42:3
text: Men know very little about the character and ways of God, except as he reveals them; and when they attempt to go beyond his revelation, they darken counsel by words without knowledge.

title: Job 42:4
text: Hear, I beseech thee; Job humbly asks God to listen to his inquiries, and teach him the truth concerning Himself and his ways.

title: Job 42:5
text:
I have heard of thee; he had had dark and indistinct views of God. 
 
  Now mine eye seeth thee; his views of God were more clear and distinct. 
 
Closer views of the character and will of God, and right feelings towards him, will lead men to abhor their sins, and heartily to turn from them to him, whose favor is life, and whose loving-kindness is better than life.

title: Job 42:6
text: Wherefore I abhor myself; on account of my sins.

title: Job 42:7
text:
As my servant Job hath; Job's general doctrine concerning God and his providence, though maintained with much impatience and infirmity of spirit, was yet correct; and it was more honorable to God than the doctrine of his friends. 
 
The Lord will in due time vindicate his servants from the aspersions which men have wrongfully cast upon them, and bring forth their righteousness as the light, and their integrity as the noonday.

title: Job 42:10
text:
Turned the captivity of Job; removed his calamities, and restored his prosperity. 
 
The end of a good man is more blessed than his beginning; and the darkness and distress of the night will be followed by the light, the joy, and the glory of a cloudless and eternal day.

title: Job 42:11
text:
Did eat bread with him; a token of restored kindness and friendship. 
 
Many who neglect a man, or stand aloof from him in adversity, will return to him and be very friendly and kind in prosperity.

title: Job 42:16
text: Let a man be patient under trials: if reviled, not revile again; hold fast his integrity, commit himself to Him that judgeth righteously, and justify God in all his ways, and his end will be peace and his eternity blessed.

title: Psalms 1:1
text:
The theme of this psalm is the permanent prosperity and happiness of the righteous, and the certain destruction of the wicked.  It stands as an appropriate introduction to the whole book.  The righteous man is described here, as often elsewhere, in absolute terms; that is, without any notice of his infirmities and failures in duty; and the promise is made to him in the same absolute way.
