The meaning of such a promise, when applied to a good man in covenant with God, yet not free from sin, is that God will withhold from him no good thing,  Psalms 84:11 ; that he will chasten him, as a father his child, for his instruction and profit, that he may purify him from sin, and thus prepare him for greater prosperity and happiness,  Psalms 94:12-13 Proverbs 3:11 I Corinthians 11:32   Hebrews 12:6-12 ; and that he will support him under his trials,  Psalms 34:17-19 , and everlasting blessedness in his presence,  Psalms 16:11 Psalms 17:15 Psalms 73:24-26 Revelation of John 14:13 .  Upon this broad principle are to be interpreted all those psalms which describe the prosperity and blessedness of the righteous in unqualified terms; as, for example,  Psalms 112:1-10 Psalms 115:1-18 Psalms 121:1-8 Psalms 125:1-5 Psalms 128:1-6 . 
 
  Walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly; does not embrace their principles, adopt their maxims, or encourage their practices. 
 
All needless counseling with the wicked should be avoided, as it tends to make us more like them.

title: Psalms 1:2
text:
In the law of the Lord; in learning and doing his will. 
 
Supreme devotion to God is the way not only of duty, but of safety, prosperity, and happiness.

title: Psalms 1:3
text:
Like a tree planted by the rivers; his excellence, usefulness, and blessedness shall habitually increase, and he shall go from one degree of holiness to another for ever. 
 
  Shall prosper; the Lord shall bless him in all his ways.

title: Psalms 1:4
text:
The ungodly; those who are not governed by the will of God. 
 
  Like the chaff; worthless; and all their blessings of short continuance. 
 
Whatever may be the condition here of those who regard not God, they are in his sight worthless; and their blessings being abused, will soon all be taken away.

title: Psalms 1:5
text: Not stand in the judgment; not be approved, but condemned and separated for ever from the righteous.  The judgment here spoken of includes all the ways in which God purifies his people from the wicked here and hereafter.  What we see of God's judgment in this world, however, is only a foreshadowing of that great day when the separation between the righteous and the wicked will be perfect and eternal.

title: Psalms 1:6
text:
Knoweth; sees and approves the course of the righteous, and will for ever bless them. 
 
  Shall perish; leads to destruction. 
 
The righteous and the wicked here lived together, and are often connected in bonds of social interaction and affection; but the Lord is perfectly acquainted with their different ways, and in the future world will make an everlasting separation between them.

title: Psalms 2:1
text:
David was the divinely constituted head of Israel, the visible church of God, and was an eminent type of Christ.  The assaults made upon him by the surrounding nations were assults upon God's church, and his victories over them were victories of the Messiah over all his enemies. The promises contained in this and similar psalms were fulfilled in David's time and person only in a lower and imperfect sense.  Their high and absolute fulfilment is in Christ, the everlasting King of David's line, who "must reign till he hath put all enemies under his feet."   I Corinthians 15:25   The dramatic character of this psalm is remarkable.  The following is the order of speakers:   Psalms 2:1-2 , the psalmist;  Psalms 2:3 , the ungodly kings and rulers;  Psalms 2:4-5 , the psalmist;  Psalms 2:6 , Jehovah;  Psalms 2:7-9 , the Messiah;  Psalms 2:10-12 , the psalmist. 
 
  The heathen--and the people; all who are opposed to being governed by God and his Son Jesus Christ. 
 
It is natural for rulers and people, when left by God to themselves, to be opposed to his reigning in and over them, and to refuse to submit to him as their rightful Lord and King; but their opposition will injure themselves only.

title: Psalms 2:3
text: Break their bands asunder; refuse to be governed by God's revealed will.

title: Psalms 2:4
text: Shall laugh--have them in derision; shall look down from heaven upon them in serene majesty, unmoved by their impotent malice.

title: Psalms 2:6
text: My king; the Messiah, and David as his type.

title: Psalms 2:7
text:
The decree; constituting Christ Mediator and universal King. 
 
  Begotten thee; manifested thee as the Messiah, the Son of God. 
 
The decree which constituted Christ Mediator and gave him the ownership of all the earth, as a reward for his sufferings unto death, secures the salvation of all who submit to and trust in him, and renders certain the destruction of all who continue to oppose and rebel against him.

title: Psalms 2:9
text: Them; his opposers.

title: Psalms 2:12
text:
Kiss the Son; submit to, trust in, and obey him.  The kiss is here, in accordance with oriental usage, a sign of submission and allegiance. 
 
  Him; the Son of God, the Messiah.

title: Psalms 3:1
text: The enemies of the righteous may be numerous, malignant, and powerful, but the Lord will take care of his people, and in due time deliver them from all their troubles.

title: Psalms 3:3
text:
Shield; protection. 
 
  My glory; here, probably, the maintainer of my glory; that is, of my kingly dignity.

title: Psalms 3:4
text:
His holy hill; alluding to Zion, where God dwelt between the cherubim, and whence he is represented as sending succor to his servants.   Psalms 20:2 Psalms 80:1  
 
The grand means of deliverance and safety to the righteous is a prayer, and having committed themselves and their cause in humble believing supplication to God, they may rest in quietness, knowing that he and he only can make them dwell in peace.

title: Psalms 3:5
text: Slept; in peace and safety.

title: Psalms 3:6
text: I will not be afraid; because he had God for his protector.

title: Psalms 3:8
text: The people of God know that the Author of their salvation is the Lord; they acknowledge him as the source of all their blessings, and to him give the glory.

title: Psalms 4:1
text:
This psalm was probably written on the same occasion as  Psalms 3:1-8 . 
 
The gracious answers which God in times past has granted to the prayers of his people, encourage them to continue to call upon him, especially in distress, expecting that he will hear and relieve them.

title: Psalms 4:2
text:
My glory; my kingly dignity conferred upon me by God. 
 
  Leasing; lies.

title: Psalms 4:3
text: Set apart him that is godly; David doubtless refers immediately to himself, as the anointed king of Israel; but the language applies to all who are doing their duty in the sphere to which God has called them.

title: Psalms 4:4
text:
In awe; of God. 
 
  Be still; cease from your attacks upon me, and quietly submit yourselves to God, who has appointed me to be your king. 
 
Acquaintance with one's own heart is essential to a right understanding of our wants as sinners, and of the way of life by faith in Jesus Christ.

title: Psalms 4:6
text:
Any good; real, substantial happiness. 
 
Satisfying enjoyment can be found only in doing the will of God, and in his love.

title: Psalms 4:7
text: Put gladness in my heart; through loving, trusting in, obeying thee, while thou liftest upon me the light of thy countenance.

title: Psalms 5:1
text: Meditation and prayer should be united, and the early part of each day spent in communion with God, and in supplication for his presence and blessing in all its duties and enjoyments.

title: Psalms 5:2
text: My King; to whom he would yield obedience.

title: Psalms 5:5
text:
The foolish; wicked. 
 
  Not stand; not be approved, but condemned.

title: Psalms 5:6
text: To be abhorred by the Lord of hosts is one of the greatest evils that can come upon the children of men, and one which, by repentance of sin and faith in Jesus Christ, they should all be most anxious to avoid.

title: Psalms 5:7
text: Thy house--thy temple; for the public worship of Jehovah.

title: Psalms 5:8
text:
Make thy way straight before my face; open before me a plain and safe path in which I may walk withouit stumbling.  God's way is here the way in which he leads the psalmist.  It is a way of protection as well as of obedience. 
 
When the righteous man is surrounded by enemies he has peculiar need of earnest prayer to be kept from any false step that shall give them an occasion to blaspheme.

title: Psalms 5:9
text:
Their mouth; the mouth of my enemies, who are also the enemies of God and righteousness. 
 
  An open sepulchre; ready to swallow up and destroy.  Compare  Jeremiah 5:16 .

title: Psalms 5:10
text: Destroy thou them; if they turn not from their sins thou wilt destroy them, and all thy people will approve of thy judgments.

title: Psalms 5:11
text: Those who have chosen God as their portion, and who put their trust in him, have cuase for habitual and ever-increasing joy.

title: Psalms 6:1
text:
Written by David under the pressure of deep and long continued suffering, which had its origin in the persecutions to which he was exposed,  Psalms 6:7 Psalms 6:8 Psalms 6:10 , but which seems to have reduced his body to a weak and languishing state. 
 
  Rebuke me not in thine anger; though David's enemies are persecuting him wrongfully, he yet humbly acknowledges the hand of God chastening him through them for his sons. 
 
Confidence in God, and a disposition to look to him for help, and place their hope in his mercy.

title: Psalms 6:2
text:
My bones; my whole frame. 
 
  Are vexed; filled with great distress.

title: Psalms 6:3
text: How long? wilt thou continue to afflict me?

title: Psalms 6:5
text:
For in death there is no remembrance of thee; at death all our opportunities of praising God on earth cease. 
 
The friends of God value life mainly for the opportunities it affords of honoring him and laboring in his cause.

title: Psalms 6:7
text: Waxeth old; becomes dim.

title: Psalms 6:8
text: Great trials, borne with submission, and removed in answer to prayer, are often followed by gladness and exceeding joy.

title: Psalms 6:9
text: Receive my prayer;  hear, and answer me in mercy.

title: Psalms 7:1
text:
Title, Shiggaion; a word of uncertain meaning.  According to some, it is a lyric ode of a bold character; according to others, a bold style of musical performance.  Its plural, Shigionoth, occurs in  Habakkuk 3:1 .  The words of Cush the Benjamite; a slanderous accusation brought by him against David, probably that he sought to take the life of Saul. 
 
Confidence in God, and a disposition to look to him for help, are the grand safeguards in persecution and in all kinds of trouble, and the sure means of ultimate deliverance and triumph.

title: Psalms 7:2
text: He; the persecutor of God's people.

title: Psalms 7:3
text: This; the evil afterwards mentioned.

title: Psalms 7:4
text: True piety towards God and sincere benevolence towards men are essential to acceptance with Him who searches the heart, and will render to every one according to his work.

title: Psalms 7:5
text: Mine honor; here, as in some other passages, a poetical word for soul, or life.   Genesis 49:6 Psalms 16:9 Psalms 57:8 Psalms 108:1

title: Psalms 7:6
text: Commanded; ordained, or appointed.

title: Psalms 7:7
text:
Compass thee about; to hear thy righteous judgments and praise thee for them. 
 
  Return thou on high; to thy judgment-seat, to execute justice upon the wicked.

title: Psalms 7:9
text: True religion will lead those who have it earnestly to desire that the wickedness of the wicked may come to an end, and the righteous be established and prospered over all the earth.

title: Psalms 7:12
text:
If he turn not; if the wicked turn not from his sin.  This condition is to be understood where evil is threatened against the wicked. 
 
  He will whet; God will whet.

title: Psalms 7:14
text:
He; the persecutor. 
 
  Travaileth with iniquity--brought forth falsehood; his plans are all mischievous, and they end in bringing mischief upon himself.  What he sows for others, he reaps for himself.  See note to  Job 15:35 . 
 
The wicked are often the means of their own destructon; and their efforts to ruin others bring ruin upon themselves.

title: Psalms 8:1
text:
Excellent is thy name; glorious are the manifestations of thy character. 
 
The manifestations of the divine perfections in the works of creation and providence are in all respects glorious, and such as should call forth devout and admiring praises from intelligent beings throughout the universe.

title: Psalms 8:2
text:
Ordained strength; literally, founded strength; that is, an impregnable fortress of strength against thine enemies.  This he does by leading little children to proclaim his praise, and thus put to silence his enemies. 
 
  Avenger; the man whose heart and lips are full of impious rage against God.

title: Psalms 8:5
text:
A little lower than the angels; in his nature and condition. 
 
  Crowned him with glory and honor; these words, and those which follow, have their highest fulfilment in Christ, who as Lord of all in our nature is crowned with glory and honor.   Hebrews 2:6-9  
 
The goodness of God to man, in making him head of this lower creation, in taking his nature upon himself in the person of his Son, and giving his life as a ransom, thus opening the way for our deliverance from sin and our preparation for celestial glory, is worthy of grateful celebration to all eternity.

title: Psalms 8:6
text: Under his feet; in subjection to him.

title: Psalms 9:1
text: Praises and all divine worship, to be acceptable to God, must flow from the heart, and be the offspring of sincere and upright devotion to his holy service.

title: Psalms 9:5
text: Thou hast rebuked the heathen; the nations that know not God. These words are spoken by prophetic anticipation.  They describe the final issue of God's judgments upon his enemies.

title: Psalms 9:6
text:
Destructions; those caused by the wicked; they and their works perish together.  But we may better render, As to the enemy, [his] destructions are completed for ever; that is, he is completely destroyed for ever. 
 
Though the wicked may flourish for a time, and succeed in their projects against the righteous, they are destined to complete and everlasting disappointment.

title: Psalms 9:9
text: A refuge; a sure defence.

title: Psalms 9:10
text:
Know thy name; are acquainted with the manifestations which thou hast made of thyself. 
 
Those who are acquainted with the manifestations of God, especially in the person and work of his Son, will in all times of trouble flee to him as their refuge; and in seeking him as their chief good, they will not want any good thing.

title: Psalms 9:11
text: In Zion; in his sanctuary, or among his redeemed people.

title: Psalms 9:12
text: Them; the humble.

title: Psalms 9:14
text: The righteous desire salvation, that the praise of their deliverance from Satan, sin, and death, and of their preparation for heavenly glory, may be given to God.

title: Psalms 9:15
text: In the net which they hid; for the purpose of taking the righteous.

title: Psalms 9:16
text:
The judgment which he executeth; on the wicked. 
 
  Higgaion; this word is rendered "solemn sound,"  Psalms 92:3 .  It seems to denoted an instrumental interlude of some kind, while the voices of the singers rested.

title: Psalms 9:18
text: The poor and the needy may for a time seem to be forgotten, and may be called to exercise long patience; but let them trust in the Lord, and in the end they will see that they have always been remembered, and their highest hopes will be more than realized.

title: Psalms 9:20
text: Put them; that is, the wicked persecutors spoken of in the preceding verses.

title: Psalms 10:3
text: Blesseth the covetous--abhorreth; or, blesseth the covetous, [and] abhorreth the Lord.

title: Psalms 10:4
text:
God is not; the wicked feel and act as if there were no God.  Psalms 10:11-13  
 
Pride leads the wicked to forsake God, and to act as if he had no existence, and as if no one would ever call them to an account for their sins.

title: Psalms 10:5
text: Far above out of his sight; he has no faith in God's word, and because he sees not His threatened judgments, which are reserved in heaven against the appointed time, he utterly disregards them.

title: Psalms 10:10
text:
He croucheth, and humbleth himself; like a lion preparing to spring on his prey.  But many render, "He [the poor man] is crushed, he sinketh down; and the poor fall." 
 
  By his strong ones; probably, by his strong limbs or jaws, the enemy being compared to a lurking lion.

title: Psalms 10:12
text: God is perfectly acquainted with the doings both of the righteous and the wicked, and in due time will appear and render to all according to their words.

title: Psalms 10:15
text: Till thou find none; that remains unpunished.

title: Psalms 11:1
text:
This psalm seems to have been written at a time when law and order were prostrate, and the wicked triumphed over the righteous. 
 
  Ye; addressed to David's timid and unbelieving friends, who counselled flight. 
 
  Flee as a bird; from  Psalms 11:1-3  we have the counsel of those friends. 
 
Without firm confidence in God and a man will be liable to desert the post of duty, and expose himself to the rebukes of the Almighty, and to the triumphs of his foes.

title: Psalms 11:3
text: The foundations; of social order, truth, and piety.

title: Psalms 11:4
text:
His eyelids try; he sees the whole conduct of men, and will protect and save his friends and destroy his enemies.  The psalmist's reply to his unbelieving friends. 
 
However adverse may be the present state of the righteous, or prosperous that of the wicked, the end of the one will be joy and triumph, of the other defeat and ruin.

title: Psalms 12:1
text:
The faithful fail; they are removed by death, and others are not raised up to fill their places. 
 
When pious men die and none are raised up to fill their places, but they are succeeded by the thoughtless, wicked, and profane, the times look dark to the people of God, and lead them to cry with peculiar earnestness to him for help.

title: Psalms 12:2
text:
They; the wicked. 
 
  A double heart; making different representations to different persons, or saying one thing and meaning another.

title: Psalms 12:4
text: Our lips are our own; we will use them as we please.

title: Psalms 12:5
text: In answer to the prayers of those who cry to him, God will arise and plead his own cause, save his people from their oppressors, increase the number of his friends, and cause them to sing for joy.

title: Psalms 12:6
text: The words of the Lord are pure words; all faithfulness and truth, like pure gold or silver that has no dross in it.

title: Psalms 12:7
text:
Them; the poor and needy.  Psalms 12:5  
 
  This generation; the generation of the wicked.

title: Psalms 13:1
text:
Forget me; forbear to deliver me. 
 
The believer may for a time seem to be forgotten, and fear that he shall be cast off for ever; but let him wait upon God, pleading his promises and trusting his grace, and in due time he shall sing of salvation.

title: Psalms 13:2
text: Take counsel in my soul; as to the way and means of deliverance from his troubles.

title: Psalms 13:3
text: Lighten mine eyes; remove from them the darkness of approaching death.

title: Psalms 13:4
text: When I am moved; overcome by his enemies.

title: Psalms 13:6
text:
Dealt bountifully with me; in delivering him from trouble, and bestowing upon him his salvation. 
 
In answer to the prayers of his people, God not only delivers them from troubles, but often does exceeding abundantly above their expectations, causing them to rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory.

title: Psalms 14:1
text:
This psalm occurs again as  Psalms 53:1-6 , with some variations. 
 
  They are corrupt; the practical atheists menitoned in the preceding words, who feel and act as if there were no God. 
 
The man who wishes that there were no God, or who feels and acts as if there were none, is in the most emphatic sense a fool.

title: Psalms 14:2
text:
Did understand, and seek God; had any true knowledge of God, or desire for communion with him.  This is to be understood as referring to men's natural state. 
 
The atheism of the heart is the fruitful source of every crime.  They who give themselves up to the practice of sin, banish the thoughts of God; and having done this, have nothing to restrain them from every iniquity.

title: Psalms 14:3
text:
Not one; that naturally does any thing spiritually good. 
 
All the good that is done or experienced in this apostate world, is the fruit of the grace of God.

title: Psalms 14:4
text: Eat up my people; plunder and destroy them.

title: Psalms 14:5
text:
There; in the midst of their wicked oppression of the righteous. 
 
  Were they in great fear; the judgment of God overtook them, and put them in great fear. 
 
Persecutors of God's people often have fearful forebodings of coming wrath.

title: Psalms 14:6
text:
Shamed; held up to contempt. 
 
Though the poor may be derided for their confidence in God, he will not disappoint them, but in due time will appear to their everlasting joy.

title: Psalms 14:7
text: Out of Zion; the dwelling-place of God; where he manifested his presence.

title: Psalms 15:1
text: Who shall abide in thy tabernacle? be admitted, as an acceptable worshipper, to thine earthly temple, and be qualified to dwell with thee in glory.

title: Psalms 15:2
text:
Walketh uprightly; conducts according to the will of God, in sincerity and righteousness and truth. 
 
Sincerity, honesty, and truthfulness in feeling and conduct; kindness and benevolence towards others; abhorrence of wickedness in every form, and delight in the holiness and happiness of them that fear and love the Lord; fidelity to all lawful engagements, and a disposition to use property in relieving the needy and in doing good, are evidences of devotion to God and preparation to dwell with him in his heavenly kingdom.

title: Psalms 15:3
text: Backbiteth not--nor doeth evil; does not injure another in word or deed.

title: Psalms 15:4
text:
Vile; wicked. 
 
  Changeth not; keeps his word, though it causes him great sacrifices.

title: Psalms 15:5
text:
To usury; the Hebrew was not allowed to receive interest for money lent to his brother Hebrew.   Exodus 22:25 Leviticus 25:36-37 Deuteronomy 23:19-20 . The spirit of these words forbids our taking unlawful or extravagant pay for the use of money, and requires us to employ our property in the service of God and to his glory. 
 
  Reward against the innocent; a bribe offered to induce him to condemn the innocent. 
 
  Never be moved; he shall have true prosperity and happiness on earth, and an everlasting abode.

title: Psalms 16:1
text: Though we cannot, by our best services, merit any good at the hand of God, or be profitable to him, we may thus benefit ourselves and our fellow men; and if we delight in doing good, especially to the friends of God for his sake, we shall have evidence that he is our portion and that it will never be taken away.

title: Psalms 16:2
text: Extendeth not to; doth not profit.

title: Psalms 16:4
text: Their drink-offerings of blood; such as were offered to idols.

title: Psalms 16:6
text: The lines; measuring lines used in the distribution of land; put here for the heritage measured out by them.  The whole of this verse is to be understood not literally of David's earthly heritage in the land of Canaan, but figuratively of God himself, as his all-satisfying portion.

title: Psalms 16:7
text:
My reins also instruct me; his midnight meditations united with the word and providences of God in affording him instruction as to his duty. 
 
The meditations of believers, by night and by day, concur with the word and the providences of God in giving them a knowledge of his will.

title: Psalms 16:9
text:
My glory; his most glorious spiritual part, his soul. 
 
  My flesh; his body.

title: Psalms 16:10
text:
In hell; in the Old Testament, the word hell is often used for the invisible world, or place of the dead, without describing their condition. 
 
  To see corruption; Christ's body arose from the grave without seeing corruption,  Acts 2:25-28 Acts 2:31 ; and the bodies of believers shall be delivered from corruption by virtue of their union with him. 
 
The victory of our Lord Jesus Christ over death and hell was a victory for himself the head, and for his body the church.  Because God has shown him the path of life, he will show it to them also that are united to him by faith.  Though their bodies go down to the grave, they will not be left there for ever.  When Christ shall appear the second time, all who have died in him shall be raised up incorruptible and glorious.  "For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality."   I Corinthians 15:52-55

title: Psalms 16:11
text: Life; the eternal life of both soul and body in God's presence. Christ has received eternal life for himself and for all that believe in him.   John 14:19

title: Psalms 17:1
text:
Feigned; insincere. 
 
Sincerity of soul in our prayers is essential to acceptance with God. He searches the heart and tries the reins of the children of men, and those who worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.

title: Psalms 17:3
text: In the night; when the mind is free from outward occupations, and its true bent is manifested most clearly.

title: Psalms 17:4
text:
The works of men; their evil works. 
 
  By the word of thy lips; by giving heed to it.   Psalms 119:9  
 
  From the paths of the destroyer; from walking in his paths; that is, imitating his ways.  The destroyer is the wicked and bloody oppressor of his fellow-men, who makes himself rich and great by violence and falsehood. 
 
The words of the Lord are the great means of keeping his people from those paths of iniquity which end in ruin.

title: Psalms 17:8
text:
As the apple of the eye; in perfect safety. 
 
Confidence in God is the grand means of security, and those who trust in him shall be kept in perfect safety.

title: Psalms 17:10
text: They are inclosed in their own fat; or, they have shut up their fat, that is, their fat heart.  They have pampered themselves by self-indulgence, and thus become hard-hearted and insensible in respect to both God and man.

title: Psalms 17:11
text: They have set their eyes bowing down to the earth; as a beast of prey before he springs upon his victim.  But we may better render, "They have set their eyes [upon the righteous] to cast [him] down to the earth."

title: Psalms 17:13
text: Thy sword; the instrument by which God punishes his people.

title: Psalms 17:14
text: Hid treasure; earthly good.

title: Psalms 17:15
text:
When I awake; in the world to come. 
 
  With thy likeness; with beholding thy likeness.  To behold the likeness of God, is to behold God himself.  So  Numbers 12:8 , where the original word is the same. 
 
As the beatific vision of God in heaven is reserved for all the righteous, they have no occasion to envy rich and prosperous sinners who have their portion in this life.   Luke 16:25

title: Psalms 18:1
text: This psalm is nearly the same as  II Samuel 22:1-51 .

title: Psalms 18:2
text:
My rock, and my fortress; source of support and security. 
 
The Lord is the safeguard and protector of his people, and supplication to him in all times of trouble is the grand means of deliverance.

title: Psalms 18:4
text:
vv 4-5. 
 
  Sorrows of death-- sorrows of hell; or, Cords of death, cords of hell; that is, snares set to take away his life and bring him down to hell, the word hell being here used, as in  Psalms 16:10 , for the place of the dead. 
 
  Prevented me; met me and stopped my way, wherever I turned.

title: Psalms 18:9
text:
Bowed the heavens; bent them aside as a curtain. 
 
At the appearance of God all the elements do him homage, and as his servants are entirely under his control.  He uses them and disposes of them as seemeth good in his sight.

title: Psalms 18:10
text: Cherub; the cherubim are represented as the bearers of God's throne,  Ezekiel 10:1-22 .

title: Psalms 18:12
text: At the brightness that was before him; literally, From the brightness before him.  Jehovah is represented as dwelling in light unapproachable, whence proceed thick clouds with tempests of hail and lightning.

title: Psalms 18:14
text: Scattered them; my enemies.

title: Psalms 18:15
text: Channels of waters--foundations of the world; the deep abysses of the sea.  These are made bare by the convulsions of nature.

title: Psalms 18:16
text: Many waters; numerous and great troubles.

title: Psalms 18:18
text:
Prevented me; thrust themselves before me and intercepted my escape. 
 
In times of calamity the Lord is the support of his people, and he will deliver and save all who put their trust in him.

title: Psalms 18:25
text: The Lord will treat men, in many respects, as the treat their fellow men.   Matthew 6:14-15

title: Psalms 18:26
text: Show thyself froward; be opposed to those who oppose thee.

title: Psalms 18:28
text: Light my candle; grant him light in darkness.

title: Psalms 18:29
text:
By my God; by his help. 
 
  Leaped over a wall; surmounted the wall of the enemy's fortress, and thus taken it by storm.

title: Psalms 18:30
text: Buckler; shield, protection.

title: Psalms 18:32
text: For all their successes the people of God are indebted to him, and to him they give up the glory.

title: Psalms 18:33
text:
Like hinds' feet; the hind is celebrated for its fleetness. 
 
  Upon my high places; where I am safe from my enemies.

title: Psalms 18:34
text: Is broken; or, is bent.  The bending of a bow of steel represents the strength he has received from Jehovah.

title: Psalms 18:40
text: The necks of mine enemies; caused my enemies to turn their backs before me.   Exodus 23:27

title: Psalms 18:41
text: The wicked may call upon God when he will not answer; they may seek him early and not find him.  If they hate knowledge, and do not choose the fear of the Lord, they must eat the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices.   Proverbs 1:23-32

title: Psalms 18:42
text: Beat them small; utterly destroy them.

title: Psalms 18:45
text: Their close places; their fortresses.

title: Psalms 18:50
text: To his seed; to whom God had confirmed the kingdom for ever.  II Samuel 7:12 II Samuel 7:16   The seed of David is, in a special sense, Christ; and, in Christ, all who have like precious faith with David.

title: Psalms 19:1
text:
The subject of  Psalms 19:1-6  is the revelation which God makes of himself in the heavens;  Psalms 19:7-11 , the revelation which he has given in his word, with its blessed effect on those who receive and obey it.  Then  Psalms 19:12-14 , a prayer that God would help the psalmist to be conformed, inwardly and outwardly, to this perfect rule, that he may be accepted and not put to shame before his Maker. 
 
In the creation and government of the world, the invisible things of God, even his eternal power and Godhead, may be so clearly seen, that all who do not render him spiritual homage will be without excuse.  Romans 1:20

title: Psalms 19:2
text: Day unto day--night unto night; each day and night delivers over to the succeeding day and night the work of declaring God's glory, so that the testimony of the heavens is uninterrupted from age to age.

title: Psalms 19:3
text: No speech--their voice is not heard; they do not speak in words to the ear, but to the understanding and the feelings.

title: Psalms 19:4
text: Their words; in silence speak to the hearts of those who attend to them.

title: Psalms 19:7
text:
The law of the Lord; the doctrine or truth which he has revealed. 
 
  Converting the soul; that believes and obeys it. 
 
  Making wise; all who embrace it. 
 
The written word of God is perfect as a rule of faith and practice, making all who follow it wise unto salvation; by being led to renounce all dependence upon their own righteousness, to trust alone for acceptance with God upon the atonement, righteousness, and intercession of Christ, and to seek to please him by keeping his commandments.

title: Psalms 19:8
text:
The statutes of the Lord; what he has ordained. 
 
  The commandment of the Lord; his requirements.

title: Psalms 19:9
text:
Clean; pure and purifying. 
 
  Judgments; decisions, especially judicial decisions.

title: Psalms 19:10
text: More to be desired--than gold; because true and right; making wise, excellent, useful, and happy all who follow them.

title: Psalms 19:12
text:
His errors; as seen in the light of the perfect and all-comprehensive law of God. 
 
  Secret faults; those which escape his own notice. 
 
The more men become acquainted with the Bible, and the more they are in the habit of comparing their hearts and lives with its requirements, the greater will be their conviction of the number and aggravations of their sins, and of their need of the grace, strength, and salvation of the Redeemer.

title: Psalms 19:13
text:
Presumptuous sins; committed against light and knowledge. 
 
  From the great transgression; more literally, from much transgression, such as must be the certain result of ignorance of God's law, or inattention to it.

title: Psalms 20:1
text:
Defend thee; by the manifestation of his power and grace.  In these words the church prays for her divinely appointed head. 
 
The manifestations of the perfections of God are a sure protection of his people, and those who trust in him will find him an habitual and all sufficient defence.   II Chronicles 20:8-9 Proverbs 18:10

title: Psalms 20:2
text: From the sanctuary--out of Zion; where God dwelt between the cherubim.

title: Psalms 20:5
text:
In thy salvation; in the salvation granted to thee, our king, by God. 
 
Those who form their plans and undertake their enterprises in the name of the Lord, and for the purpose of honoring him, will find in him a ground of dependence more safe and more efficacious than fleets and armies, or any aid that mere creatures can afford.

title: Psalms 20:6
text: His anointed; David was the Lord's anointed, and as such was a type of the Messiah.

title: Psalms 20:7
text: The name of the Lord; his manifestations of himself in behalf of his people.

title: Psalms 20:8
text: They are brought down; those who trust in earthly help,  Psalms 20:7 .

title: Psalms 20:9
text: The King; King of heaven, Jehovah.

title: Psalms 21:1
text: The Lord's salvation is the joy and rejoicing of his people.  They glory in it, as the ground of all their present blessings, and all their future hopes.

title: Psalms 21:3
text: Preventest him; meetest him as a friend and helper.

title: Psalms 21:4
text: He asked life of thee; the life here spoken of seems not to be simply David's life as a man, but to include the life of his successors upon the throne which was to be perpetuated "for ever and ever" in Christ.

title: Psalms 21:5
text: Honor and majesty hast thou laid upon him; by establishing the throne of his kingdom for ever.   II Samuel 7:13 II Samuel 7:16

title: Psalms 21:8
text: However long God may bear with the wicked, and however numerous the blessings which he may bestow upon them, if his blessings do not lead them to repentance, but are abused, they will only be the means of ripening them for a more aggravated destruction.

title: Psalms 21:9
text: As a fiery oven; utterly consuming them.

title: Psalms 22:1
text:
This psalm has its chief fulfilment in Christ.  It is fulfilled in all his followers, so far as they constitute his body and suffer with him. 
 
  My God, my God; the language of Christ on the cross.   Matthew 27:46  
 
We should never forget that all the sufferings of the Saviour were for our sakes, that we might be saved from the pangs of the second death, and inherit everlasting life and glory.   John 3:16

title: Psalms 22:2
text: Thou hearest not; God did not answer in the removal of David's sufferings.

title: Psalms 22:6
text: I am a worm; exceedingly weak and despised, and treated with contempt.

title: Psalms 22:7
text: They shoot out the lip; expressive of the manner in which the multitude treated the Saviour.

title: Psalms 22:8
text:
Let him deliver him; the ironical language of his opposers. 
 
  Seeing he delighted in him; seeing God delighted in this sufferer, who is the Messiah. 
 
The exactness with which the circumstances of our Saviour's crucifixion were foretold more than a thousand years before it took place, is evidence that the Bible inspired, and that holy men in preparing it wrote as they were moved by the Holy Ghost; so that what they wrote is the testimony of God.

title: Psalms 22:9
text: Thou art he; the language of the Saviour, expressive of his holy confidence in God the Father.

title: Psalms 22:12
text:
Many bulls; his numerous, fierce, and strong enemies. 
 
  Bulls of Bashan; the fiercest and strongest.

title: Psalms 22:14
text: Poured out like water; expressive of extreme weakness, the most exhausting sufferings.

title: Psalms 22:16
text:
They pierced my hands and my feet;  Matthew 27:44 John 19:23-21:25 
 
The wicked, in crucifying the Lord of glory, did, without intending it or thinking of it, precisely what God declared a thousand years before that they would do.   Acts 2:23

title: Psalms 22:20
text: My darling; an expression for his soul or life, as his most precious possession, and one that could not be replaced when destroyed.

title: Psalms 22:21
text: The horns of the unicorns; the power and malice of his mightiest and most cruel opposers.

title: Psalms 22:22
text:
My brethren; the redeemed, whom Christ made his brethren by taking upon himself their nature.   Hebrews 2:11-14   The victory over his enemies, which the Saviour here anticipates, is shared by all his followers. 
 
The Scriptures were fulfilled not only in the curcifixion of our Lord, but also in his resurrection and the events which followed.

title: Psalms 22:25
text: I will pay my vows; the vows made in the time of my trouble. According to Hebrew usage, they consisted of thank-offerings, which were a form of peace-offering, and were paid publicly at the tabernacle or temple in the presence of the congregation.   Psalms 116:14-19  After certain prescribed portions had been burned on the altar, the offerer and his friends feasted on the remainder.  Leviticus 3:1-17 Leviticus 3:1-17  When, on occasions of great joy, kings offered peace-offerings, they made a feast for the whole people.   II Samuel 6:18-19 I Kings 8:62-66   In allusion to these sacrificial vows of the ancient Hebrews, the mighty sufferer of this psalm, who is David in the type but Christ in the antitype, promises, when he has obtained deliverance, to spread a feast for "all the kindreds of the nations,"  Psalms 22:26-29 .  Compare  Isaiah 25:6 Isaiah 55:1-2 .

title: Psalms 22:26
text: Shall eat; of the feast provided by the Redeemer, when he pays his vows for deliverance.  The allusion is to the sacrificial vows of the ancient Hebrews.

title: Psalms 22:27
text: All the ends of the world; people of all countries.  This shall be the fruit of the Saviour's sufferings.   Isaiah 53:10-11

title: Psalms 22:28
text: He is the governor among the nations; the rightful King of all people.

title: Psalms 22:29
text:
All they that be fat upon earth; the rich, great, and powerful. 
 
  They that go down to the dust; the poor, afflicted, and despised. All classes must partake of his salvation, or perish. 
 
The Scriptures will yet be fulfilled in the universal spread of the gospel, and in all people's bowing in cheerful and willing obedience to the Saviour; owning him as the Lord their righteousness and salvation, and giving united, hearty, and everlasting thanks to his great and holy name.

title: Psalms 22:30
text: A generation; a posterity that shall serve the Lord.

title: Psalms 22:31
text: Declare his righteousness; they shall declare to those who come after them the righteousness of the Lord as the ground of human hope, and what he has done for the lost children of men.

title: Psalms 23:1
text:
My shepherd; to feed, guide, and protect him.  Compare  John 10:10-16 . 
 
Those who have Jehovah to protect and provide for them, will not want any good thing.  He will giude them by his counsel while on earth, and afterwards receive them to glory.

title: Psalms 23:2
text: Green pastures; expressive of the refreshment and support which by his ordinances the Lord grants his people.

title: Psalms 23:3
text: His name's sake; the display of his perfections.

title: Psalms 23:4
text:
Thy rod and thy staff; the shepherd's badges, and the symbols of his presence. 
 
To the believer, even the valley of the shadow of death will be illuminated with the presence and favor of Jehovah, so that he shall fear no evil, but when absent from the body, shall be present with the Lord and rejoice for ever in the fulness of his love.

title: Psalms 23:5
text: My cup; of blessings.

title: Psalms 23:6
text: Dwell in the house of the Lord; be admitted to the membership of God's holy family, enjoy communion with him, and dwell in his presence for ever.  Compare  Psalms 16:11 Psalms 49:15 Psalms 73:24 ; and especially  Psalms 36:7-9 .

title: Psalms 24:1
text:
There is much in the character of this psalm to favor the ancient supposition that it was sung on the occasion of the transfer of the ark to the tabernacle which David had pitched for it on Zion.   II Samuel 6:12-19  
 
As Jehovah is the creator and preserver, so his is the owner of the world and all things therein; and he has a perfect right to govern and dispose of all as seemeth good in his sight.

title: Psalms 24:2
text: Founded it upon the seas--established it upon the floods; the allusion is to the fact that the dry land rises out of the depths of the ocean, as if it had this for its foundation.   Psalms 136:6

title: Psalms 24:3
text:
Who shall ascend--who shall stand; whom will God admit there as an acceptable worshipper?  See note to  Psalms 15:1 . 
 
  His holy place; the place of his immediate presence on mount Zion.

title: Psalms 24:4
text:
Lifted up his soul unto vanity; given to vanity his love and confidence.  Vanity includes all earthly confidences, but especially trust in false gods. 
 
Purity of heart and of life is essential to our enjoying the presence and favor of Jehovah, and is the evidence of our being interested in his salvation.

title: Psalms 24:6
text: Him; the God of salvation.

title: Psalms 24:7
text: Lift up your heads; sung, it is supposed, when the ark, the symbol of God's presence, entered the gates of mount Zion.  They are called everlasting because the true Zion, which the literal earthly Zion represented in David's day, is everlasting.  In the same way the symbolical entrance of God into the earthly Zion through the ark of the covenant, may be regarded as prefiguring the entrance of Christ, the King of glory, into the heavenly Zion.

title: Psalms 24:8
text: The King of glory is mighty to save and mighty to destroy; his friends through his grace will be saved with an everlasting salvation, and his enemies be utterly and for ever destroyed.

title: Psalms 25:1
text: This is the first of the alphabetic psalms; that is, psalms where the verses correspond to the twenty-two letters of the Hebrew alphabet, each beginning with one of its letters in regular order.  As the natural result of their structure, such psalms consist rather of collections of pious thought and sentiments, than of connected trains of discourse.

title: Psalms 25:4
text: Right views of ourselves will lead us to feel our need of being taught of God, and habitually to seek help from him.

title: Psalms 25:7
text: Sins committed in youth may, even when repented of, greatly imbitter the comforts of age, and be felt in their effects to the end of life.

title: Psalms 25:8
text: In the way; the way of truth and of duty God will teach to all sinners who feel their need of being taught, and are disposed to learn of him.   Matthew 11:28-30

title: Psalms 25:10
text: The paths of the Lord; the ways in which he deals with his people are wise, faithful, and gracious, however trying and mysterious they may sometimes be.

title: Psalms 25:11
text: The greatness of one's iniquities is no insuperable barrier to their being pardoned, and may, in some cases, be pleaded as a reason why the Lord, to the honor of his abounding grace, should show mercy.  Romans 5:20

title: Psalms 25:14
text:
The secret of the Lord; his intimate friendship, with the blessedness and prosperity which it gives. 
 
The blessedness of serving God is known only by being experienced, and can be known in no other way.

title: Psalms 25:15
text: Out of the net; deliver him from his enemies.

title: Psalms 25:18
text:
My sins; the cause of his troubles. 
 
Sin is viewed by the penitent soul as the cause of all his troubles; and he is more anxious to be delivered from it than from all outward distresses.

title: Psalms 25:22
text:
Israel; the people of God. 
 
The benevolent soul desires and prays for the choicest of heaven's blessings not only on itself, but on all who love and serve the Lord, throughtout the earth.

title: Psalms 26:2
text: The humble and penitent believer will not trust to his own heart, but knowing its deceitfulness he will habitually apply to God to search him and try him, and to lead him in the way everlasting.

title: Psalms 26:4
text:
Vain persons; persons of falsehood. 
 
  Disemblers; hypocrites.

title: Psalms 26:6
text:
Wash my hands; avoid all impurity. 
 
  Compass thine altar; that I may there offer sacrifices to thee. 
 
An indispensible prepartion for worshipping God acceptably, is the putting away of iniquity in heart and life.   Matthew 5:23-24

title: Psalms 26:8
text: The dwelling place of God is peculiarly dear to his people, and their joy in the manifestations of his presence gives them reason to hope that they shall dwell with him for ever.

title: Psalms 26:9
text: Gather not my soul with sinners; take not away my soul with sinners.

title: Psalms 26:11
text: While the people of God are careful to be sincere, upright, and honest in their lives, and trust for salvation only in the mercy of God in Christ Jesus, they stand on firm ground, and may walk in safety through all the snares and dangers of life.

title: Psalms 26:12
text: Even place; on firm, solid ground.

title: Psalms 27:1
text:
My salvation; Saviour, author of salvation. 
 
Those who have God for their Saviour, Protector, and Guide, have no reason to fear, but may walk through life and through the valley of the shadow of death unmoved by the enemies and dangers that may surround them.

title: Psalms 27:2
text: Eat up my flesh; destroy me.

title: Psalms 27:3
text:
In this; even in this situation. 
 
  Be confident; that God will be my salvation.

title: Psalms 27:4
text: May dwell in the house of the Lord; as one of his household,  Psalms 27:5 .  It is not merely the public worship of God in his sanctuary which the psalmist desires, but also that inward union and communion with God, of which this is the visible earthly embodiment.

title: Psalms 27:5
text:
His pavilion; where he himself dwells, and where I shall be safe from all the assaults of my foes. 
 
  Secret; hiding-place, as the original word is elsewhere rendered.  Psalms 32:7 Psalms 91:1  
 
God's favor and friendship constitute a more effectual protection than all earthly resources.  The man whose feet God sets upon a rock cannot be cast down by the assaults of his enemies.

title: Psalms 27:6
text: Though the believer will come off conqueror and more than conqueror over all his foes, yet it will be wholly through the grace of God, and to Him he will give all the glory.

title: Psalms 27:8
text: Thy face, Lord, will I seek; his inclinations corresponded with his duty.

title: Psalms 27:10
text:
When my father and my mother forsake me; in times of the most complete desertion.  He mentions father and mother, because they are the last to forsake one. 
 
Though the believer should be forsaken of all earthly friends, and even have not where to lay his head, God will befriend him, provide for him, and bestow upon him all which he needs and which will promote his highest good.

title: Psalms 27:11
text:
Thy way; the way of thine appointment, the same as the "plain path" mentioned in the next clause.  It is both the way of duty, and the way of divine protection and safety. 
 
  Plain path; that is, as the original denotes, a level path, where there is no danger of stumbling. 
 
The believer who is surrounded by powerful and crafty foes has especial need to pray for divine guidance, that he may be preserved from every false step and kept in the path of duty.

title: Psalms 27:14
text:
Wait on the Lord; by prayer and supplication, and in the use of all the appointed means of grace. 
 
Waiting upon the Lord in the way of his appointment, his people will renew their strength, will mount up on wings as eagles, run and not be weary, walk and not faint.

title: Psalms 28:1
text:
My rock; my firm and unfailing support. 
 
Nothing but the grace of God and constant help from him, can keep even believers from falling away to their own destruction.

title: Psalms 28:2
text: Thy holy oracle; the inner sanctuary, where God dwelt between the cherubim.

title: Psalms 28:3
text: Draw me not away; take me not away to punishment.

title: Psalms 28:5
text: Disregard of God and his ways is the means of destruction to those who continue in it.

title: Psalms 28:7
text: Trust in the Lord is the sure means of defence from all enemies, and a preparation for everlasting joy and praise.

title: Psalms 28:8
text:
Their strength; the strength of his people. 
 
  His anointed; David, as the anointed head of God's people, representing Christ, who is in a higher sense the anointed of God.

title: Psalms 29:1
text:
Give; ascribe. 
 
  Ye mighty; or, ye sons of the mighty; these words are most naturally understood of the holy angels. Compare  Psalms 103:20 Psalms 148:2 .

title: Psalms 29:2
text: All the blessings which are enjoyed even by the most mighty of God's creatures, come from God, and lay them under peculiar obligations to love and adore him.

title: Psalms 29:3
text: The voice of the Lord; as in a storm of lightning and thunder.

title: Psalms 29:4
text: The voice of the Lord in thunder, lightning, earthquakes, and tempests is omnipotent; nothing can stand before it.  He speaks, and it is done; accomplishing his pleasure in heaven, on earth, and throughout all places of his vast dominion.  None can stay his power, or say to him, What doest thou?

title: Psalms 29:6
text: Sirion; the Zidonian name of Hermon, a summit of Anti-Lebanon.

title: Psalms 29:7
text: Divideth the flames of fire; parteth the lightnings.

title: Psalms 29:8
text: Kadesh; a wilderness on the southern boundary of Palestine.

title: Psalms 29:9
text:
Discovereth the forests; strips them bare by tempests. 
 
  In his temple; his heavenly temple, or his palace in the skies, where he sits as king upon the flood.

title: Psalms 29:10
text:
The flood; the waters above the firmament.  Compare  Psalms 104:3 . But as the original word is everywhere else applied to the deluge of Noah, we may perhaps better render the clause, "Jehovah sat upon the deluge;" that is, he presided, as the Judge of all the earth, over that mighty catastrophe.  The connection of thought between a tempest of thunder and lightning and the deluge is easy and natural. 
 
Amidst all the convulsions of nature, the Lord reigns, King over all; giving strength, security, and joy to his people, and overruling all to work out for them an exceeding and an eternal weight of glory.

title: Psalms 30:1
text: Title:  others render this title thus:  A Psalm, a Song of dedication for the house, by David; and they suppose the reference to be to the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, which David purchased upon the occasion of the pestilence with which Israel was visited for his sin in numbering the people.  Of this David said, "This is the house of the Lord God,"  I Chronicles 22:1 , and it seems probable, from the verses that follow, that he then dedicated that spot as the site of the future temple.  With this supposition the contents of the psalm well agree.

title: Psalms 30:2
text: Prayer is the grand means of deliverance from trouble; and when deliverance is granted, devout praises should be rendered to God, the author and giver of all good.

title: Psalms 30:6
text: Continued prosperity often leads men to forget their dependence on God, and makes affliction needful to teach them that all their blessings come from him.

title: Psalms 30:7
text: Made my mountain to stand strong; given me steadfast prosperity.

title: Psalms 30:11
text: God brings his people out of trouble, that they may unite in praising and adoring him.

title: Psalms 30:12
text: My glory; my soul, as the word is elsewhere used.  See note to  Psalms 7:5 , where the word in the original is the same as here.

title: Psalms 31:3
text: For the display of his own perfections, believers beseech God to deliver them from their troubles, and daily they commit themselves, their lives, and all their interests to his disposal.

title: Psalms 31:4
text: They; his enemies.

title: Psalms 31:7
text: Known my soul; acknowledged and delivered me.

title: Psalms 31:8
text: A large room; a place where he might enjoy freedom and safety.

title: Psalms 31:9
text: Sin is the cause of every sorrow, and the penitent soul desires deliverance from this more than from outward troubles; and for this mercy he looks to the rich grace of God in Jesus Christ.

title: Psalms 31:10
text:
Because of mine iniquity; though the presecutions to which he was subjected by his enemies were unjust, he yet humbly acknowledges in them God's hand chastising him for his sins. 
 
  My bones are consumed; decayed, waxed old, and worn out with distresses.

title: Psalms 31:11
text: Fled from me; lest they should be involved in his ruin.

title: Psalms 31:15
text: My times; the trials and changes of life and the hour of death. Though surrounded with enemies who sought his life, they could do nothing except what God suffered them.

title: Psalms 31:19
text: Confidence in God, manifested under great trials, honors him and inspires hope in his mercy.  Those who experience it, wish to have all unite in praising and adoring him for his wonderful love to the children of men.

title: Psalms 31:20
text:
A pavilion; a secure hiding-place. 
 
  The strife of tongues; the war which their enemies make upon them by the weapons of calumny and falsehood.

title: Psalms 31:21
text: In a strong city; by placing me in a fenced city, or by giving me protection like that which a fenced city furnishes.

title: Psalms 32:1
text:
The probable occasion of this psalm was the season of anguish and remorse through which David passed in consequence of his sin in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.   II Samuel 11:1-27  
 
  Covered; blotted out, pardoned. 
 
Forgiveness of sins is essential to happiness here or hereafter, and those who receive it may be pronounced truly blessed, both in this world and the world to come.

title: Psalms 32:3
text:
Kept silence; refused to confess his sins. 
 
  Waxed old; through the greatness of his distress.

title: Psalms 32:4
text: My moisture is turned into the drought of summer; he became emaciated and dried up nder the burden of his iniquities.

title: Psalms 32:5
text: Ingenuous confession of sin and hearty turning from it are essential to forgiveness; and those who will not confess and forsake it, must suffer its dreadful consequences for ever.

title: Psalms 32:6
text: For this; on account of God's readiness to pardon.

title: Psalms 32:8
text: Those who by repentance of sin and faith in Jesus Christ have turned to God and found pardoning mercy, are exceedingly anxious that others should take the same blessed way, and thus obtain rest, peace, and joy to their souls.

title: Psalms 32:9
text: The horse--the mule; which refuse to be governed except by force.

title: Psalms 32:10
text: The wicked; those who refuse to yield obedience to the divine will.

title: Psalms 33:4
text: The Lord is worthy of universal praise and adoration, not only for what he is in himself, but for what he has manifested of himself to the children of men.  All his works praise him, and his saints bless him.

title: Psalms 33:7
text: Layeth up the depth; restraineth the waters in their places.

title: Psalms 33:8
text: The manifestations of God in creation and in providence show that he is infinite, and lay men under obligations to worship him with reverence and holy fear.

title: Psalms 33:9
text: It was done; the earth was created.

title: Psalms 33:10
text: The heathen; the nations that know not God.

title: Psalms 33:12
text: Those who choose God as their portion, his service as their employment, and his favor as their reward, will be truly and for ever blessed.

title: Psalms 33:15
text: Fashioneth their hearts alike; that is, as the original means, the heart of one as well as of another.  As he is the former of the hearts of all, so he knows the thoughts of all.

title: Psalms 33:18
text: Upon them; for their good.

title: Psalms 33:19
text: No reliance can be placed on creatures for safety, without the protecting care and kindness of Jehovah.  He taketh pleasure in those that fear him and that hope in his mercy.

title: Psalms 34:1
text:
Title, changed his behavior; or, more literally, changed his understanding, that is, feigned himself mad.   I Samuel 21:13  
 
We always have reason to bless God, whatever may be our present condition; our mercies are great and multiplied, and our sufferings less than we deserve.

title: Psalms 34:2
text: Make her boast in the Lord; glory in him as my all-sufficient good.

title: Psalms 34:4
text: Jehovah can deliver his people not only from evil, but also from the fear of it; so that in seeking him they shall not want any good, but be kept in perfect peace and filled with joy unspeakable, their minds being stayed on him.

title: Psalms 34:5
text: They; who seek the Lord as their chief good.

title: Psalms 34:6
text: This poor man; David, who had been delivered from great and sore distresses.

title: Psalms 34:7
text: The angel of the Lord; the minister of God's will, sent to deliver all who trust in him.

title: Psalms 34:9
text: No want; of any thing which will conduce to their highest good.

title: Psalms 34:11
text: Those who know the blessedness of fearing, loving, and obeying God, are desirous that all others, especially the young, should experience the same benefit; and the earlier in life they become devoted to him, the greater ordinarily will be their excellence, usefulness, and happiness in future years.

title: Psalms 34:15
text: Upon the righteous; for their benefit.

title: Psalms 34:17
text: Supplication to God in trouble is the unfailing resource of his people, and they have blessed experience from time to time of his willingness and power to save.

title: Psalms 34:18
text: Of a broken heart; humbled and penitent for sin, and turned from the love and practice of it to God.

title: Psalms 34:20
text: Not one of them is broken; the meaning of this and other like promises is, that God continually watches over the bodies of his saints, as well as over their souls, so that no real evil can befall them.  Whatever discipline he sees good to lay upon their bodies, he will make conducive to their highest welfare; so that though it be in respect to its outward form an evil, it is turned by his providence and grace into a blessing.

title: Psalms 34:21
text:
vv 21-22. 
 
  Be desolate; the word in the original means, be held guilty, and, as such, be destroyed.

title: Psalms 35:4
text:
Let them be confounded; this form of expression is a prediction of what will take place with regard to those who continue in wickedness, and also implies denunciation uttered by inspired men against the enemies of God. 
 
Those who perseveringly oppose God and his people will be confounded and put to shame.  They will be cast away as worthless and be destroyed.

title: Psalms 35:5
text:
As chaff; driven by the wind and utterly destroyed. 
 
  The angel of the Lord; the minister of God's will, sent to destroy his enemies.

title: Psalms 35:8
text:
Him; the chief persecutor, who had excited others to the same diabolical work. 
 
Leaders in persecution will be distinguished in their punishment, and the destruction which they sought to bring upon others will come on themselves.

title: Psalms 35:10
text: All my bones; the bones are here put for the whole man.

title: Psalms 35:11
text: I knew not; was ignorant of, because I had not committed them.

title: Psalms 35:13
text:
Returned into mine own bosom; he experienced the benefit of his prayers, though they did not benefit his enemies. 
 
The people of God should never be overcome of evil, but endeavor to overcome evil with good; and in this way, if they do not benefit others, they will greatly benefit themselves.

title: Psalms 35:17
text: My darling; my soul.   Psalms 22:20

title: Psalms 35:18
text: The friends of God desire his salvation, not only on account of its effects on themselves, but that God may be honored, and increasing multitudes be led to glorify him.

title: Psalms 35:19
text: Wink with the eye; in malicious triumph.

title: Psalms 35:20
text: Them that are quiet in the land; the meek and peaceable servants of God.

title: Psalms 35:21
text: Aha; an expression of triumph and contempt.

title: Psalms 35:26
text: The destruction of the people of God would bring great dishonor on him, while their deliverance and salvation will be greatly to his glory.

title: Psalms 36:1
text:
Saith within my heart; is conclusive evidence to me. 
 
The conduct of wicked men shows the state of their hearts, and none are the friends of God who do not make it their great object habitually to obey him.

title: Psalms 36:2
text:
He flattereth himself; that he is good, notwithstanding all his iniquities. 
 
Wicked men live in contrast self-flattery and self-delusion.  Thus they keep themselves ignorant of their true character, and encourage themselves in a life of sin, till they perish without remedy.

title: Psalms 36:3
text: When men neglect to do what they know to be right, they deliberately do what they know to be evil; and unless restrained by the grace of God, will grow worse and worse till they perish.

title: Psalms 36:5
text: The glorious perfections of God infinitely surpass every thing in nature; and are a sure foundation of confidence to all who trust in him.

title: Psalms 36:7
text: By the loving kindness of God many are led to trust in him, and thus to learn that in the keeping of his commands there is great reward.  In his presence their is fulness of joy, and at his right hand there are pleasures for evermore.

title: Psalms 36:8
text: Fatness of thy house; its abundant spiritual provisions.  The meaning of the psalmist is, that he shall be admitted, as a member of God's spiritual family, to dwell in his presence, and be filled with joy from the light of his countenance.  Of this, communion with God in his earthly sanctuary is an earnest and a pledge.

title: Psalms 36:9
text:
The fountain; God is the author of life, and all its blessings flow from him. 
 
  In thy light shall we see light; God is the uncreated source of light; when he shines upon the souls of his people, they see light. Light is here put for salvation in the widest sense.

title: Psalms 36:10
text: Know thee; in such a manner as to trust in and obey thee.

title: Psalms 37:1
text:
This psalm is throughout an expansion of the original promise of God to his covenant people, that, so long as they obeyed him, he would give them quiet possession and enjoyment of the promised land.  Leviticus 26:3-13 Deuteronomy 28:1-14   But the earthly inheritance of Canaan foreshadowed a far higher and more spiritual inheritance; namely, the possession of God himself as the soul's everlasting portion.  They who have God for their inheritance, inherit with him the earth and all things in it, in the sense that with him the earth and all things in it, in the sense that he will make all things work together for their present and everlasting welfare.   Romans 8:28 I Corinthians 3:21-23 Revelation of John 21:7  In this high spiritual sense our Lord has interpreted  Psalms 37:11 . See  Matthew 5:5 . 
 
  Because of evil-doers--workers of iniquity; because they prosper in their sinful ways,  Psalms 37:7 . 
 
Uneasiness at the prosperity of others is rebellion against the providence of God, and a source of sin and misery to him who indulges it.

title: Psalms 37:3
text:
Dwell in the land; be supplied with all needed good. 
 
  Verily thou shalt be fed; or, thou shalt feed on truth; that is, God's truth and faithfulness shall be thy support.

title: Psalms 37:4
text: Delight in the character, will, and ways of God is a means of increasing excellence, usefulness, and enjoyment.

title: Psalms 37:5
text: He shall bring it to pass; accomplish, in the best way, the most desirable ends for thy welfare.

title: Psalms 37:6
text: Bring forth thy righteousness--thy judgment; shall vindicate thy character, and deliver thee from the oppression of the wicked, in the most open and public way.

title: Psalms 37:9
text: Wait upon the Lord; in humble dependence on him, and diligent use of the means of his appointment.   Psalms 37:34

title: Psalms 37:10
text: The prosperity of the wicked, however great, is of short continuance, and will soon come to a perpetual end.

title: Psalms 37:13
text: His day; the sinner's day of ruin.

title: Psalms 37:15
text: Enter into their own heart; their efforts to destroy others shall ruin themselves.

title: Psalms 37:16
text: The blessing of God as a portion is more valuable than the possession of all earthly good, and it will continue for ever.

title: Psalms 37:20
text: As the fat of lambs; which is burned upon the altar and goes up in smoke.  Others render, "As the glory of the pastures;" that is, as the grass, which withers and crumbles to dust under the summer's heat.

title: Psalms 37:21
text: The wicked borroweth--showeth mercy, and giveth; to the righteous, who has the disposition to do good, God gives the means; from the wicked, who wants the disposition, he takes away the means also.

title: Psalms 37:22
text: Him; God.

title: Psalms 37:25
text: Devotion to God is the best way to secure not only one's own good, but the good of his children and of his most distant posterity.

title: Psalms 37:26
text: Merciful, and lendeth; see note to  Psalms 37:21 .

title: Psalms 37:27
text: Dwell for evermore; in God's presence and under his protection.

title: Psalms 37:31
text: None of his steps shall slide; he shall not fall into sin, and therefore not into calamity.

title: Psalms 37:34
text: Perseverance in the path of duty will in due time be honored, and meet with an abundant reward.

title: Psalms 37:35
text: A green bay-tree; rather, a tree growing in its native soil, and therefore vigorous and strong.

title: Psalms 37:40
text: Trust in God through Christ is the grand means of peace and safety, and will secure eternal life.

title: Psalms 38:1
text: Title, to bring to remembrance; to bring himself to remembrance before God by recounting to Him his sorrows, and pleading before Him His promises.  David wrote this psalm under a great pressure of suffering, arising from the persecution of his enemies and the desertion of his friends.  To this, in the opinion of some, was added a distressing disease; but others understand  Psalms 38:3 Psalms 38:5 Psalms 38:7 Psalms 38:11 , as a figurative description of the calamities brought upon him by the persecution of his enemies.

title: Psalms 38:2
text: Thine arrows; the afflictions which God sent upon him.

title: Psalms 38:3
text: The righteous view their sins as the cause of all their calamities, and however great their distresses, they feel that they suffer less than their iniquities deserve.

title: Psalms 38:5
text: My wounds; those made by the arrows of the Almighty,  Psalms 38:2 .

title: Psalms 38:9
text: God is perfectly acquainted with all the afflictions of his people, and lays no more upon them than he will enable them by his grace to bear and will overrule for their sanctification and salvation.

title: Psalms 38:11
text: Sore; more literally, stroke, the suffering which God had inflicted on him.  While his enemies took advantage of his distresses, his friends kept at a distance from him.

title: Psalms 38:13
text:
Heard not; he was silent, as though he heard not.  A description of meekness and patience. 
 
Silent and hearty submission to the will of God as manifested in his providence honors him, and prepares the way for deliverance from all evil and the enjoyment of great and everlasting good.  The Lord Jesus Christ, who was brought as a lamb to the slaughter, opened not his mouth.

title: Psalms 38:16
text: Slippeth; falls into calamity.  So also the words "to halt," in the following verse.

title: Psalms 38:18
text:
Declare mine iniquity; confess it. 
 
Penitence for sin, ingenuous confession of it, and hearty application to the blood of Christ for pardon, are essential to forgiveness with God, and to the experience of his salvation.

title: Psalms 39:1
text:
Keep my mouth; be silent. 
 
  While the wicked is before me; under the pressure of present suffering, the psalmist was greatly tempted to impatient complaints respecting God's dealings with him.  See  Psalms 39:9-11 .  To guard against these, he resolved to impose upon himself entire silence in the presence of the wicked. 
 
Those who continue to wait upon God by humble prayer and supplication, and in the diligent use of all the appointed means of grace, will find in the end that the Lord hears and answers, and does exceeding abundantly for them according to all their wants.

title: Psalms 39:2
text:
Even from good; from the fear of saying something wrong, he refrained from uttering any thing, even that which was right, and might have been profitable. 
 
Great circumspection in conversation, especially in the presence of the wicked, is a duty; but neither fear nor favor should hinder us from speaking that which is good, or making known our wants and offering our requests in prayer and supplication to God.

title: Psalms 39:3
text:
While I was musing; in silence.  The suppression of his feelings within his own bosom only made him more vehement, till he could no longer refrain, but spoke to God as in the following verses. 
 
The blessings which God bestows upon his people in answer to prayer, encourage many to pray and to put their trust in him.

title: Psalms 39:6
text:
They; who seek this world as their chief good. 
 
Those who seek the world as their chief good, find that it leaves them when they most need support; while it may be the ruin of those who come after them.

title: Psalms 39:9
text: Thou didst it; his afflictions were sent by God.

title: Psalms 39:11
text: Like a moth; as a moth destroys a garment, so health and beauty are consumed by the afflicting hand of God.

title: Psalms 39:12
text:
A stranger--a sojourner; one on a pilgrimage; passing quickly through this to the eternal world. 
 
As the continuance of man upon the earth is like a vapor which appeareth for a little time and then vanisheth away, his treasure should be laid up in heaven and his affections should be there; then, when absent from the body he will be present with the Lord, and the God whom he has served will be his inheritance and his portion for ever.

title: Psalms 40:1
text: This psalm has its fulfilment in the sufferings and deliverances of all God's people; but more especially of those who are set over them, as was David, and thus act in their behalf.  And since God has made our Lord Jesus Christ "head over all things to the church, which is his body," it is fulfilled in him in the highest sense, and is accordingly applied to him in the New Testament.

title: Psalms 40:2
text: Horrible pit--miry clay; great difficulties and distresses.

title: Psalms 40:3
text:
A new song; for new deliverance. 
 
  See it; his deliverance and subsequent blessings.

title: Psalms 40:6
text:
Sacrifice and offering; such external services as the law prescribed. 
 
  Mine ears hast thou opened; to hearken to and obey the Father's will.  See  Exodus 21:6 Hebrews 10:5 .

title: Psalms 40:7
text: Lo, I come; that is, to do thy will.  These words apply in their highest sense to the Saviour.

title: Psalms 40:8
text: External service is nothing in the sight of God, without obedience of heart to his revealed will.

title: Psalms 40:9
text: Preached righteousness; declared divine truth to the people.

title: Psalms 40:12
text:
Mine iniquities have taken hold upon me; these words apply, in their proper sense, only to the chastisements which God inflicts upon his people for their sins.  In the Lord Jesus they are fulfilled only in the sense that God laid upon him the iniquities of us all, so that, though guiltless, he suffered for us. 
 
The number and aggravations of our sins are such as would for ever shut us out from the favor of God, and prevent our ever seeking him, were it not for his mercy and grace in Christ Jesus.

title: Psalms 40:17
text: The kind thoughts of God towards the poor and needy keep them from sinking into despair, lead them to hope for deliverance, and prepare them to magnify the riches of his grace in their salvation.

title: Psalms 41:1
text:
This psalm is best explained upon the supposition that David wrote it when he was lying upon a bed of sickness,  Psalms 41:8 .  This encouraged his enemies to form mischievous plots against him,  Psalms 41:7 ; though at the same time they paid him hypocritical visits of pretended friendship,  Psalms 41:6 . 
 
  Considereth: has compassion upon the poor, and assists them. David's own condition of distress and weakness seems to have been the occasion of this reflection. 
 
Compassion to the poor and needy, and readiness to assist them for the Lord's sake and in imitation of his example, is an evidence of love to him and preparation for the reception of his mercies.

title: Psalms 41:3
text: Make all his bed; comfort and support him.

title: Psalms 41:4
text: The pardon of sin and deliverance from its guilt and power are more to be desired than deliverance from temporal suffering, or the possession of all earthly good.

title: Psalms 41:9
text:
Mine own familiar friend; these words apply to the conduct of Ahithophel towards David, but had their most perfect fulfilment in the treachery of Judas, and were applied to him by the Saviour himself.  John 13:18  
 
Confidence in creatures may be sadly disappointed; but trust in the Lord, and expectation of good from him in the keeping of his commands, will be fully realized and meet an abundant reward.

title: Psalms 41:10
text: May requite them; in these words David, and in David Christ, speaks as the head and representative of God's church.  It is no private revenge which he desires, but the deliverance of God's people from their malicious foes, who in seeking his destruction seek theirs also.

title: Psalms 41:11
text: God's faithfulness to his covenant people makes the destruction of their incorrigible enemies necessary and certain.  Though they may triumph for a season, he will manifest his everlasting lovingkindness towards his church in their final overthrow.

title: Psalms 41:12
text: Settest me before thy face; makest me blessed in thy presence.

title: Psalms 41:13
text: Amen, and Amen; this doxology marks the conclusion of the first of the five books, or rolls, into which the Psalms have been from ancient times divided.

title: Psalms 42:1
text:
Hart; deer. 
 
Piety will lead those who have it to desire the presence and favor of God more than all earthly good.

title: Psalms 42:2
text:
Appear before God; in the place of his worship; from which the psalmist was manifestly exiled when he wrote this and the following psalm. 
 
A characteristic of true religion is strong attachment to the public worship of God.  The who undervalue and neglect the sanctuary, are unlike the believers described in God's word.

title: Psalms 42:3
text: They; his unbelieving enemies.

title: Psalms 42:5
text:
Help of his countenance; to see the light of God's countenance is to enjoy his presence and favor; and that is salvation.  Numbers 6:25-26 Psalms 4:6   The psalmist has reference to those manifestations of God's presence which he had enjoyed in the sanctuary.  Psalms 63:2  
 
The scriptural way of finding relief from anxiety of spirit, is to pray, and trust in God's promises.

title: Psalms 42:6
text:
Hermonites; the country north-east of Palestine. 
 
  The hill Mizar; a little hill in the land of Hermon.  Even if there, far away from mount Zion, he would still trust in God.

title: Psalms 42:7
text: Thy water-spouts; the troubles with which David was afflicted.

title: Psalms 42:9
text:
Forgotten me; delayed to deliver me. 
 
Though God may long delay to answer the prayers of his people, or appear for their deliverance from trouble, they will not despair, but continue to call upon him, to hope in his mercy, and expect that in due time he will grant them complete and enduring relief.

title: Psalms 42:10
text: A sword in my bones; expressive of intense distress.

title: Psalms 42:11
text: The health of my countenance; his deliverer, and restorer to health, prosperity, gladness, and joy.

title: Psalms 43:1
text:
This short psalm is entirely in the strain of  Psalms 42:1-11 , and seems to form a sort of supplement to it. 
 
The piety or usefulness of any one, however great, will not in this world save him from trouble.

title: Psalms 43:3
text:
The holy hill; Zion. 
 
  Thy tabernacles; the tabernacle which David pitched on Zion when he transferred the ark to that place.  The plural "tabernacles" is elsewhere used, perhaps with reference to its various divisions into the court, the holy place, and the holy of holies.   Psalms 84:1  
 
The greatest desire of a pious man is to be led in the path of truth and duty, and to enjoy the ordinances and favor of God.  In these he rejoices more than in all earthly good.

title: Psalms 43:5
text: In his greatest distresses the good man still trusts in God, and is supported by the hope that he shall in due time be delivered from all trouble, and prepared to praise and enjoy Him for ever.

title: Psalms 44:1
text:
This psalm is eminently national in its character, having been written in behalf of the suffering covenant people at a time when their enemies were triumphant over them. 
 
The history of God's dealings with his people is full of instruction, and a knowledge of it should be communicated from parents to their children.

title: Psalms 44:3
text:
The land; the land of Canaan. 
 
The mercies which men enjoy come not through their own power and goodness, but through the power and goodness of God.

title: Psalms 44:4
text: Jacob; the children of Israel.

title: Psalms 44:5
text: Through thy name; through thy perfections.  The name of God expresses the sum of his revealed attributes.

title: Psalms 44:8
text: Boast; acknowledge thee as our only deliverer, and glory not in our strength, but in thine alone.

title: Psalms 44:9
text: In the discipline of his people, God sometimes forsakes them "for a small moment."   Isaiah 54:8-9   Then their enemies triumph over them. But no evil can come upon them except by his permission, and for the purpose of purifying them from sin.  By this discipline he prepares his visible earthly church for greater enlargement and strength in this world, and the true spiritual members of it for glory everlasting.

title: Psalms 44:10
