text: Spoil for themselves; for their own pleasure and aggrandizement.

title: Psalms 44:14
text: Byword--shaking of the head; a subject of contempt.

title: Psalms 44:17
text:
Not forgotten thee; not apostatized from God. 
 
Whatever evils may come on the true people of God, they will not forsake his service.

title: Psalms 44:19
text:
Place of dragons; desolate place where wild animals dwell.  The word here rendered "dragons" does not mean sea-monsters, which the Hebrew expresses by a different word. 
 
  Shadow of death; great and dreadful darkness.

title: Psalms 44:21
text: All things are naked and open to the all seeing eye of God, and the great concern of his people is to approve themselves to him; in their deepest troubles they feel that their help must come from him.

title: Psalms 44:22
text: Killed all the day long; continually exposed to murderous persecution.  These words, in which the ancient church expressed her bitter experience, are applied by the apostle Paul to the sufferings of Christians under the new dispensation.

title: Psalms 44:23
text: Why sleepest thou; God is represented as sleeping when he allows the enemies of his people to prevail against them.

title: Psalms 44:24
text: Forgettest our affliction; delayest to remove it.

title: Psalms 45:1
text:
The theme of this psalm is Jesus Christ the King of kings, and the espousal of his church to him.  In the Old Testament, God is often represented as the husband of Zion, that is, of his church.  Isaiah 54:4-6 Isaiah 62:4-5 .  In like manner the New Testament church is called "the bride, the Lamb's wife," and she is "arrayed in fine linen, clean and white," for the day of her marriage.  Ephesians 5:23 Revelation of John 19:7-8 Revelation of John 21:9   The espousal of the Saviour to his church is here represented under imagery borrowed from the marriage customs of eastern nations. 
 
  Inditing; meditating in preparation to speak. 
 
  The king; Jesus Christ. 
 
  The pen of a ready writer; the fulness of his feelings makes his tongue fervent and rapid in its utterance, like the pen of a ready writer. 
 
The thoughts of true believers are very much occupied about Christ and his cause.

title: Psalms 45:2
text: Grace is poured into thy lips; he received the Holy Spirit without measure.

title: Psalms 45:3
text: Since God has given to Christ all power in heaven and in earth, and made him "most mighty" in behalf of the church, they who love the prosperity of his kingdom shall see their utmost desires fulfilled.

title: Psalms 45:5
text: The king's enemies; the enemies of Christ.  Compare  Isaiah 11:4 Revelation of John 19:21 .

title: Psalms 45:6
text:
O God; this is applied by the Holy Spirit to Jesus Christ.  Hebrews 1:8-9  
 
Jesus Christ is God over all; he is so addressed by the Father, and his works prove him to be divine.

title: Psalms 45:8
text: Myrrh, and aloes, and cassia; put for sweet odors generally.  The aloes here spoken of are the lign-aloes, mentioned  Numbers 24:6 Proverbs 7:17 Song of Solomon 4:14 .  It is a species of fragrant wood.

title: Psalms 45:9
text: Gold Ophir; Ophir is here mentioned as emphatically the gold-land of the ancient Hebrews.  For its situation see note to  I Kings 9:28 .

title: Psalms 45:10
text:
Forget--thine own people; be wholly devoted to Jesus Christ, and love him more than father, mother, or any earthly friend. 
 
Those who would partake of Christ's salvation must love him supremely, and be ready, when called, to forsake all for his sake.

title: Psalms 45:11
text: Thy beauty; the holiness and spiritual beauty of his church.

title: Psalms 45:12
text: The daughter of Tyre; that is, Tyre herself, represented as a princely female.  The Tyrians were celebrated for their extensive commerce and great wealth.  The general idea is, that the rich and mighty should contribute their offerings to Christ and his bride the church.

title: Psalms 45:13
text:
The king's daughter; Christ's redeemed and sanctified church. 
 
  Within; within the king's palace.  Her glorious apparel represents her spiritual beauty. 
 
Divine grace changes the heart and makes it meet to be a habitation for God through his Spirit.

title: Psalms 45:16
text:
Thy children; the children of the King: the church of Christ is here, as elsewhere, represented as the mother of a numerous and honorable offspring. 
 
Death is continually removing the fathers from Christ's church; but the number and strength of Christ's spiritual offspring on earth shall be increased, till they shall inherit the world.  In that happy day the righteous shall be "princes in all the earth."

title: Psalms 46:1
text:
The occasion of the present psalm seems to have been some remarkable triumph of God's people over their enemies; perhaps their deliverance from the Assyrian army in the days of Hezekiah.   II Kings 19:35 Isaiah 37:36  In it the church rises above all human trust to simple faith in God's almighty power and unchangeable love.   Psalms 47:1-48:14  are two psalms in the same general strain. 
 
  A very present help; found by experience to be ever ready and all-powerful to help his people. 
 
Those who have God for their defender need fear no evil.

title: Psalms 46:2
text: Though the earth be removed; the figures employed in this and the following verse denote violent commotions and changes of every kind, physical and political.

title: Psalms 46:4
text:
A river; the river of the water of life proceeding from God's throne.   Ezekiel 47:1 Revelation of John 22:1   This is the symbol of his life-giving presence and power. 
 
  The city of God; Jerusalem, the place of God's special presence under the Mosaic economy.  This city of God is now his true church.

title: Psalms 46:5
text:
Right early; in due season; when help is most needed. 
 
The presence and favor of God are at all times the security, support, and comfort of his people.

title: Psalms 46:6
text: The earth melted; showing its dependence on God, and that all things are entirely under his control.

title: Psalms 46:9
text:
He maketh wars to cease; by the destruction of the hostile forces. This is the final issue of all assaults upon his people; and while the conflict rages, he governs in the midst of it, and overrules it for his glory and their good. 
 
In the midst of wars and tumults, it is a consolation to God's people to know that the issues of them are in his hand, and that he will in the end make them subservient to their peace and prosperity.

title: Psalms 46:10
text:
Be still; desist from your vain assaults upon my people. 
 
One great design of God in all his dispensations is to manifest his true character, and make himself known to all people as the one only living and true Jehovah.

title: Psalms 46:11
text: Us; the people of God.

title: Psalms 47:1
text:
All ye people; that is, as the original word means, all ye nations. Here, as often elsewhere in the Psalms, the gentile nations are called upon to rejoice in God, in anticipation of their reception, through faith, into the church. 
 
God is the joy of his people.  In him they glory as their righteousness, wisdom, and strength.

title: Psalms 47:3
text: Under us; under his covenant people.  The victories of ancient Israel over the surrounding heathen nations foreshadowed the spiritual subjection of the nations to the church through faith in Christ.

title: Psalms 47:4
text:
Our inheritance--the excellency of Jacob; designations of the goodly heritage which God conferred upon his ancient people. 
 
The condition of each individual is chosen for him by God, and with it he should be content, and thus by his conduct say, Not my will, but thine be done.

title: Psalms 47:5
text:
God is gone up; from the conquest of his enemies to heaven. 
 
  A shout--the sound of a trumpet; the signs of rejoicing.

title: Psalms 47:6
text: Those who from the heart offer praises to God, glorify him.  In this, the high and the low, the rich and the poor, persons of all descriptions may unite, and thus secure his approbation and blessing.

title: Psalms 47:7
text: All the earth; God is not a local deity, but a universal monarch.

title: Psalms 47:8
text:
God reigneth over the heathen; they will one day all be brought to acknowledge and adore him as their King. 
 
The prophets of the Old Testament foresaw and predicted the day when all heathen nations shall be brought to acknowledge and glorify God, and he shall be greatly exalted throughout the whole earth.

title: Psalms 47:9
text:
Gathered together; to worship God and acknowledge him as their Lord.  These are the princes of the heathen mentioned in the preceding verse. 
 
  The people of the God of Abraham; who had become such by their submission to him. 
 
  The shields of the earth; the same as the "princes of the people,"  Hosea 4:8 .

title: Psalms 48:1
text: The city of our God; Jerusalem.

title: Psalms 48:2
text:
The joy of the whole earth; as the seat of the true worship of Jehovah, which was appointed to extend itself over the whole earth.  Isaiah 2:2-4  
 
  Mount Zion, on the sides of the north; "the sides of the north" seem to include not only the northern slope of the hill of Zion, but also Moriah, which lay to the north-east, and upon which the temple was built. 
 
The true spiritual Zion is the light and glory of the whole earth.  God administers the government of the world for her good, and he will make her a blessing to all nations.

title: Psalms 48:5
text:
They were troubled, and hasted away; the enemies of Jerusalem that had come up against it, were scattered and dispersed. 
 
The enemies of God, in their assaults upon his people, bring ruin upon themselves.  God is with those who love him, and they must prevail.

title: Psalms 48:7
text:
Thou breakest the ships of Tarshish; a particular instance of God's power, to represent his universal sovereignty. 
 
  With an east wind; compare  Acts 27:14 .

title: Psalms 48:8
text: As we have heard, so have we seen; the wonderful doings of God in past ages of which we have heard, have been repeated before our eyes.

title: Psalms 48:10
text: So is thy praise; or, so be thy praise.  The name of God is the sum of his perfections, as manifested to men.  With this the praises rendered to him by men ought to correspond.

title: Psalms 48:11
text: Thy judgments; the retributions of God, especially with reference to his enemies.

title: Psalms 48:12
text: Tell the towers thereof; count the towers of Jerusalem, that ye may see her impregnable strength.

title: Psalms 48:13
text: It is the privilege and duty of God's people, in each successive generation, to record his glorious interpositions in their behalf, for the comfort and encouragement of those who come after them.

title: Psalms 48:14
text: God will never forsake those who trust in him, but will guide them by his counsel, and afterwards receive them to glory.

title: Psalms 49:1
text:
The theme of this psalm is the vanity of all earthly honors and possessions, in contrast with the righteous man's portion, which is everlasting life, honor, and blessedness in God's presence. 
 
That wisdom which is from above, and that understanding which consists in the fear of the Lord, are equally essential to all classes of people.

title: Psalms 49:3
text: Wisdom; that course which it is proper for frail man to pursue.

title: Psalms 49:4
text:
Incline mine ear; in the attitude of earnest attention, as I sing my song with the accompaniment of the harp.  The psalmist receives from God the instructions which he communicates to others, and he, as well as his hearers, must reverently attend to them. 
 
  A parable--dark saying; here used of instruction communicated in a figurative and sententious style.

title: Psalms 49:5
text:
The iniquity of my heels; his past offences; but some render the words, the iniquity of my oppressors, who followed him with their persecutions. 
 
They that fear God and trust him for what they need, have no reason to fear any one else.

title: Psalms 49:7
text: Redeem his brother; save him from the grave.

title: Psalms 49:8
text:
Redemption of their soul; preservation of their life. 
 
  Precious; it exceeds all price which men can pay for it.  This is true alike of the redemption of the natural life and of the immortal spirit. 
 
No earthly treasures, however costly and abundant, can save the possessor or his friends from the stroke of death.

title: Psalms 49:12
text: Abideth not; he must soon die.

title: Psalms 49:13
text:
Approve their sayings; imitate their example. 
 
Multitudes imitate the folly and wickedness of those who have gone before them, in living for earth, and not for heaven.

title: Psalms 49:14
text: The morning; soon, in the morning of the resurrection.

title: Psalms 49:15
text: God will redeem my soul from the power of the grave; he will preserve the lives of his saints from the dangers of every kind until their appointed time comes; and will finally raise them from the dead, and receive them, soul and body, to himself.

title: Psalms 49:16
text: No one should be fearful or envious at the prosperity and wealth of others, for they will soon die, and go hence as destitute as if they had lived in poverty.

title: Psalms 49:18
text: Those who live only to gratify their appetites and passions, sink themselves in infamy; men may applaud, but God will condemn them.

title: Psalms 49:19
text: They shall never see light; the wicked have all their good things in this life.

title: Psalms 49:20
text: Understandeth not; understandeth not his duty as a rational being, mortal and yet immortal.

title: Psalms 50:1
text: In this psalm God is represented as coming forth in majesty and glory from his dwelling place in mount Zion, and summoning his covenant people to judgment for their hypocrisy and wickedness.

title: Psalms 50:2
text: The perfection of beauty; Zion, as the royal abode of Jehovah, was to the pious Israelite the sum of all excellence and beauty.  Psalms 48:2

title: Psalms 50:3
text:
Shall come; from Zion to judge his people. 
 
A day is coming when all shall discern between him that serveth God in truth, and him that serveth him not.

title: Psalms 50:4
text: Call to the heavens--to the earth; to heaven and earth with all their inhabitants, to be present as witnesses.

title: Psalms 50:5
text:
My saints; my visible, professed worshippers.  Israel, as the peculiar people of God, and consecrated to his service, is called "a holy nation,"  Exodus 19:6 . 
 
  By sacrifice; the national covenant with Israel was originally ratified by sacrifices and the sprinkling of blood,  Exodus 24:5-8 ; and the stated sacrifices appointed under the law, may be regarded as a perpetual renewing of this covenant.

title: Psalms 50:6
text: His righteousness; the correctness of his decisions.

title: Psalms 50:8
text: External service merely, without the heart being engaged, will be of no avail in the sight of God.

title: Psalms 50:9
text: I will take no bullock; God does not require sacrifices, or any other services which men can render, for his own sake, "as though he needed any thing," nor will he accept them unless offered in faith and love.   Acts 17:25

title: Psalms 50:14
text: Thanksgiving; a spiritual service: not that thanksgiving should be substituted for sacrifice, but that these should be an expression of thanksgiving.

title: Psalms 50:15
text: Humble, believing, affectionate prayer will always be heard, and in God's own way and time be abundantly answered.

title: Psalms 50:16
text:
The wicked; the open violators of God's law. 
 
God will not accept any service at the hand of the habitual violators of his law.

title: Psalms 50:21
text: Such a one as thyself; one who would connive at wickedness, and suffer it to go unpunished.

title: Psalms 50:22
text:
Tear you in pieces; suddenly and utterly destroy you. 
 
God often waits upon sinners with much long-suffering, but will finally call them to account, and punish them according to their deserts.

title: Psalms 50:23
text:
Offereth praise; offers sacrifices of thanksgiving. See  Psalms 50:14 . 
 
Without an upright life, all professions of godliness, and all claims to true religion and salvation are vain.   Matthew 7:15-23 James 1:26 I John 3:7

title: Psalms 51:1
text:
My transgressions; especially his sins in the matter of Uriah, with which he was charged by the prophet Nathan, and of which he was now deeply sensible. 
 
All the hope of the true penitent is in the free mercy and rich grace of God, and these form his only plea before him.

title: Psalms 51:4
text:
Against thee, thee only; his sin was principally, or especially against God, and most aggravated in his sight. 
 
  Be justified--and be clear when thou judgest; clear from all wrong in condemning him. 
 
However greatly any one injures his fellow men by his sins, their chief guilt is in being committed against God.

title: Psalms 51:6
text: Truth in the inward parts; purity, sincerity, and uprightness of soul.

title: Psalms 51:7
text:
Hyssop; a plant or shrub used in external cleansing, and emblem of internal purity. 
 
Purification from sin is the work of the Holy Spirit, and to him the believer looks for this inestimable blessing.

title: Psalms 51:8
text: The bones which thou hast broken; that the distresses brought upon him might be removed.

title: Psalms 51:11
text: Without the constant aid of the Holy Spirit, even the most eminent believers will be in constant danger of falling into the most aggravated sins.

title: Psalms 51:12
text:
The joy of thy salvation; which he had lost by his sins. 
 
  Uphold me; without this he would again fall into sin.

title: Psalms 51:13
text: It is only when we have the joy of God's salvation in our own hearts, that we are qualified to guide sinners to repentance.  The believer desires God's presence and the light of his countenance, not for his own sake alone, but for the sake of his fellow men.

title: Psalms 51:14
text: Bloodguiltiness; in procuring the death of Uriah.

title: Psalms 51:15
text: For a heart to praise God men are dependent on him, and they should continually look up to him for this inestimable blessing.

title: Psalms 51:17
text: The sacrifices of God; the offerings which are pleasing to him and which he will accept.

title: Psalms 51:18
text:
Zion; the church of God. 
 
The sincere penitent desires spiritual blessings not only for himself but for others, especially for the people of God in every part of the world.

title: Psalms 51:19
text: Sacrifices of righteousness; such as God requires.

title: Psalms 52:1
text:
Title, when Doeg the Edomite came; see the narrative in  I Samuel 21:1-7 I Samuel 22:9-23 . 
 
  Mighty man; Doeg the Edomite. 
 
  Endureth continually; as much as to say, It will protect me from thy mischievous designs. 
 
To boast in iniquity is the way to perdition.

title: Psalms 52:2
text: Like a sharp razor; wounding deep and suddenly.

title: Psalms 52:4
text: Devouring words; words that injure and destroy.  They occasioned the death of all Ahimelech's house, with the exception of Abiathar.

title: Psalms 52:5
text: Slander and calumny are exceedingly heinous in God's sight.  he will sooner or later destroy all who practise them; and will permit his servants to rejoice in his righteous judgments.

title: Psalms 52:6
text:
Fear; fear to sin. 
 
  Laugh at him; rejoice at his ruin.

title: Psalms 52:7
text: Ungodly men who trust in their power and wealth, will have speedy and sore disappointment.

title: Psalms 52:8
text:
Like a green olive-tree; prosperous and flourishing. 
 
The righteous, who put their trust in God, will never be disappointed; they shall be like trees planted by the waters, ever green and fruitful.

title: Psalms 52:9
text: I will wait on thy name; adore God for the manifestations of his character, and expect from him all needed good.

title: Psalms 53:1
text:
This psalm is, for substance, the same as  Psalms 14:1-7 . 
 
Those who say, There is no God, even in their hearts, are dupes of their own wickedness and folly.

title: Psalms 53:2
text: None naturally seek after God, nor will any ever do it without the influences of his grace.

title: Psalms 53:5
text:
Where no fear was; no external cause of fear. 
 
God can fill the wicked with trembling and consternation in the absence of all external appearances of danger; and in the end, more and greater evils than they feared will come upon them.

title: Psalms 53:6
text:
Bringeth back the captivity of his people; delivers them from trouble, and bestows upon them prosperity. 
 
Let the righteous wait patiently upon God, and their highest expectations will be more than realized.

title: Psalms 54:1
text:
Title, when the Ziphim came; the Ziphim are the same as the Ziphites,  I Samuel 23:19 . 
 
  By thy name; by thy glorious perfections; for these, as manifested to men, constitute God's name.

title: Psalms 54:2
text: Prayer is the refuge of God's people.  In every time of trouble they look to him, and find him to be a very present and all sufficient helper.

title: Psalms 54:3
text: Strangers; the Ziphites, as having the spirit of strangers, that is, foreign enemies; unless the reference be to foreigners in the service of Saul, such as Doeg the Edomite, who were among the foremost in persecuting David.

title: Psalms 54:4
text: Them that uphold my soul; those in Israel who adhered to the cause of David.

title: Psalms 54:5
text: The enemies of God are destined to destruction, while his people will behold and acquiesce in his judgments.

title: Psalms 55:1
text: This psalm probably refers to the rebellion of Absalom.

title: Psalms 55:3
text: Cast iniquity upon me; overwhelm me with their wickedness.

title: Psalms 55:4
text: A conviction of sin as the cause of all our trouble fills the soul with anguish which is more distressing than any external trials.

title: Psalms 55:5
text:
Horror hath overwhelmed me; his horror was in view of the plans devised by enemies for his destruction; but it was aggravated by the consciousness of his own sinfulness. 
 
It is the lot of those whom God appoints to eminent stations in his church to endure great suffering in her behalf, both from inward conflicts and outward opposition.

title: Psalms 55:8
text: Windy storm and tempest; the trouble which surrounded him.

title: Psalms 55:9
text:
Divide their tongues; distract their counsels.  This was strikingly fulfilled in the case of Ahithophel's counsel. 
 
  The city; Jerusalem. 
 
The hearts of the wicked, as well as the righteous, are in the hands of God, and he can at any time divide their counsels and bring their projects to naught.

title: Psalms 55:10
text: They go about it upon the walls; violence and strife are, as it were, the watchmen of the city night and day.

title: Psalms 55:12
text:
An enemy; that is, open and avowed. 
 
  Then I would have hid myself from him; guarded myself against his assaults. 
 
The defection of former friends is harder to bear than the opposition of those who have been open enemies.

title: Psalms 55:13
text:
Thou, a man mine equal; Ahithophel. 
 
  My guide; or, my friend, as the original word is elsewhere rendered.   Proverbs 16:28 Proverbs 17:9

title: Psalms 55:14
text: In company; with the festive throng.

title: Psalms 55:15
text: Go down quick into hell; go down alive into the place of the dead, like Korah and his company.   Numbers 16:33

title: Psalms 55:17
text: Regularity and constancy in prayer are essential to peace of conscience, and that joy in the Holy Ghost which is a safeguard and support in trouble.

title: Psalms 55:20
text: He; the wicked man spoken of,  Psalms 55:13 .

title: Psalms 55:22
text:
Cast thy burden upon the Lord; depend entirely on him for all needed good. 
 
Dependence on God will keep the soul in peace: when the wicked are cut off, the righteous will stand unmoved.

title: Psalms 55:23
text: Half their days; half the natural term of life: a prophecy of the premature death of David's enemies.

title: Psalms 56:1
text:
Title, Jonath-elam-rechokim; "the dumb dove of distant ones," most probably an enigmatical designation of David, as an innocent, defenceless man, in the hands of distant ones, that is foreigners. 
 
The only hope for man in trouble is in the mercy of God; to this his people look, and on it they depend for all they need.

title: Psalms 56:3
text: Trust in God is the grand support in adversity, and is one of the things which distinguish the righteous from the wicked.

title: Psalms 56:4
text:
In God; by God's mercy and gracious assistance. 
 
  His word; his word of promise, as fulfilled to me in my preservation in the midst of enemies.

title: Psalms 56:5
text: Wrest; pervert.

title: Psalms 56:8
text:
Tellest; numberest. 
 
  Into thy bottle--in thy book; the meaning is, Carefully treasure them up in thy memory. 
 
The various removals of the people of God are all ordered by him, and he never forgets their sufferings for his sake, but will give a gracious and an abundant reward.

title: Psalms 56:11
text: Confidence in God is a safeguard against the fear of man.

title: Psalms 56:12
text: Thy vows are upon me; the psalmist here anticipates his approaching deliverance, and promises to render to God the thank-offerings which he has vowed.

title: Psalms 57:1
text: The mercy of God forms the never-failing plea of his people; to him as a refuge they apply in every season of calamity, and patiently wait for his salvation.

title: Psalms 57:4
text:
Lions; fierce and cruel men who sought to destroy him. 
 
  Set on fire; inflamed by their passions, and inflaming others. 
 
  Spears and arrows; instruments of destruction. 
 
However numerous the enemies, and however great the danger of God's people, he will protect them, and at length deliver them from all their troubles.

title: Psalms 57:5
text: Be thou exalted, O God; for the deliverance vouchsafed to me; which the psalmist here anticipates.

title: Psalms 57:6
text: The efforts of the wicked to destroy the righteous often prove the means of their own ruin.

title: Psalms 57:7
text: Fixed; settled on the foundation of the everlasting covenant; determined, in the strength and by the grace of God, to trust in and praise him.

title: Psalms 57:8
text: My glory; the same as, my soul, see note to  Psalms 16:9 .

title: Psalms 57:9
text: The godly not only praise God themselves, but desire that he may be praised by all people throughout the earth.

title: Psalms 57:10
text: Great unto the heavens; immeasurably great.

title: Psalms 58:1
text:
Do ye judge uprightly; the reference is to the decisions of wicked rulers who were the enemies and persecutors of David. 
 
No iniquity is more hateful than that which is practised under the cover of law.

title: Psalms 58:2
text: Ye weigh the violence of your hands; dispense violence instead of justice.

title: Psalms 58:3
text:
As soon as they be born; at the commencement of their course of moral action, they naturally depart from God.   Genesis 8:21  
 
Men are from the beginning of their moral existence prone to evil as the sparks to fly upward, or the waters to run downward.

title: Psalms 58:4
text: Like the deaf adder; as this is insensible to all the words of the charmer, so are they to all attempts to recall them from their wicked ways.

title: Psalms 58:6
text: Break their teeth; disable them from doing mischief.

title: Psalms 58:7
text:
Them; the arrows. 
 
  As cut in pieces; broken, or blunted, so that they can do no execution.

title: Psalms 58:8
text: Which melteth; probably an allusion to the slime secreted from its own body which the snail leaves in its path.

title: Psalms 58:9
text:
Feel the thorns; feel their heat.  Kindling a fire of thorns under their pots is a figure for plotting wicked schemes, which God will carry away as with a tempest, before their accomplishment. 
 
  Shall take them away; shall sweep away the thorns with a tempest, as the original word implies, and thus put an end, so to speak, to the cooking of their mischievous plots. 
 
  Both living, and in his wrath; the literal meaning of the original, seems to be that God's wrath will take away the thorns while yet living, that is, yet green and unburned, before the pots have felt the heat from their flame.  Others prefer to render, Whether raw, or cooked; in other words, whether their schemes are immature, or now complete and ripening to accomplishment. 
 
The destruction of the ungodly will be sudden and complete; they will be taken away in the midst of their wicked plans.

title: Psalms 58:10
text: Wash his feet in the blood of the wicked; in token of triumph.

title: Psalms 59:1
text: Title, when Saul sent; see  I Samuel 19:11 .

title: Psalms 59:3
text:
Not for my transgression; the opposition of the wicked to him was not caused by his sins against them. 
 
However numerous or mighty their enemies, God will protect his people, and eventually deliver them from all harm.

title: Psalms 59:4
text: They run; that is, run upon me as enemies.

title: Psalms 59:5
text: The heathen; the enemies of God and his people.

title: Psalms 59:6
text:
This verse, in the original, is the same as the fourteenth, word for word; and may, like it, be considered as either a prediction or a prayer. 
 
  Return; like hungry dogs that have taken no prey. 
 
  Make a noise; howl from hunger. 
 
  Go round about the city; in search of food.

title: Psalms 59:7
text: The wicked often flatter themselves that no one takes notice of their transgressions, or will call them to account for their sins.  But there is nothing covered that shall not be revealed, neither is there any thing hid, which is not seen, and shall not be made known.

title: Psalms 59:9
text: Because of his strength; because of the strength of my enemy who seeks my life.

title: Psalms 59:10
text: Prevent me; go before me and give me the victory over all my foes.

title: Psalms 59:11
text:
Slay them not; but preserve them in such a way as to be a warning to all others against continuing in sin. 
 
The condition of the wicked in this world is often a standing monument of their transgressions, and of the anger of God against them.

title: Psalms 59:12
text: Taken; as by a net.

title: Psalms 59:13
text:
In Jacob; among his people. 
 
God ruleth in all places throughout the earth, and especially among his chosen people, and will cause all things to work for good to those who love him.

title: Psalms 59:14
text: See  Psalms 59:6 .

title: Psalms 60:1
text:
Title, Aram-naharaim; Syria of the two rivers; that is, Mesopotamia. 
 
  Aram-zobah; that is, Syria Zobah.  This country probably lay northeast of Damascus, on the west side of the Euphrates. 
 
  Returned; from the expedition against Syria. 
 
  Of Edom in the valley of salt; probably the valley at the south end of the Dead sea, which is at the present day bordered on the west by a salt mountain.  For the events referred to in this title, see notes on  I Chronicles 18:12 .  Compare also  II Samuel 8:11-14 . 
 

 
  Thou hast cast us off; the first three verses of the psalm refer to the period before the victories celebrated in the remaining verses. 
 
Trials are the consequences of sin, and should lead us to self-examination, repentance, and hearty turning unto the Lord.

title: Psalms 60:3
text:
Thou hast showed thy people hard things; afflictions, especially reverses in war. 
 
  Drink the wine of astonishment; wine that produces giddiness and reeling; a frequent scriptural metaphor to express the amazement and perplexity produced by God's heavy judgments.   Jeremiah 25:15-16 Jeremiah 25:27  
 
Even the people of God, if they sin against him, are often visited with great and sore troubles, from which nothing but his grace can deliver them.

title: Psalms 60:4
text: A banner; as a signal and pledge of God's presence.  The allusion is to a military standard elevated on the top of a mountain as a rallying point in time of war.  Here God himself furnishes the banner, and thus pledges his presence and help.

title: Psalms 60:6
text: Shechem--Succoth; two places of the land of Israel, the former on the west side of Jordan, the latter on the east.  They stand here as representatives of all the cities of Israel.

title: Psalms 60:7
text:
Gilead--Manasseh--Ephraim; three regions put to represent the whole land which should be subjected to David's power. 
 
  The strength of my head; my helmet, that is, my defence. 
 
  My lawgiver; the seat of my kingdom.   Genesis 49:10  
 
Jehovah is king over all, and the rightful proprietor of all the kingdoms and nations of the earth.

title: Psalms 60:8
text:
My washpot; put to dishonorable service as a conquered people. 
 
  Cast out my shoe; probably in token of possession.

title: Psalms 60:9
text: The strong city; Petra, the capital of Edom.

title: Psalms 60:11
text: God is the only effectual helper in trouble, and to him alone men should look as their deliverer.

title: Psalms 60:12
text: Tread down our enemies; enable us to overcome them.

title: Psalms 61:2
text:
From the end of the earth; this psalm was probably written when David was an exile from the sanctuary.  Separation from God's presence seemed to him like banishment to the ends of the earth. 
 
God is a sure refuge, in all times of trouble, to those who pray to and put their trust in him.

title: Psalms 61:3
text: A strong tower; place and means of defence.

title: Psalms 61:4
text: I will abide in thy tabernacle; or, let me abide in thy tabernacle. to abide in God's tabernacle is to be admitted to commuion with him as a member of his household.  Of this the visible tabernacle service was a sign and a pledge.  See notes to  Psalms 15:1 Psalms 27:4 .

title: Psalms 61:5
text:
The heritage of those that fear thy name; the presence and blessing of God. 
 
God witnesses the engagements and hears the supplications of his people, and none truly seek him in vain.

title: Psalms 61:7
text:
He shall abide before God for ever; probably an allusion to the promise made by God to David through Nathan: "Thy house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee."   II Samuel 7:16  
 
However great or long continued their trials, the people of God are ripening for heaven and preparing to dwell with him for ever.

title: Psalms 61:8
text: My vows; his engagements to serve the Lord.

title: Psalms 62:1
text:
Title, to Jeduthun; or, over Jeduthan; that is, over the company of singers belonging to his family. 
 
To wait upon God by prayer and supplication, submission to his will, and devotion to his service, is the way to experience his salvation.

title: Psalms 62:4
text:
They; the wicked who persecuted David. 
 
  His excellency; his kingly dignity.

title: Psalms 62:5
text: Expectations from men will be disappointed, while expectations from God will be abundantly more than realized.

title: Psalms 62:9
text:
A lie; given to deception, they cannot be trusted in. 
 
  To be laid in the balance; the meaning is, that if they be weighed in the balances of truth, they will be found lighter than vanity.

title: Psalms 62:10
text: Riches, when idolized, become a curse to the possessor.

title: Psalms 62:11
text: That power; to raise up, or cast down.

title: Psalms 63:1
text:
Title, in the wilderness of Judah; this wilderness lay along the eastern border of Judah. 
 
  A dry and thirsty land; at a distance from the tabernacle and ordinances of God.  The meaning of the psalmist is, that separation from the place where God manifests his presence is to his soul what a dry and thirsty wilderness is to the body. 
 
To be deprived of the privileges of the sanctuary is a great calamity, and one which is severely felt by all who love God.

title: Psalms 63:4
text: Lift up my hands; the attitude of prayer.

title: Psalms 63:5
text:
Be satisfied; with communion with thee, as the all-satisfying portion of my soul. 
 
No joys are so elevated, pure, and satisfying as those which spring from the service and enjoyment of God.

title: Psalms 63:9
text: The people of God are his peculiar treasure, and those who seek to destroy them will themselves be destroyed.

title: Psalms 63:10
text: A portion for foxes; the Hebrew includes, under one word, foxes and jackals.  Jackals are numerous in Palestine, and prey on dead bodies. To be a portion for jackals, is to be left unburied on the battle-field as the food of jackals.

title: Psalms 63:11
text:
The king; David. 
 
  Sweareth by him; by the name of God, as a sign of allegiance to him. 
 
  Shall glory; glory in the salvation that God bestows upon him. 
 
Lying tongues shall be put to silence, and none but the lovers of truth and righteousness shall inherit the divine favor.

title: Psalms 64:4
text: Shoot at him; speak violent and bitter words against him.

title: Psalms 64:5
text: The wicked encourage each other in sin, and flatter themselves and one another that their evil deeds will never be brought to light.

title: Psalms 64:6
text: They search out iniquities; devise wicked plans.

title: Psalms 64:8
text:
Their own tongue; their bitter words. 
 
The evils which the wicked seek to bring upon the righteous often fall upon themselves.

title: Psalms 64:9
text: Shall fear; fear the judgments of God.

title: Psalms 64:10
text:
Shall glory; glory or rejoice in God, who has delivered them. 
 
Uprightness of heart is essential to joy in a holy God.

title: Psalms 65:1
text: Title, A Psalm and Song; or, "A Psalm, a Song;" that is, a psalm which is also a song of praise.  This psalm is properly named a song, for it celebrates God's majesty, greatness, and forgiving love; especially his goodness, as manifested in the gift of "rain from heaven and fruitful seasons."

title: Psalms 65:2
text: Shall all flesh come; all flesh is dependent on God for life and breath and all things; and shall come to God in prayer, in the day when all nations shall be enlightened by his word and Spirit.

title: Psalms 65:3
text: Purge them away; forgive their sins and purify their souls through the great atonement.

title: Psalms 65:4
text: No blessedness is so great as that which results from being chosen of God to salvation, through the sanctification of the Spirit, and belief of his truth.

title: Psalms 65:5
text: Terrible things; those which God accomplishes for the destruction of his enemies and the salvation of his people.

title: Psalms 65:7
text: God rules in the kingdoms of nature and of providence, as well as of grace, and controls all things according to the wise and good counsels of his own perfect will.

title: Psalms 65:8
text: Thy tokens; the signs of God's presence and almighty power in nature.

title: Psalms 65:9
text:
The river of God; God's inexhaustible store of waters, from which he sends upon the earth refreshing showers. 
 
All the blessings of this life come from God, and are the fruit of his kindness, mercy, and grace to the children of men.

title: Psalms 65:11
text: Thy paths drop fatness; that is, wherever thou goest thou scatterest fatness around thee.  Fatness stands here, as often elsewhere, for a rich abundance of the best gifts.

title: Psalms 65:12
text: They drop; drop fatness.  But we may render more literally, "the pastures of the wilderness drop," that is, with fatness, in consequence of God's visit to them.

title: Psalms 65:13
text: All the works of God praise him, and his saints bless him for the mercies of this life and of that which is to come.

title: Psalms 66:1
text:
In this psalm the writer takes occasion, from a personal deliverance vouchsafed to him by God--or, as some think, a deliverance granted to God's people, in whose name he speaks--to celebrate the wonderful dealings of God with his covenant people in all past ages. 
 
The friends of God are desirous that all in every land may know, acknowledge, praise, and adore him.

title: Psalms 66:3
text: Submit themselves unto thee; be forced to profess subjection and obedience to thee.

title: Psalms 66:6
text: He turned the sea into dry land; at the time the children of Israel crossed the Red sea.

title: Psalms 66:9
text: The preservation of our bodies and souls is the work of God, and the fruit of his kindness; they should therefore be devoted to his service.

title: Psalms 66:10
text: Proved us; by afflictions.

title: Psalms 66:12
text:
Through fire and through water; fiery trials and floods of temptation. 
 
  Into a wealthy place; into circumstances of propserity.

title: Psalms 66:13
text: Deliverance from special troubles calls for special thanksgiving to God, and the promises which we made in affliction should be conscientiously fulfilled.

title: Psalms 66:17
text: Jehovah is a God who hears prayer, and supplications offered to him in spirit and in truth will be abundantly answered.

title: Psalms 66:18
text: Iniquity in my heart; such as he was charged with, or any known sin.

title: Psalms 67:1
text:
This psalm breathes throughout the true missionary spirit.  The psalmist, in the exercise of lively faith and ardent love, anticipates the conversion of all nations to God, and calls upon them all to praise him for his gracious guidance. 
 
  Unto us; that is, unto us his covenant people; for it is from Zion, as blessed by Jehovah, that salvation is to go forth to all the gentile nations.   Isaiah 2:3 Isaiah 25:6  
 
The light of God's countenance and the joys of his salvation, when granted to his people, tend to spread the knowledge of his name and lead all to praise him.

title: Psalms 67:2
text: Thy way; thy way of salvation, in which all thy glorious attributes are manifested.

title: Psalms 67:3
text: Let the people praise thee; "all nations" spoken of in the preceding verse.  This is the effect of their knowing God's salvation.

title: Psalms 67:4
text:
Govern the nations; rather, lead the nations, that is, into the way of salvation. 
 
The government of God is a subject of great joy to his people, and they earnestly desire that all the nations of the earth should submit themselves to it, and be happy under it.

title: Psalms 67:6
text: Shall bless us; with all needed temporal and spiritual good.

title: Psalms 67:7
text:
All the ends of the earth shall fear him; the effect of God's blessing his own people. 
 
The prophets of the Old Testament were animated by the same spirit as the apostles under the New Testament.  They earnestly desired and prayed for the conversion and salvation of all nations; and they foresaw, with exceeding joy, the extension of the knowledge of God over all the earth.

title: Psalms 68:1
text:
The remarkable character of this psalm is best explained upon the supposition that it was written to be sung when the ark was carried in solemn procession to Jerusalem, either upon the occasion of its removal from the house of Obed-edom to Zion,  II Samuel 6:12-19 , or, as some think, at a later period, when it was brought back at the head of David's victorious army, whom it had accompanied in one of his wars. The ark was the divinely appointed symbol of God's presence.  Its entrance into Jerusalem, in triumphal procession, naturally recalled to the psalmist's mind the time when God came down from heaven to deliver his covenant people,  Exodus 3:7-8 , went before them by the way of Sinai and the Arabian wilderness to the promised land, overthrew their enemies, and put them in possession of it.  All this he celebrates in the loftiest strains of lyric poetry, with some marked allusions to the song of Deborah and Barak; and, at the close, anticipates the day when this mighty God shall receive the homage of all nations. 
 
The writers of the New Testament regard God's descent from heaven for the salvation of his ancient people, as a prophetic type of the higher salvation which Jesus Christ wrought for his people, when he was made flesh and dwelt among men.  See note to  Psalms 68:18 . 
 
  Let God arise; these are the words employed by Moses when the ark set forward,  Numbers 10:35 .  They contain both a prayer and a prediction. 
 
Though God delay for a season to appear to his people, in due time he will arise and have mercy upon them, and will confound and destroy those who rise up against them.

title: Psalms 68:4
text:
Upon the heavens; rather, through the deserts; in allusion to God's guidance of the covenant people through the wilderness of Arabia. 
 
  Jah; an abbreviation of the word Jehovah.

title: Psalms 68:6
text:
Setteth the solitary in families; provides a home for the desolate and outcast. 
 
  Dwell in a dry land; where they are destitute of the comforts which he gives those who love and obey him.

title: Psalms 68:7
text:
Wentest forth before thy people; in bringing them out of Egypt.  In this and the following verse the sacred writer agrees very closely with the words of Deborah and Barak's song.   Judges 5:4-5  
 
The deliverance of God's people and his mercies to them in times past, are foretastes and earnests of what he will do for them in time to come.

title: Psalms 68:8
text: Dropped; as in a storm of thunder and lightning.

title: Psalms 68:9
text:
A plentiful rain; most probably an allusion to the manna and quails, which are elsewhere described under the figure of rain.  Psalms 78:24 Psalms 78:27  
 
  Thine inheritance; Israel, as the heritage of God.

title: Psalms 68:10
text: Therein; in the promised land, to which the Israelites were brought through God's sustaining power in the wilderness.

title: Psalms 68:11
text:
Gave the word; the word of victory, when Israel took possession of Canaan. 
 
  Those that published it; the female singers that celebrated it. The allusion is to the choral songs of the Israelitish women with which they celebrated the victories of God's people.  Exodus 15:20 Judges 11:34 I Samuel 18:6  
 
The words of truth and love which God gives to his people encourage them to go forward in duty, putting their trust in him and expecting that he will finally give them the victory over all their foes.

title: Psalms 68:12
text: Did flee; the enemies of Israel.

title: Psalms 68:13
text:
Lain among the pots; wrought in brick and mortar in Egypt.  but some render the words, "when ye lie down among your folds;" that is, rest in peace, after the conquest of the land. 
 
Whatever may have been their former character or employment, when made partakers of divine mercy and adorned with the graces of the Holy Spirit, saints become beautiful and lovely in the eyes of the Lord of hosts and of all good beings.

title: Psalms 68:14
text:
In it; in the promised land. 
 
  White as snow; according to some, the meaning is, that the fields were white with the bones of God's enemies.  But the more probable reference is to the splendor of God's presence.

title: Psalms 68:15
text: The hill of God-- hill of Bashan; or, as we may render, "A hill of God is the hill of Bashan; a hill of [lofty] peaks is the hill of Bashan."  A hill of God means a very great and majestic hill.  The meaning of the psalmist is, that though Bashan may excel Zion in outward height and splendor, God has honored the latter by making it his peculiar abode.

title: Psalms 68:16
text: Leap ye; or, look askance; from envy at the honor conferred on the hill of Zion.

title: Psalms 68:17
text:
Twenty thousand; put for a vast multitude.  The reference is to the angelic hosts who were present at the giving of the law on Sinai.  Acts 7:53 Galatians 3:19  
 
God has multitudes which no man can number, who at his call are ready to engage in his cause and fight against his foes.

title: Psalms 68:18
text: Received gifts; applied by the apostle Paul to the ascension gifts bestowed by Christ upon his church.   Ephesians 4:8

title: Psalms 68:20
text: Issues; deliverance.

title: Psalms 68:22
text: I will bring again; according to some, I will bring my people home again from their dispersion.  But the connection favors the idea that the reference is rather to God's enemies, thus: Though they hide themselves from me in Bashan, or in the depths of the sea, thence will I bring them, that I may inflict upon them the punishment of their sins.  Compare  Amos 9:2-4 , where a similar figure is used.

title: Psalms 68:23
text:
Dipped in the blood of thine enemies; that they might utterly overcome them. 
 
Utter destruction is before the wicked; and except they repent, their ruin will be awful and sure.

title: Psalms 68:24
text:
They have seen; thy people. 
 
  Thy goings; in triumphal procession. 
 
  In the sanctuary; or, into the sanctuary on mount Zion.

title: Psalms 68:26
text: From the fountain of Israel; ye that come from the fountain of Israel, that is, the descendents of Israel.

title: Psalms 68:27
text:
Little Benjamin; the youngest of Jacob's sons, and also the smallest of the tribes present at the triumphal procession. 
 
  Judah--Zebulun--Naphtali; tribes by which they had been principally delivered, here put to represent the whole nation.

title: Psalms 68:29
text: The hearts of kings and rulers are in the hands of the Lord; and when he inclines them, they favor his people and become nursing fathers and mothers to his church.

title: Psalms 68:30
text: The multitude of the bulls, with the calves; the great, strong, and powerful; young and old.

title: Psalms 68:31
text:
Egypt; Ethiopia; representatives of the heathen world, especially Africa. 
 
The dark and polluted places of the earth, which are now full of the habitations of wickedness and cruelty, shall one day all be enlightened and purified, and become a habitation for God through his Spirit.

title: Psalms 68:33
text: Heavens of heavens; the highest heavens.

title: Psalms 68:35
text:
Out of thy holy places; literally, out of thy sanctuaries.  The plural is used here, and in  Psalms 73:17 , (in the Hebrew,) and  Leviticus 21:23 , in reference to the various divisions of the sanctuary. 
 
The God of salvation to his people will be the God of vengeance to those who continue to rebel against him.  He is a light and glory to those who serve him, but to his persevering enemies a consuming fire.

title: Psalms 69:1
text:
This psalm is often quoted in the New Testament, and applied to our Saviour.  It does not refer exclusively to Christ's person, as is manifest from  Psalms 69:5 ; but rather to the church of God in Christ her Head.  It describes the great conflict between the kingdom of God and the kingdom of Satan.  In this conflict Christ, as the Head of the church, is the principal sufferer, but each of his members also suffers with him.  In an especial manner were the sufferings of David, the divinely constituted head of God's covenant people, typical of Christ's sufferings. 
 
  The waters; an emblem of great troubles. 
 
  Unto my soul; so that they are ready to destroy my life. 
 
In the great conflict between Christ and Satan, all the true members of Christ's body have a part.  They cannot reign with him till they have suffered with him.  When for his sake they sink in deep waters, they will, in imitation of his example, earnestly cry to God for help, and wait upon him till he is pleased to appear for their salvation.

title: Psalms 69:2
text: In deep mire; distressing affliction.

title: Psalms 69:4
text:
More than the hairs; very numerous. 
 
  Then I restored that which I took not away; this psalm might literally apply to David, but more fully in its spiritual meaning to Christ.

title: Psalms 69:6
text:
For my sake; the highest application of these words is to Christ. Had he been overcome in the conflict with Satan, all the hopes of his followers must have been for ever put to shame.  In a lower, and yet a true sense, they apply to all the faithful servants of God, and more especially to those who are, like David, intrusted with important offices in her behalf. 
 
The people of God are anxious not to dishonor him, or be the occasion of injury to their fellow men, especially to such as love his salvation.

title: Psalms 69:8
text: A stranger unto my brethren; they treated him with neglect and scorn.

title: Psalms 69:9
text:
The zeal of thy house; zeal for the honor of thy house.  Applied to Jesus Christ,  John 2:17 . 
 
  Hath eaten me up; consumed me. 
 
God is very dear to his people, and leads them to show much zeal, make great sacrifices, and perform numerous labors to promote his honor.

title: Psalms 69:12
text:
Speak against me; on account of his devotion to God. 
 
Piety and drunkenness are in direct opposition to each other, and as one prevails the other will be done away.

title: Psalms 69:21
text:
They gave me vinegar; see  Matthew 27:34 . 
 
The minuteness with which the treatment of the Saviour was foretold in the Old Testament, and the exact fulfilment of the description in him, is proof that it was given by inspiration, and that holy men of old wrote and spoke as they were directed by the Holy Ghost.

title: Psalms 69:22
text: Let their table become a snare; the prayer contained in this and hte six following verses, is also a prophecy of the doom that should overtake the incorrigible enemies of God's people.  It was fulfilled upon David's enemies, such as Ahithophel, but it has its highest fulfilment in the case of Christ's enemies.  Compare  Romans 11:9-10 .

title: Psalms 69:25
text: See  Matthew 23:38 .

title: Psalms 69:27
text:
Add iniquity; punishment. 
 
  Come into thy righteousness; be numbered among the righteous, or share in the blessings of their salvation.

title: Psalms 69:31
text: The offerings of the heart, as manifested in prayer and praise, are more precious in the sight of God than any external service, and are essential to true religion.

title: Psalms 69:32
text: The humble shall see this, and be glad; the cause of Christ is the cause of the humble; they sympathize with him in his sufferings, and rejoice with him in his triumphs.

title: Psalms 69:35
text:
God will save Zion; the deliverance of Christ, who is the chief subject of this psalm, includes in itself the deliverance of Zion also; that is, his church universal. 
 
The deliverance of Christ in the hour of his trial, is a pledge of the deliverance of all who put their trust in him.  Since he was victorious over Satan, none of his true disciples can fail of victory.  He conquered the powers of hell for himself, and for all his followers.

title: Psalms 70:1
text: See notes to  Psalms 40:17 , with which this psalm substantially agrees.

title: Psalms 70:3
text:
Aha; an expression of contemptuous exultation. 
 
The end of all who persist in persecuting God's servants, shall be "shame and everlasting contempt."  But they who seek God in sincerity and truth shall be, through grace, rewarded with everlasting glory and blessedness.

title: Psalms 70:5
text: The unworthiness and poverty of sinners forms no barrier against their acceptance with God; when their wants are duly felt, and they apply to God for help, he is glorified in bestowing it upon them.

title: Psalms 71:1
text:
In its general character, this psalm agrees with  Psalms 22:1-31 Psalms 40:1-17 Psalms 69:1-36 , and is to be interpreted upon the same principles. 
 

 
Trust in the Lord is the sure means of safety to his people, and their habitual resort in time of trouble.

title: Psalms 71:6
text: God is our maker, our preserver, and the giver of all our mercies.  On him we ever have been and must be dependent for all good, and to him we should be habitually devoted.

title: Psalms 71:7
text: I am as a wonder unto many; an object of astonishment from the intensity of my sufferings.  These words were strikingly fulfilled in the person of our Lord, the great Head of the church.   Isaiah 52:14  They are fulfilled also in each of his members, according to the measure of "the afflictions of Christ," which God has appointed him to "fill up."   Colossians 1:24

title: Psalms 71:9
text: Old age is a time when men peculiarly need the presence and favor of God, and he will not cast off any who truly trust in him.

title: Psalms 71:11
text: God hath forsaken him; this they concluded from his distresses.

title: Psalms 71:13
text: Let them be confounded; see note to  Psalms 69:22 .

title: Psalms 71:15
text:
The numbers; the number of his mercies. 
 
The mercies of God are innumerable, and call for habitual thanksgiving.

title: Psalms 71:20
text:
Shalt quicken me again; grant him deliverance from trouble and give him prosperity. 
 
  From the depths of the earth; from the deep waters of the earth, put here as a symbol of great distress.   Psalms 69:2 Psalms 130:1  
 
However great the present trials of God's people, they may rejoice in the anticipation of being one day delivered, and made conquerors and more than conquerors over all their foes.

title: Psalms 71:22
text: Psaltery; a stringed instrument of music.

title: Psalms 72:1
text:
Thy judgments; thy righteous decisions. 
 
  The king's son; literally, Solomon, so called as the son of David and his successor on the throne, in correspondence with the original promise of God to David, "He shall build a house for my name, and I will stablish the throne of his kingdom for ever,"  II Samuel 7:13 ; the words include the entire line of Solomon's successors, which is perpetuated for ever in Christ.  Thus Christ himself is the main subject of the psalm.  In Solomon it has only an incipient fulfilment. 
 
All wise decisions and all righteous conduct proceed from God their author; and to him all should look that he would grant them the influence of his grace, and thus fit them for the various duties to which they are called.

title: Psalms 72:3
text: The mountains shall bring peace--by righteousness; the mountains and hills shall, as it were, bring forth a harvest of peace to God's people, as the effect of righteousness.  Peace includes in itself all prosperity, temporal and spiritual.  Righteousness is here the righteous government of the king whom this psalm celebrated, producing righteousness among the people.

title: Psalms 72:4
text: The kingdom of Christ, with the salvation which it brings to the soul, is the heritage of none but the poor in spirit.  The proud and self sufficient are excluded from it, and must stumble and fall into perdition.

title: Psalms 72:6
text: He shall come down; the effect of his righteous administration shall be like that of rain on meadows newly mown.  Compare  II Samuel 23:3-4 .  The happy effects of Solomon's just and peaceable reign were typical of the nobler influences of Christ's spiritual reign over his people.

title: Psalms 72:7
text: Since the cause of the righteous is the cause of Christ, it must increase and prosper until it becomes triumphant over the whole earth; and, during its conflict with the kingdom of Satan, all that are spiritually united to Christ, enjoy, in the midst of their outward trials, the peace of God which passeth all understanding.

title: Psalms 72:8
text: From sea to sea; over all the earth.   Psalms 72:11 Psalms 72:17

title: Psalms 72:9
text: Lick the dust; be utterly subdued.

title: Psalms 72:10
text:
vv 10-11. 
 
  Tarshish--the isles--Sheba and Seba; Tarshish was a celebrated mart of trade in the south-west of Spain.  The isles are, in general, the sea-coasts and islands of the Mediterranean.  Sheba was a country of Southern Arabia, celebrated for its gold, spices, and precious stones.  I Kings 10:10   Seba is generally supposed to have been Meroe, a province of Ethiopia.  These countries stand here to represent all the nations of the earth, which shall in due time give their wealth and homage to Christ.  Compare  Isaiah 60:1-22 .

title: Psalms 72:12
text:
vv 12-13. 
 
  He shall deliver the needy; the protection which Solomon as a righteous king gave to the poor and needy, represented the higher spiritual protection which Christ gives to all the poor in spirit, who feel their need of him and come to him for help and salvation.  Compare  Matthew 11:28-30 . 
 
Whatever may be the outward worldly condition of Christ's disciples, he will give them all needful protection, help, and comfort here, and eternal deliverance from all oppression and sorrow hereafter.

title: Psalms 72:15
text:
For him; for the extension of his blessed kingdom in the world, and in the heart of him who offers the prayer. 
 
All the true members of Christ's body are animated by his spirit, which is the spirit of love and self-denial.  They continually pray for his honor and the enlargement of his kingdom among men; and to this end give liberally of that which God has entrusted to them.

title: Psalms 72:16
text: Upon the top of the mountains; upon the most unlikely places, as well as others, the gospel shall take deep root and produce abundant fruits.

title: Psalms 72:20
text: Are ended; this is the close of the second of the books into which the Psalms were anciently divided.

title: Psalms 73:1
text:
The psalmist relates through what a severe inward conflict he has passed in view of the prosperity of the wicked and the afflictions of the righteous, and how he has overcome it by a revelation in God's sanctuary of the different ends that await the two classes of men. 
 
  To such as are of a clean heart; by these words he limits his declaration concerning Israel to such as are Israelites indeed.

title: Psalms 73:3
text: Envy is as the rottenness of the bones.  He who indulges in it, whether saint or sinner, will be wretched.

title: Psalms 73:4
text: No bands; no peculiar terrors or distresses.

title: Psalms 73:5
text: Not in trouble; as many pious men are.

title: Psalms 73:6
text:
As a chain; that is, a chain worn for ornament.  Genesis 41:42 Proverbs 1:9 Daniel 5:16 Daniel 5:29  
 
The pride of the wicked is increased by their prosperity, which may be given them in wrath as a punishment for sins, and be the occasion of ripening them for ruin.

title: Psalms 73:7
text: More; of this world.

title: Psalms 73:9
text: Walketh through the earth; is used without restraint.

title: Psalms 73:10
text:
Therefore; because of this disagreement between the character of men and their present lot. 
 
  His people return hither; of this clause the original admits of two readings, and it is otherwise of difficult explanation.  Our English version follows one reading, the other is thus: "He maketh his people to return hither."  Of the various interpretations that have been proposed, the following is perhaps as probable as any: God makes his people, after all their wanderings this way and that in search of an explanation of this mystery, to come back hither, namely, to the point whence they set out--that good men are afflicted, and bad men prospered. 
 
  Waters of a full cup are wrung out to them; they drink to the dregs a bitter cup in witnessing the prosperity of the wicked, while they are themselves filled with trouble, and their sufferings are aggravated by the temptation to distrust God's justice. 
 
Great afflictions are no certain sign of peculiar wickedness; they may be sent in mercy, as fatherly chastisements, and be designed to wean men from the world, quicken them in duty, and fit them for heaven.

title: Psalms 73:11
text: They; the wicked.

title: Psalms 73:13
text: I have cleansed my heart in vain; this was what the psalmist was tempted to say, that his piety was useless.

title: Psalms 73:14
text: Plagued; visited with distresses.

title: Psalms 73:15
text: I should offend; such doctrines expressed would grieve the people of God, as being contrary to their experience, contrary to truth, and adapted to do mischief.

title: Psalms 73:16
text:
To know this; the reasons of the prosperity of the wicked and the adversity of the righteous. 
 
The ways of Providence with men often appear unaccountable, and the reasons of them will not be known in this world.  We must keep in view the end of the righteous and the wicked, and act with habitual reference to the closing scenes of life.

title: Psalms 73:18
text: In slippery places; where, notwithstanding their present prosperity, they are on the brink of perdition.

title: Psalms 73:19
text: Brought into desolation; perish at death.

title: Psalms 73:20
text:
When thou awakest; when God leaves the wicked for a season to triumph over the good, he is said to sleep.   Psalms 44:23  
 
  Their image; their vain show of happiness, which is as unsubstantial and fleeting as a night-vision.

title: Psalms 73:21
text: Thus my heart was grieved; before I understood the end of the wicked.  The psalmist reviews his former feelings with deep repentance.

title: Psalms 73:22
text: To envy the wicked on account of their worldly prosperity is foolish and sinful.  It is finding fault with the providence of God, and exposes those who indulge in it to his wrath.

title: Psalms 73:23
text:
Thou hast holden me; kept him from utter apostasy and ruin. 
 
God holds up his people and keeps them, notwithstanding their follies and sins; and in drawing near to him in humble repentance and obedient faith, they find not only their greatest safety, but also their highest joy.

title: Psalms 73:24
text:
Afterward; after the trials of the present life. 
 
  Receive me to glory; the consciousness of union by faith and love with the eternal God, brings to the psalmist the assurance of a blessed immortality to be spent in God's presence.

title: Psalms 73:25
text: But thee; none in comparison with God.

title: Psalms 73:26
text:
My flesh and my heart faileth; these words describe his mortal body as subject to decay and death. 
 
  Strength of my heart; the supporter of my soul.  He uses the word "heart" here of his spiritual and immortal nature.

title: Psalms 74:1
text:
Title, of Asaph; as this psalm must be referred to the destruction of the temple by the Chaldeans, many understand "Asaph" as standing for Asaph's family; as several psalms are, according to one interpretation, ascribed to "the sons of Korah," that is, to some one of his descendants. 
 
  The sheep of thy pasture; Israel, as the peculiar people of God, and especially the pious among this people. 
 
The fatherly corrections which God inflicts on his people, and which are indications of his love, may sometimes be mistaken by them for expressions of anger; but in the end they will see that it was in kindness to their souls.

title: Psalms 74:2
text: The rod of thine inheritance; or, the tribe of thine inheritance, the word tribe being used collectively for the whole people.

title: Psalms 74:3
text: Lift up thy feet; that is, march forth from thy hiding-place and look upon the desolations caused by the enemy.

title: Psalms 74:4
text:
Thy congregations; rather, thy places of assembly.  The Hebrew word is the same that is rendered "synagogues," in  Psalms 74:8 , where see note. 
 
  There ensigns for signs; they have set up their own heathenish ensigns, as tokens of their dominion, where once the symbol of God's presence and power stood. 
 
  Ensigns; tokens of authority.

title: Psalms 74:5
text: A man was famous--thick trees; the meaning of this and the following verse, according to our version, seems to be, that once men showed their power and skill in cutting down forest-trees for useful purposes, such as building; but now they make themselves famous as destroyers.  We may, however, render literally thus: "He [the enemy] makes himself known as one who lifts up axes upon thick trees.  And now they break down," etc.  That is, he proceeds with the cedar-work of the temple as one does with the common trees of the forest, destroying without thought or care.

title: Psalms 74:6
text: Carved work; with which the place of worship was adorned.

title: Psalms 74:8
text:
All the synagogue of--the land; or, all the places of assembly in the land.  See notes to  Psalms 74:4 .  There is no necessity of understanding this of the Jewish synagogues, which were first built at a later date.  None of the ancient versions so translate it. 
 
Men may be so blinded and hardened by sin as to attempt the utter destruction of the Lord's people; but in due time he will arise, plead his own cause, and bring destruction upon those who continue to oppose it.

title: Psalms 74:9
text:
Our signs; tokens of God's presence, especially as manifested in the gift of prophecy. 
 
  How long; how long our troubles will continue.

title: Psalms 74:11
text: Withdrawest thou thy hand; delaying to deliver them.

title: Psalms 74:12
text: Working salvation; in the deliverance of Israel from Egypt and from all their enemies.

title: Psalms 74:13
text:
Dragons; monsters of the deep; representing the great and powerful opposers of divine truth.  So also leviathan in the following verse. 
 
Past deliverances of God's people encourage them to expect his interposition in future, and to look to him for the aid which they need.

title: Psalms 74:16
text: The vicissitudes of the seasons are all ordered by God, and he who can make day and night, summer and winter, can do all things which the good of his people and the blessings he bestows upon them, manifest the perfections of his character and show forth his glory.

title: Psalms 74:19
text: Thy turtledove; an appellation of endearment, showing God's tender regard for his people.

title: Psalms 74:20
text:
The covenant; that he made with Abraham and his posterity, especially with reference to the coming of the Messiah. 
 
  The dark places of the earth; those not enlightened by revelation. The psalmist means that the cruelty of these dark places is exercised against God's covenant-people, which is a reason why he should remember his covenant with them. 
 
The covenant which God made with his people, with reference to the Redeemer and the blessings of his universal reign, is ordered in all things and sure; and not one jot or tittle of it will fail till it is all completely accomplished.

title: Psalms 75:1
text:
God's people praise him for his promised interposition in a time of great trouble and confusion, occasioned by their subjection to the insolence and oppression of the wicked. 
 
  Thy name is near; thou art coming forth to display thy glorious perfections in the protection and deliverance of thy people. 
 
The works of Jehovah, especially his protection of his people and the blessings he bestows upon them, manifest the perfections of his character and show forth his glory.

title: Psalms 75:2
text: When I shall receive the congregation; or, When I shall take a set time.  In this and the following verse Jehovah is the speaker.

title: Psalms 75:3
text:
Are dissolved; order and equity are overthrown by the triumph of the ungodly. 
 
  I bear up the pillars of it; I who have established and now maintain the pillars of the earth, will reestablish order in it. 
 
The earth and all things therein are dependent upon God, and are entirely under his control.

title: Psalms 75:4
text:
I said unto the fools; this is the psalmist's admonition to the wicked, in view of God's promised interposition. 
 
  Lift not up the horn; indulge not in pride or haughtiness.

title: Psalms 75:6
text: No one is elevated to office or influence among men except such as God appoints.

title: Psalms 75:8
text: A cup--full of mixture; a cup drugged with spices to increase its intoxicating effect.  This is a common scriptural figure to represent the effects of God's judgments upon the wicked.

title: Psalms 75:10
text: A great and eternal distinction will be witnessed between the righteous and the wicked, between him that serveth God and him that serveth him not.

title: Psalms 76:1
text:
The reference of this psalm to the overthrow of Sennacherib's army cannot be mistaken.  See the history,  II Kings 18:1-19:37 Isaiah 36:1-37:38 . As to the title Asaph, see introductory note to  Psalms 74:1 . 
 
God is known only in those lands which are enlightened by revelation; all others are veiled in darkness and the shadow of death.  Hence, those who are blessed with the word of God should communicate it to all people.

title: Psalms 76:2
text: Salem; the ancient anme, as is generally believed, of Jerusalem, signifying peace.   Genesis 14:18

title: Psalms 76:3
text: The arrows of the bow; weapons of war.

title: Psalms 76:4
text: Than the mountains of prey; mountains inhabited by beasts of prey, here used figuratively to represent the warlike heathen nations. Compare  Daniel 7:3 .

title: Psalms 76:5
text:
They have slept their sleep; the sleep of death; as was the case with the Assyrians, when a hundred and eighty-five thousand were killed in a night. 
 
  Found their hands; been able to use them.

title: Psalms 76:6
text:
A dead sleep; the sleep of death. 
 
Without the sustaining care of Jehovah no one can live, and when he ceases to support them his enemies sleep the sleep of death.

title: Psalms 76:8
text: The earth feared; on account of the wrath of Jehovah, as displayed in the salvation of his people and the destruction of their enemies.

title: Psalms 76:10
text:
Praise thee; be made the occasion of his praise. 
 
  The remainder of wrath shalt thou restrain; or, more literally, with the remainder of wrath shalt thou gird thyself; that is, that thou mayest use it as a weapon against those who indulge in it. 
 
God will not suffer any more of human wrath to exist than he can overrule for the advancement of his glory and the good of his people.

title: Psalms 76:12
text: Before the power of God, kings and princes are as helpless as the feeblest among their subjects.  At his rebuke they perish with all their hosts.

title: Psalms 77:1
text:
The psalmist, in deep distress, encourages himself by the remembrance of God's goodness and wonderful dealings towards his people in times past.  According to the opinion of some, he speaks in the name of the afflicted people of God. 
 
While men of the world in their troubles look to creatures for help, or sink down in discouragement, the people of God cry unto him, and he in due time delivers them.

title: Psalms 77:2
text:
My sore ran; rather, my hand, was spread out; that is, in prayer. 
 
  In the night; his troubles continued while others were refreshed with sleep.

title: Psalms 77:5
text:
The days of old; when God appeared for the salvation of his people. 
 
A consideration of the mercies of God in times past is well suited to raise the expectation of his help in time to come.

title: Psalms 77:9
text: Forgotten to be gracious; this the psalmist was tempted to believe.

title: Psalms 77:10
text:
This is my infirmity; that is, as the original word implies, my affliction, laid upon me by God, and therefore to be borne with faith and patience.  Accordingly the tone of the psalm here changes from the spirit of despondency to that of hope. 
 
  The years of the right hand of the Most High; when he wrought wonders for the deliverance of his people. 
 
Despair of the mercy of God is highly sinful, and a temptation of the devil for the purpose of ruining the souls of men.

title: Psalms 77:13
text:
In the sanctuary; the place where God is worshipped, and where his character and the reasons of his dealings are best learned. 
 
The house of God is the place where he especially manifests himself to his people, and enables them so to cast their cares upon him as to find that he careth for them.

title: Psalms 77:16
text:
The waters saw thee; alluding to his wonders at the Red sea. 
 
No obstructions will hinder the salvation of God's people when he appears for their deliverance.  He can open the way for them through the sea, raise up leaders, and guide them safely to his heavenly rest.

title: Psalms 77:19
text: Thy footsteps are not known; the works and ways of God are inscrutable, and surpass finite comprehension.

title: Psalms 78:1
text: A historic psalm, for the instruction of God's covenant people.  It was probably written in David's day, and ends with his elevation to the throne.

title: Psalms 78:2
text:
Parable--dark sayings; see note to  Psalms 49:4 . 
 
Many of the instructions and truths of the Bible are dark sayings to those who reject them, while they are plain and highly useful to those who believe and obey them.

title: Psalms 78:4
text: A knowledge of the past dealings of God should be communicated by parents to their children, as a means of leading them to adore him, and preparing them to transmit the knowledge of his perfections to those who come after them.

title: Psalms 78:5
text: Make them known; the testimony and law just spoken of.

title: Psalms 78:8
text:
Set not their heart aright; did not heartily obey God. 
 
Men must keep their hearts with all diligence, if they would have their lives directed according to his precepts.

title: Psalms 78:9
text:
The children of Ephraim; here representing the whole people.  They seem to be specially named because they were the leading tribe before the time of the kings. 
 
  Turned back; the reference is not probably to any particular recorded event, but to their general unbelief and unfaithfulness.

title: Psalms 78:12
text:
Zoan; one of the principal cities of Egypt.   Numbers 13:22  
 
No displays of the mercies or judgments of God will lead men to love and obey him; but whatever may be the manifestations of himself, without his grace they will continue to rebel against him.

title: Psalms 78:13
text: He divided the sea; at the time of the deliverance of Israel from Egypt.

title: Psalms 78:18
text: They tempted God; by distrusting his power, truth, and love.

title: Psalms 78:21
text:
A fire was kindled; see  Numbers 11:1 . 
 
Unbelief of divine testimony is a great sin, and God is angry with those who indulge it.  They treat him as if he were a liar, and cut themselves off from the blessings of his salvation.

title: Psalms 78:24
text: Corn of heaven; manna, which came from above.

title: Psalms 78:25
text: Angels' food; the manna is so called from its excellence as coming from heaven.

title: Psalms 78:27
text: Blessings greatly desired may be given in judgment, and be the occasion of ruin to those who receive them.

title: Psalms 78:33
text:
Their days did he consume in vanity, and their years in trouble; the reference is to the wearisome sojourn of forty years in the wilderness, during which time all the men who came out of Egypt were wasted away.  Compare  Psalms 90:7-9 . 
 
Continuance in sin causes continuance of trouble, and though great afflictions may produce external reformation, yet if the heart be not turned to God, the outward profession of love to him will be hypocrisy.

title: Psalms 78:34
text: Slew them; many of them; and visited others with sore calamities.

title: Psalms 78:36
text: They lied; by an insincere profession of love and obedience.

title: Psalms 78:38
text: God shows his compassion by waiting long even upon flagrant transgressors, and often by removing from them temporal calamities and continuing to bless them, notwithstanding their sins, in proof that he desires not their death, but that they should turn and live.

title: Psalms 78:41
text: Limited the Holy One; by ascribing bounds to his power.

title: Psalms 78:43
text: The field of Zion; the region about the city.   Psalms 78:12

title: Psalms 78:47
text: With frost; rather, with hailstones.

title: Psalms 78:51
text: The tabernacles of Ham; the dwelling-places of the Egyptians, his descendants.

title: Psalms 78:52
text: God will make a way for his chosen people, and grant them deliverance; but his enemies, however numerous and powerful, will be destroyed.

title: Psalms 78:54
text:
The border of his sanctuary; the boundary of the holy land. 
 
  This mountain; Zion, as now the central point of the nation.  See  Psalms 78:68 .

title: Psalms 78:57
text: Like a deceitful bow; not accomplishing the end for which they were made.

title: Psalms 78:60
text:
Shiloh; a place in the tribe of Ephraim in which had been kept the ark of God, the symbol of his presence. 
 
The withdrawal of God's presence from a people on account of their sins, is a forerunner of dreadful calamities, and often of approaching ruin.

title: Psalms 78:61
