text: His strength--his glory; the ark, which was the emblem of these, and which was taken captive by the Philistines.   I Samuel 4:11

title: Psalms 78:63
text: Not given to marriage; literally, not praised, that is, in nuptial songs, according to the custom of the age.

title: Psalms 78:64
text: Their widows made no lamentation; the meaning seems to be, that the bodies of the slain were left to perish on the field of battle, so that their widows could not mourn over them, as was done at a regular funeral.  Compare  Jeremiah 16:6-7 Jeremiah 25:33  and especially  Jeremiah 22:18-19 .

title: Psalms 78:65
text: The Lord awaked; arose for the deliverance of his people.

title: Psalms 78:66
text: God may permit the wicked to triumph for a time, as a punishment of his people; but their triumph will be short, and their punishment without end.

title: Psalms 78:67
text: Refused the tabernacle of Joseph; refused to have his descendants, the tribe of Ephraim, longer govern the people.

title: Psalms 78:68
text:
Chose the tribe of Judah; to have the preeminence, as furnishing the royal family. 
 
  The mount Zion; as the site of the tabernacle, and afterwards of the temple.  Moriah was reckoned as a part of Zion. 
 
Civil power is the gift of God.  He takes it from one and gives it to another, as seemeth good in his sight; and holds all who receive it accountable to him for its use.

title: Psalms 78:69
text: His sanctuary; the temple, or place of public worship.

title: Psalms 79:1
text:
A psalm belonging to the same period as  Psalms 74:1-23 ; that is, the Babylonish invasion and captivity. 
 
For the sins of God's people, they are often brought into trouble; and they cannot obtain deliverance till, by repentance and reformation, they forsake their iniquities and turn to him.

title: Psalms 79:4
text: To our neighbors; to the surrounding heathen nations, who rejoiced in their calamities.   Psalms 137:7 Obadiah 1:12-14

title: Psalms 79:7
text: Devoured Jacob; overcome the Israelites and slain them, or carried them away captive.

title: Psalms 79:8
text: The only hope of sinners is in the mercy of God through our Lord Jesus Christ, and to him they should look for pardon, salvation, and all needed good.

title: Psalms 79:9
text: Purge away our sins; forgive them for Christ's sake.

title: Psalms 79:10
text: Revenging of the blood of thy servants; punishing those who slew them.

title: Psalms 79:12
text: While the Lord delivers his servants, he brings deserved punishment upon his enemies.  To the one he is a kind and merciful shepherd, and to the other a consuming fire.

title: Psalms 80:1
text:
A prayer of God's people in deep distress occasioned by the oppression of foreign enemies, in which the transfer of Israel from Egypt to Canaan is beautifully set forth under the allegory of a vine.  It belongs apparently to the later period before the Babylonish captivity. In the opinion of many, its occasion was the overthrow of the kingdom of Israel by the Assyrians. 
 
  Joseph; the Israelites.

title: Psalms 80:2
text: Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh; during the sojourn of the Israelites in the wilderness of Arabia, these three tribes encamped together on the west side of the tabernacle,  Numbers 2:18-22 ; and in the order of march, they followed the Kohathites who bore the ark of the covenant, the symbol of God's presence,  Numbers 10:21-22 ; thus having "the ark of the covenant of the Lord of hosts, which dwelleth between the cherubim," immediately before them.  Exodus 25:20 Exodus 25:22 II Samuel 6:2

title: Psalms 80:3
text: The light of God's countenance is the greatest blessing that any can enjoy, and is most earnestly desired and sought by his obedient people.

title: Psalms 80:5
text: Bread of tears; deep afflictions, causing many to weep.

title: Psalms 80:8
text:
A vine; the church, as embodied in the nation of Israel. 
 
For all her prosperity the church is dependent on the grace of God, while her sins are the cause of all her sorrows.

title: Psalms 80:10
text: And the boughs thereof were like the goodly cedars; or, and with the boughs thereof, the cedars of God [were covered.]

title: Psalms 80:11
text:
The sea; the Mediterranean. 
 
  The river; Euphrates.

title: Psalms 80:13
text: The boar--and the wild beast; representing the heathen by whom the Israelites were overcome.

title: Psalms 80:15
text: Help for the guilty is laid upon One who is mighty to save, who came to take away sin by the sacrifice of himself, and who ever lives to make intercession for all who come unto God through him.

title: Psalms 80:17
text: The son of man; the Messiah, for whose advent God's people looked to deliver them from their troubles.

title: Psalms 81:1
text:
A song for the festival of the passover.  See note to  Psalms 81:5 . 
 
The praise of God forms an important part of the business of his people, and while it honors him, it enlivens, invigorates, and sanctifies their own souls.

title: Psalms 81:3
text:
In the new moon; this was done at the beginning of every month,  Numbers 10:10   But the beginning of the month Abib, being also the beginning of the year,  Exodus 12:2 , would naturally be observed with peculiar solemnities. 
 
  In the time appointed; or, at the full moon, as the Hebrew word seems to signify.  The passover was eaten on the fourteenth day of the month Abib, consequently at the full moon.

title: Psalms 81:5
text:
This; the solemn feast spoken of above, the feast of the passover. 
 
  In Joseph; among the Israelites. 
 
  Testimony; a perpetual witness of the deliverance of Israel. 
 
  A language that I understood not; the language of a foreign people, the Egyptians.

title: Psalms 81:6
text: The burden--the pots; the hard service in brick and mortar.

title: Psalms 81:7
text:
The secret place of thunder; the cloud which encompasses God's throne, whence proceed thunderings and lightnings. 
 
God is ever ready to hear and answer those who in sincerity and truth call upon him, and to grant them the blessings which they need.  Let them hearken unto him, and they shall not want any good thing.

title: Psalms 81:10
text:
Open thy mouth; enlarge thy desires. 
 
  I will fill it; give abundance of blessings.

title: Psalms 81:12
text: The reason why any are ever left of God to hardness of heart and blindness of mind, to follow their own inclinations to their ruin, is, they choose not to walk in his ways.

title: Psalms 81:13
text: God sincerely and earnestly desires the salvation of men, and is greatly dishonored and grieved when they refuse to obey him, and thus cut themselves off from his blessing, when by obedience they might through grace secure all needed good for this life and the life to come.

title: Psalms 81:15
text: Their time; the time of his people's prosperity.

title: Psalms 81:16
text: Fed them--with the finest of the wheat; given them the richest blessings.

title: Psalms 82:1
text:
A psalm in which unjust rulers and judges are rebuked, and their duties set forth. 
 
  The gods; rulers; called gods on account of their having received from God authority to act as his representatives and in his behalf.  Exodus 22:28  
 
Although rulers are elevated to a resemblance in authority and power to the Most High, yet they are dependent upon God for their influence, and to him must render an account for the manner in which they employ it.

title: Psalms 82:2
text: Accept the persons; be guilty of partiality and injustice.

title: Psalms 82:4
text: One great object of civil government is to defend the poor, weak, and defenceless against the encroachments of the rich and the strong, and to award equal justice to all.

title: Psalms 82:5
text:
Walk on in darkness; continue to pervert justice in their administration. 
 
  Out of course; society is disorganized by their ignorance and iniquity.

title: Psalms 82:6
text: Ye are gods; the representatives of God.  See note to  Psalms 82:1 ; also note to  John 10:35 .

title: Psalms 82:7
text:
Like men; like other men, they must die and give an account of their stewardship. 
 
It becomes rulers as well as ruled to keep in view their sins, and act with an habitual reference to the time when all will stand on a level before God, and receive a retribution according to their works.

title: Psalms 83:1
text: A prayer in view of a formidable combination of the enemies of God's people to destroy them.  Some refer it to the combination of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, and others against Jehoshaphat, which is recorded in  II Chronicles 20:1-37 .

title: Psalms 83:3
text:
Thy hidden ones; thy people, whom thou hidest in thy pavilion from the assaults of their enemies.   Psalms 27:5 Psalms 31:20  
 
The wicked have often sought the destruction of the righteous, but their plans have been defeated, and the ruin which they thought to bring upon others came upon themselves.

title: Psalms 83:6
text: Hagarenes; a people driven from their own lands by the tribe of Simeon, in the days of Saul.

title: Psalms 83:7
text: Gebal; supposed to have been a part of Idumea.

title: Psalms 83:8
text:
Assur; Assyria. 
 
  Children of Lot; Moab and Ammon.

title: Psalms 83:9
text: Midianites--Sisera--Jabin;  Judges 4:1-5:31 Judges 7:1-21:25

title: Psalms 83:10
text:
Endor; near to mount Tabor, in the north part of Canaan. 
 
However numerous or formidable the enemies of the church, or however extensive the combinations formed against her, in answer to her prayers they will be overcome, scattered, and destroyed.

title: Psalms 83:13
text: Like a wheel; whirling like stubble or chaff before the wind.

title: Psalms 83:14
text: The mountains; their productions.

title: Psalms 83:16
text:
With shame; that is, dishonor, that by this chastisement they may be brought to seek thy name.  But some, in view of the following words, supply in the last clause of this verse the word "men," as is done in  Psalms 83:18 , and render thus: "Fill their faces with shame; that men may seek thy name, O Lord. 
 
The Lord will be known by the judgments which he executes, and the destruction of the wicked will be an eternal monument of his truth, his justice, and his power.

title: Psalms 84:1
text:
Amiable; lovely. 
 
  Thy tabernacles; the place where Jehovah was worshipped. 
 
The worship and service of God are inexpressibly dear to his people. His ordinances are as food to their souls; and when deprived of them they become enfeebled and faint for want of spiritual food.

title: Psalms 84:5
text:
In whose heart are the ways; whose hearts are set on the ways that lead to the house, worship, and service of God. 
 
Men must depend upon God and draw their support and strength from him, in order successfully to walk in his ways, or find that consolation which his service is suited to afford.

title: Psalms 84:6
text:
The valley of Baca; a barren, desolate valley; put here as the emblem of suffering and want. 
 
  Make it a well; turn it into a fountain of water.  The meaning is, that God's accompanying blessing opens a fountain for their refeshment, as was done for Israel of old, in the wilderness.  Compare  Isaiah 43:19-20 . 
 
When God requires any service of his people, he will give them the strength and the means necessary for its performance.

title: Psalms 84:7
text: From strength to strength; from one stage to another with increasing energy and vigor, through the refreshment they obtain.

title: Psalms 84:9
text: Thine anointed; Christ, or David as the representative and type of Christ.

title: Psalms 84:10
text:
Better; more desirable and precious. 
 
In the spiritual worship of God is greater enjoyment to the spiritually minded, than in all the pleasures of sin.  It is the fruit of divine grace, and a sure preparation for endless glory.

title: Psalms 84:11
text:
Sun and shield; protector, benefactor, and source of all good. 
 
  Grace and glory; one as a preparation for the other.

title: Psalms 85:1
text: This psalm is referred by many to the time when the restoration of the Jewish state after the Babylonish captivity was in progress, but not yet completed, and many trials and difficulties remained to be encountered.  The writer first thanks God for the good work which he has begun, and then prays that he would remove the present severe pressure of trouble.

title: Psalms 85:2
text:
Covered; that is, by forgiveness. 
 
All needed blessings are through grace connected with the forgiveness of sin, without which nothing will avail to salvation.

title: Psalms 85:4
text: Turn us; restore us to our former prosperity.  In the mind of a pious Israelite, such restoration always included the idea of repentance and reformation.

title: Psalms 85:6
text:
Revive us again; by thy life-giving presence and favor.  The reviving for which the psalmist prays, includes both the spiritual and the temporal prosperity of Israel, which were inseparably connected with each other. 
 
God is the source of all prosperity, national and individual, spiritual and temporal.  Men are dependent upon him for "every good and perfect gift;" especially for the beginning and increase of true religion and the salvation connected with it.

title: Psalms 85:8
text:
To folly; especially to idolatry and its vices. 
 
God will not spare the sins of his covenant people.  If they would receive a gracious answer to their prayers, they must repent of their folly and return to it no more.

title: Psalms 85:10
text:
Mercy and truth are met together; they harmonize in the dealings of God, especially in his method of forgiving sin and saving sinners through the Redeemer. 
 
All the attributes of God harmonize in his dealings with men, especially in the way in which he delivers them from hell and prepares them for heaven.

title: Psalms 85:11
text:
Spring out of the earth; like an abundant harvest. 
 
  Righteousness shall look down from heaven; as a friend and helper. The reference is to God's truth and righteousness, as manifested in the fulfilment of his engagements to his covenant people.

title: Psalms 85:13
text: The way of his steps; lead us to imitate his example.

title: Psalms 86:1
text: Poor and needy; this, in a spiritual sense, is the case with all men.

title: Psalms 86:2
text:
Holy; one consecrated to God. 
 
Consciousness of devotion to God gives great encouragement to pray and to trust in him, with the expectation of receiving all needed good.

title: Psalms 86:3
text: Daily; literally, all the day.

title: Psalms 86:7
text: Prayer is the unfailing resource of God's people in time of trouble, and the sure means of help.

title: Psalms 86:8
text: Gods; such as were worshipped among the heathen.

title: Psalms 86:9
text:
All nations--shall come and worship before thee; in the days of millennial glory. 
 
However small the number of those who now worship God in spirit and in truth, the time is coming when the whole family of man shall unite in this blessed employment.

title: Psalms 86:11
text: Unite my heart; bring my affections and all my powers into sweet accordance with thy will.

title: Psalms 86:13
text: Deliverance from hell and preparation for heaven is a blessing which God in his rich mercy and grace grants to his people, and for which they are bound, and will be disposed, to adore and praise him for ever.

title: Psalms 87:1
text:
A psalm which predicts the conversion of all nations to Christ under the beautiful figure of their birth in Zion. 
 
  His foundation; God's foundation, that is, the temple which he has founded.

title: Psalms 87:2
text:
Zion; Zion, as the centre of the ancient Jewish theocracy, is put by the inspired writers to represent that theocracy.  Of this the Christian church is the true heir and successor,  Romans 4:16 , so that all the promises made by God to Zion belong to her. 
 
The place of public worship is dear not only to the people of God, but to God himself.

title: Psalms 87:4
text:
I will make mention of Rahab and Babylon; I will name them as nations that have been converted to God, and thus become spiritually the children of Zion. 
 
  Rahab; a name for Egypt. 
 
  This man; in the Hebrew, simply this, referring to the various nations just enumerated.

title: Psalms 87:5
text:
Was born in her; had become spiritually her offspring.  The reference is still to the conversion of the nations to Zion. 
 
To be born under the gospel, and to be spiritually a partaker of its salvation, is a greater honor and blessedness than to have descended from the greatest kings, or be a partaker of all earthly good.

title: Psalms 87:6
text:
When he writeth up the people; when he enrolls the nations. 
 
God has given to his Son all nations, as his inheritance; and in due time he will enroll them all as the spiritual citizens of Zion.

title: Psalms 87:7
text:
Springs; sources of salvation in the widest sense.   Psalms 46:4  
 
  In thee; in Zion, as of the residence of God. 
 
God's presence and the light of his countenance fill the true Zion with joy and gladness; and through her he dispenses to all nations the blessings of his salvation.

title: Psalms 88:1
text: Whether this psalm describes the sufferings of an afflicted believer, or of the Jewish nation under the figure of an individual, is a question upon which commentators are not agreed.  Upon the latter supposition, it belongs, with  Psalms 89:1-52 , to the later period of the Jewish kingdom.  The ancient interpreters refer it to Christ.  This agrees with the New Testament view, which considers the afflictions of Christ's servants, before and after his advent, as parts of one great conflict, in which he, as the Head of his church, is the central and chief sufferer; so that the sorrows of David and other ancient believers who lived before Christ, are conformed to his sorrows, as types to their antitype.

title: Psalms 88:3
text: Man is born to trouble, as the sparks fly upward, or as the waters run downward.  Happy they who improve it in such a manner that their sufferings shall be in this life only, and perfect felicity be their portion in the life to come.

title: Psalms 88:5
text:
Free among the dead; commonly understood to mean, discharged from all the affairs of life, like the dead.  But some prefer to render the words, prostrate among the dead. 
 
  Cut off from thy hand; separated from the care and protection of thy hand, the care which God bestows upon men as inhabitants of this world, which ceases when they are laid in the grave.   Psalms 88:10-12

title: Psalms 88:7
text: Thy waves; the troubles that God brought upon him.

title: Psalms 88:8
text: To be deserted by friends and acquaintances in time of trouble adds greatly to calamities, and shows that no dependence can safely be placed upon any but the Lord, who will never forsake those who put their trust in him.

title: Psalms 88:12
text: In the dark; the grave.

title: Psalms 88:13
text: Prevent thee; meet thee, as one that goes before another in the way.  This is the ancient meaning of the word.

title: Psalms 88:15
text:
Ready to die; in view of the distress that he feared was coming upon him. 
 
The terrors of the Lord on account of sin may be such as to destroy reason, and even life itself; and thre is no security from them but in Christ, who died, the just for the unjust, and will save from sin and its conseqences all who put their trust in him.

title: Psalms 88:17
text: They; the terrors of the Lord with which he was afflicted.

title: Psalms 89:1
text:
This psalm may be viewed as an amplification of the ancient promise of God to David by Nathan,  II Samuel 7:12-17 , with a prayer that God would conform his dealings with his covenant people to it.  It plainly belongs to the later period of the Jewish history, when calamity upon calamity befell the kings of David's line, and with them the nation. 
 
The children of God, even in the deepest trials, have cause to sing of the mercies of the Lord, and praise him for his kindness to the sons of men.

title: Psalms 89:2
text:
Mercy--faithfulness; God's mercy and faithfulness to David and his seed. 
 
  Establish; make as permanent as the heavens.

title: Psalms 89:3
text: My chosen; applied to David, and through him to the Messiah, in whom the predictions of this psalm and many other psalms have their full accomplishment.

title: Psalms 89:7
text: God is to be adored with reverence and holy fear, as well as with confidence and filial affection.

title: Psalms 89:9
text: He who rules the waves of the sea is engaged for the protection of his people, and is able with perfect ease to control the movements of his and their enemies, and cause even their wrath to praise him and advance the good of his chosen.

title: Psalms 89:10
text: Rahab; Egypt, as a representative of the persecuting heathen powers.

title: Psalms 89:12
text:
Tabor; a mountain and city on the confines of Zebulun, in the north-east part of the plain of Esdraelon. 
 
  Hermon; a mountain on the northern border of Palestine.

title: Psalms 89:15
text: The joyful sound; calling the people to the worship of God.

title: Psalms 89:16
text: If sinners are ever exalted, it must be, not on account of their own righteousness, but through the righteousness of God, which is unto and upon all that believe.

title: Psalms 89:19
text: To thy holy one; to David, and in David to Christ, in whom alone the promise has its perfect fulfilment.

title: Psalms 89:20
text: Anointed him; the holy oil by which David was consecrated to the kingly office was a symbol of the Holy Spirit, who came upon him from the day of his anointing,  I Samuel 16:13 ; and who was given to Christ without measure at his baptism.

title: Psalms 89:25
text: His hand; his ruling hand.

title: Psalms 89:27
text: No earthly kings can be compared in excellence, dignity, honor, and glory with the Son of God.  He is the chief among ten thousand, altogether lovely, the brightness of Jehovah's glory, and the express image of his person, in whom dwells the fulness of the godhead bodily.

title: Psalms 89:30
text: His children; David's children, who occupied the earthly throne on Zion.

title: Psalms 89:33
text: Utterly take from him; by rejecting his house, as he did the house of Saul.   II Samuel 7:15

title: Psalms 89:36
text:
His seed shall endure for ever, and his throne as the sun; this is true of Christ and his people. 
 
The covenant of God with Christ, and through him with his people, is an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things and sure.  Those who become interested in it, by the mighty power of God through faith unto salvation.

title: Psalms 89:39
text: Made void the covenant; as it seemed to the psalmist, but not in reality; for God's present dealings with the family of David were in accordance with the threatening contained in the original promise,  II Samuel 7:14 , repeated afterwards by David in his last charge to Solomon,  I Chronicles 28:9 , and by God himself in a vision of Solomon,  II Chronicles 7:19-20 .

title: Psalms 89:40
text: His hedges; the hedges which God had built around David and his kingdom.

title: Psalms 89:47
text: How short my time is; in view of the shortness of life and the approach of death, he beseeches God to manifest his loving-kindness, that life may not be filled with trouble and sorrow.  This thought is prominent in the book of Job.

title: Psalms 89:48
text: The time of man's continuance upon the earth must be short.  He should therefore do the work assigned him with fidelity, and in such a manner that when absent from the body he may be present with the Lord.

title: Psalms 89:52
text: Amen, and Amen; this doxology closes the third ancient division of the Psalms.

title: Psalms 90:1
text:
This psalm is a peculiar in its character as in its authorship.  Its theme is the brevity of human life, and the sorrow that attends it, both being considered as the fruit of sin.  It is very appropriate to the closing period of Israel's sojourn in the wilderness of Arabia, where Moses saw the evil generation which he had led out of Egypt continually wasting away before his eyes; while he and Aaron his brother were doomed to die in the same wilderness. 
 
  Dwelling-place; place of refuge, rest, and comfort. 
 
The eternity and unchangeableness of Jehovah, and the freeness, richness, and abundance of his grace, are an unfailing refuge, support, and comfort to his people.

title: Psalms 90:4
text: A thousand years; God does not estimate time as we do.  To him no duration can be long.   II Peter 3:8

title: Psalms 90:7
text: Death is sent by Jehovah, and is an expression of his anger against the sins of men.  Dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return, is the decision of the Almighty, and all generatins have been an illustration of its truth.

title: Psalms 90:8
text: In the light of thy countenance; our sins are all seen and duly appreciated by God.

title: Psalms 90:9
text: As a tale that is told; or, as a thought which flits through the mind and then is gone.

title: Psalms 90:11
text: Who knoweth--thy wrath; this verse may be literally rendered, "Who knoweth the power of thine anger; and, according to thy fear, thy wrath?" that is, Who knoweth thy wrath, as true reverence for thine awful majesty demands?  It is greater than all men's fears; they can never comprehend its terribleness nor extent.

title: Psalms 90:12
text:
Wisdom; from above, and that will avail to salvation. 
 
Divine teaching alone can give that wisdom which is essential to true happiness in this world, and to blessedness in the world to come.  All should, therefore, habitually and earnestly seek it.

title: Psalms 90:13
text: Return, O Lord; cease from afflicting us, and visit us anew with prosperity.

title: Psalms 90:16
text: Thy work; of love and mercy.

title: Psalms 90:17
text:
The beauty of the Lord; the light of his countenance and the joys of his presence. 
 
  Establish thou the work of our hands; cause it to be continued and to prosper. 
 
God is the author and finisher of all good works.  With his presence and blessing they will continue to prosper.  Men must die, and leave many things unfinished; but God lives.  His cause will extend, and by such instruments as he shall raise up, will ultimately triumph.

title: Psalms 91:1
text:
The present is the first of ten anonymous psalms which seem to belong to the same age.  They are all of a joyous character, anticipating, in the language of faith and hope, the triumph of God's people over all evil.  Their general character gives them a peculiar adaptation to the public worship of God in all ages. 
 
The change of persons in the psalm now before us is remarkable.  The writer announces as his theme the safety of the believer who dwells under God's protection,  Psalms 91:1 ; he speaks of himself as such a believer,  Psalms 91:2 , he addresses such a believer,  Psalms 91:3-13 ; and finally,  Psalms 91:14-16 , God addresses the believer. 
 
  Secret place of the Most High; his pavilion, in which he hides his friends from all harm.   Psalms 27:5 Psalms 31:20 .  We dwell in the secret place of the Most High by faith in him and habitual communion with him. 
 
Habitual access to God is a source of perpetual and perfect security.

title: Psalms 91:3
text:
The snare of the fowler; the plots of crafty foes.   Psalms 124:7  
 
  Noisome; destructive.

title: Psalms 91:5
text:
Terror; danger that causes terror. 
 
  By night--by day; they whom God protects shall be safe from every danger. 
 
From the numerous evils by night and by day to which the wicked are exposed, those who trust in the Lord shall be delivered.

title: Psalms 91:7
text: A thousand--ten thousand; a definite for an indefinite number.

title: Psalms 91:9
text: Because thou hast made--habitation; this verse may be literally rendered thus: "For thou, Lord, art my refuge; thou hast made the Most High thy habitation."  As in  Psalms 91:2-3 , he first speaks of himself as a believer, and then addresses the believer.  We make the Lord our dwelling-place, by habitually resorting to him for comfort and protection.

title: Psalms 91:10
text: There shall no evil befall thee; this promise is not inconsistent with the chastisement wherewith God visits his people for their profit, that they may be "partakers of his holiness;" this, though for the present "not joyous, but grievous," is no evil, but a rich blessing.

title: Psalms 91:11
text: To the heirs of salvation, angels are ministering spirits; in the path of duty God will protect them from all evil, or sanctify his dispensations to their highest good.

title: Psalms 91:12
text: Dash; stumble by striking.  To be kept from stumbling, is to be kept in the way of truth and safety.   Proverbs 3:23   These words contain no promise of protection when we tempt God by needlessly exposing ourselves to danger.   Matthew 4:5-7

title: Psalms 91:13
text:
Tread upon; overcome. 
 
  Lion--adder--young lion--dragon; enemies of all classes, the strong and the subtle, the fierce and the malignant.

title: Psalms 91:14
text: Known my name; been acquainted with my character, and confided in my care.

title: Psalms 91:15
text: God's people are not exempt from trouble; but the have his promise that in all their trials he will be with them and deliver them and make them partakers of his everlasting salvation.

title: Psalms 92:4
text: Thy work; thy providential dealings with the righteous and the wicked, as shown in this psalm.

title: Psalms 92:5
text: The righteous understand God's government, and triumph with holy gladness in the everlasting protection and salvation which it secures to them.

title: Psalms 92:6
text:
A brutish man--a fool; one who is ignorant of God and estranged from him.  Such men are short-sighted, and make the enjoyment of this world their chief good, not foreseeing the destruction which God is about to bring upon them. 
 
  This; God's works and thoughts, especially as manifested in the salvation of the righteous, and the destruction of the wicked. 
 
The wicked understand not the ways of God's providence, and are not aware that the present prosperity which they abuse will be the occasion of their ruin.

title: Psalms 92:7
text: Spring as the grass; have great present prosperity.

title: Psalms 92:10
text:
My horn; my power and influence. 
 
  Anointed with fresh oil; as was done on festive occasions.  This is to be understood spiritually of the strength, comfort, and prosperity which God imparts to the righteous through his providence, word, and Spirit. 
 
They who put their trust in God shall continually receive from him new strength for the performance of the new services which he requires of them.

title: Psalms 92:11
text:
Mine eye--shall see; the destruction of my enemies. 
 
Since God will, in his own time and way, destroy his enemies, the righteous have no occasion to envy their present greatness and power, or to be disquieted by the wicked devices which they bring to pass.

title: Psalms 92:12
text:
The palm-tree; a tree which becomes very large, affords a refreshing shade, and bears abundance of fruit. 
 
  A cedar in Lebanon; the most majestic and enduring of trees.

title: Psalms 92:13
text: Planted in the house of the Lord; the righteous are figuratively described as planted in God's house, because they derive their strength and fruitfulness from communion with him.

title: Psalms 92:14
text:
Be fat and flourishing; be blessed with great prosperity. 
 
Continued fruitfulness, extending into old age, is one of the "exceeding great and precious promises" which God gives to those who put their trust in him and are faithful in his service.

title: Psalms 92:15
text: The righteous and the wicked here dwell together, and appear in many respects alike; but in the end, God will make such a difference between them as shall manifest to all his uprightness in the administration of his government.

title: Psalms 93:1
text: Established; the idea is, that He who has by his omnipotence established the world and made it immovable, can sustain his people in all trials and dangers, and make them victorious over all their foes.

title: Psalms 93:2
text: God is unchangeable; the same yesterday, today, and for ever.  Those who trust in him will never be disappointed.

title: Psalms 93:3
text: The floods; the waters of the great deep, here representing the tumultuous and angry resistance of the nations to God's authority.  Psalms 2:1

title: Psalms 93:4
text:
Mightier than--many waters; able to control alike the raging billows of the sea, and the angry passions of men, for the accomplishment of his own glorious designs. 
 
God's control over the angry passions of men is as absolute as over the fiercest elements of nature.  He overrules them as he does "fire and hail, snow and vapor," and "stormy wind," for the accomplishment of his glorious purposes.

title: Psalms 93:5
text:
Thy testimonies; the declarations of thy word. 
 
As Jehovah is holy, he requires his people to be holy; and without holiness no man can worship him acceptably in this world, or be prepared for his presence in the world to come.

title: Psalms 94:1
text:
Show thyself; as the protector of thy people, able and ready to save them and punish those who rise up against them. 
 
Jehovah is a God of justice as well as mercy, and in the end will treat every man according to his work.

title: Psalms 94:5
text: Thy heritage; Israel, as a "peculiar treasure" unto God "above all people."   Exodus 19:5

title: Psalms 94:7
text: The wicked act as if there were no God, or as if he did not regard them or their doings.

title: Psalms 94:8
text: Brutish--fools; the persons mentioned in the preceding verse, whose ignorance of God leads them to feel and act as though he did not see them or their works.

title: Psalms 94:12
text:
Chastenest; the immediate reference is to the chastisement which God administers through the agency of the wicked spoken of in the preceding verses; but the words apply to chastisement in the widest sense. 
 
  Teachest--out of thy law; in connection with thy chastening hand. 
 
When God chastens his people, he teaches them by his Spirit out of his word.  The teaching of his Spirit with his chastening rod makes them wise unto eternal life, and thus most blessed for evermore.

title: Psalms 94:13
text: They who meekly submit themselves to God's chastisement, and learn the rich lessons of heavenly wisdom which it offers, shall find in God a sure resting place from trouble, and shall see the overthrow of the wicked who sought their destruction.

title: Psalms 94:14
text: His inheritance; his people.

title: Psalms 94:15
text:
Judgment shall return unto righteousness; from which it seemed for a time to have departed.  Whatever present appearances may be, all the dealings of God will in the end appear to be righteous. 
 
  Shall follow it; shall welcome the return of God's righteous judgment, and follow its path with joy.

title: Psalms 94:17
text:
Almost dwelt in silence; would soon have died and been silent in the grave. 
 
The pious ascribe the continuance of all their blessings to the grace of God, and give him the glory.

title: Psalms 94:19
text:
Thoughts; anxious and distracting thoughts. 
 
  Thy comforts; the consolations which thou givest.  These come in to cheer and tranquillize my spirit. 
 
Communion with God is a sure relief from anxious and distracting cares.

title: Psalms 94:20
text:
The throne of iniquity; of wicked rulers who enact unjust and cruel laws. 
 
Laws of mischief and thrones of iniquity, though having transient power by God's permission, are offensive to him, and must receive his frown.

title: Psalms 94:22
text: The Lord will defend his people, and bring upon their enemies the evils which they thought to bring upon others; and though for a time the wicked may seem to prosper, they will finally perish, and have none to help them.

title: Psalms 94:23
text: Their own iniquity; its destructive effects.

title: Psalms 95:1
text: The service of God should be the employment, and the praises of God the joy of every heart.

title: Psalms 95:4
text: Deep places; inmost recesses.

title: Psalms 95:7
text:
People of his pasture; whom he guides, guards, and nourishes. 
 
  Hear his voice; obey his commands. 
 
Nothing should hinder us from devoting the present time to God, lest, if we procrastinate, life should end, and all opportunity and inclination to serve him be lost for ever.

title: Psalms 95:8
text: Provocation--temptation; in the Hebrew, these words are Meribah and Massah, the same as in  Exodus 17:7 , which mean "chiding," and "temptation."  The conduct of the Israelites at Massah and Meribah is mentioned as an example of their spirit of unbelief and rebellion.

title: Psalms 95:10
text: Err in their heart; err from the path of duty through an unbelieving heart.

title: Psalms 95:11
text:
My rest; the land of Canaan, an emblem of heaven. 
 
Though God waits upon the wicked with much long-suffering and patience, if they continue in sin he will at last exclude them for ever from the rest of heaven, and punish them according to their deserts.

title: Psalms 96:1
text:
We have here another of those noble psalms in which the writer, under the illumination of the Holy Ghost, anticipates and predicts the conversion of all the nations to God.  It constitutes, with slight variations, a part of the psalm that David delivered to Asaph to sing, when the ark was removed to Zion.   I Chronicles 16:23-33  
 
  A new song; for new displays of his glory.

title: Psalms 96:2
text: The great business of all should be to embrace and make known the salvation which God has provided for lost and guilty men.

title: Psalms 96:4
text: They who love God earnestly desire that their fellow men should know and serve him.

title: Psalms 96:5
text: The nations; heathen nations.

title: Psalms 96:6
text: Strength and beauty are in his sanctuary; it is there that he dwells and reveals himself to his worshippers in his strength and beauty.   Psalms 63:2

title: Psalms 96:8
text: The glory of all the good done or enjoyed in this world belongs to God, and should be publicly given to him.

title: Psalms 96:9
text: Fear before him, all the earth; exhortations like this, given by the spirit of prophecy, contain in themselves a pledge of the future conversion of all nations.

title: Psalms 96:10
text:
The world also shall be established; this includes both the right ordering of nature, and the right government of human affairs.  As the powers of nature obey God from age to age, so will he finally bring all nations into a state of permanent obedience to his authority. 
 
By the extension of true piety over the whole earth, God will finally establish all that is good upon an enduring and unchangeable basis.

title: Psalms 96:13
text:
To judge the earth; by saving the righteous and destroying the wicked. 
 
The coming of God to save his people and judge the world in righteousness and truth, is anticipated with great joy by those that love him.

title: Psalms 97:1
text:
In  Psalms 97:1-98:9  God's sovereignty over all the earth is set forth, with special reference to the overthrow of his enemies. 
 
The universal and perfect government of God is a source of unspeakable joy to all who love him.

title: Psalms 97:2
Psalms 97:3
text: The government of God is a source of terror and destruction to his enemies.

title: Psalms 97:5
text: When God appears, to fulfil his promises and execute his threatenings, all opposition vanishes before him and all difficulties disappear.

title: Psalms 97:6
text: Though a great portion of the earth is still ignorant of God and his ways, the time is coming when all shall behold his glory and rejoice in his love.

title: Psalms 97:7
text: All ye gods; applied in the New Testament to the angels, as the psalm itself is to Christ.   Hebrews 1:6

title: Psalms 97:8
text: Daughters of Judah; the people of Judah, as representing God's church.

title: Psalms 97:9
text: All gods; heathen gods.

title: Psalms 97:10
text: Though surrounded with enemies and exposed to numerous dasngers, God will keep all who trust in him through faith unto salvation.

title: Psalms 97:11
text:
Light is sown; as seed destined to produce an abundant harvest. 
 
As the seed which is sown with toil springs up from beneath the clods and yields an abundant harvest; so labor performed in the night of trouble is often, to the righteous, the beginning of great prosperity and joy.

title: Psalms 97:12
text: The holiness of God is a terror to the wicked, but to the righteous a source of great joy.

title: Psalms 98:1
text: The people of God praise him for his victory over sin and death, while they embrace and rejoice in his salvation.

title: Psalms 98:2
text: Made known his salvation: his righteousness; manifested his righteousness in the salvation of his people.  These words are fulfilled in every interposition of God for his people, especially in the mission of his Son.

title: Psalms 98:3
text:
Remembered his mercy and his truth; in the fulfilment of his promises. 
 
The places most distant from Judea, including the remotest heathen nations, shall one day hear of and experience the salvation of God.

title: Psalms 98:9
text: The coming of God to judge the world by Jesus Chrsit, is an event to which the righteous look forward with unspeakable joy.

title: Psalms 99:1
text:
Jehovah, as the King who reigns in Zion, is to be feared and obeyed by all. 
 
  Let the people tremble; let all nations tremble before his majesty, and submit themselves to him. 
 
  Between the cherubim; that overshadowed the ark.  This was the most holy place, from which God manifested his glory.

title: Psalms 99:3
text:
Name; to praise God's name, is to praise his infinite perfections as manifested to men; all these his name comprehends. 
 
The holiness of God forms a just ground for loving, worshipping, and obeying him.   Psalms 99:5 Psalms 99:9

title: Psalms 99:4
text: All God's attributes are in harmony with each other.  His omnipotence is the omnipotence of infinite righteousness.

title: Psalms 99:5
text: His footstool; his early tabernacle.   I Chronicles 28:2

title: Psalms 99:6
text:
Moses--among his priests; Moses was of the family which God selected for the priesthood, and in the institution of the Jewish ritual he performed some priestly functions, as that of consecrating Aaron and his sons with sacrifices.   Leviticus 8:1-36  
 
  Samuel among them that call upon his name; the meaning of this verse is, Moses and Aaron and Samuel among his priests who called on his name.  All three belonged to the priestly order, and are mentioned as eminent examples of men who called on God in intercessory prayer for his people. 
 
Jehovah has in every age been a prayer hearing God, and all who call upon him in spirit and in truth receive a gracious answer.

title: Psalms 99:8
text:
Inventions; sinful deeds, as that of making the golden calf. 
 
Though Jehovah forgives the penitent, he often chastises them for their sins.

title: Psalms 100:1
text:
All nations are called upon to praise Jehovah as their creator, preserver, and benefactor.  This psalm contains, like many others, a prophetic anticipation of the conversion of all the gentile nations. 
 
As the Lord is good to all, all should unite in praising and adoring him.

title: Psalms 100:3
text:
Not we; men must not take to themselves the glory of their own powers, or privileges. 
 
The grace of God is the cause of all the distinctions among the children of men, whereby one has richer blessings and is more favored than another.

title: Psalms 100:4
text: His gates; the place in which he is worshipped.

title: Psalms 100:5
text: Jehovah is the same yesterday, today, and for ever; none who put their trust in him will be disappointed.

title: Psalms 101:1
text:
Mercy and judgment; God's mercy and judgment in exalting David's family to the throne in the place of Saul's.  The psalmist then proceeds to show how he will execute his high office. 
 
They whom God has exalted to high stations, should ascribe to him the praise of all their influence and opportunities to do good.

title: Psalms 101:2
text:
Come unto me; as my helper in the discharge of my duties.  He is conscious that he cannot execute his good intentions without God's aid. 
 
Pious rulers will endeavor, both in the family and in public life, to set a holy example which may be safely and usefully followed by all.

title: Psalms 101:4
text: Know; regard with favor.

title: Psalms 101:6
text:
The faithful of the land; men who are trustworthy, and can be relied on to do their duty. 
 
  Dwell with me; as my servants. 
 
Righteous magistrates will choose only the good and faithful for their conucillors and helpers.

title: Psalms 101:8
text:
Early; literally, morning by morning, that is, with promptness and vigilance. 
 
It is the aim of every good ruler to favor righteousness and put down iniquity.

title: Psalms 102:1
text:
Title.  The affliction which exhausts the psalmist's strength, and threatens to shorten his days, is not simply personal suffering from sickness, but suffering which he shares in common with Zion, and which is caused, in part at least, by the reproaches that he endures for her sake.  This explains why he connects his own restoration with the enlargement of God's people. 
 
Prayer is the unfailing resource of God's people in trouble, and by it they obtain from God the support and comfort which they need.

title: Psalms 102:3
text: Burned; with inward heat.

title: Psalms 102:5
text: My bones cleave to my skin; a description of extreme emaciation.

title: Psalms 102:6
text: Of the desert; or, dwelling in desolate places.

title: Psalms 102:7
text:
A sparrow; the Hebrew word is often used for the smaller birds generally. 
 
  Alone; sitting solitary, as when deprived of its mate or its young.

title: Psalms 102:10
text:
Lifted me up, and cast me down; lifted me up from the ground, that thou mightest dash me against it. 
 
Trials as well as mercies come from God, and when they truly mourn her low estate, the time of her deliverance is near.

title: Psalms 102:11
text: Like a shadow that declineth; that is stretched out at evening, a sign that it is soon to disappear in the darkness of night.

title: Psalms 102:14
text:
Take pleasure in her stones; an affectionate interest in Zion, even in her desolations. 
 
Zion is dear to the friends of God, and when they truly mourn her low estate, the time of her deliverance is near.

title: Psalms 102:15
text:
So; as the effect of God's having mercy upon Zion. 
 
The prosperity of the church glorifies God and brings salvation to men.

title: Psalms 102:18
text: It is God's design that his dealings with his people in one age, should be recorded for the admonition and encouragement of all coming generations.

title: Psalms 102:20
text: Those that are appointed to death; the prisoners whom their enemies had appointed to death.  These words have their highest fulfilment in the redemption which Christ brings to men from the spiritual bondage of sin and death eternal; and to him, as one with the Father, this psalm is applied in the New Testament.   Hebrews 1:10-12

title: Psalms 102:22
text: God is moved with compassion in view of the sorrows which sin has brought upon the human race, and he will one day break the yoke of Satan and set the world free from his dominion.  Then His service shall be the joyful employment of all men.

title: Psalms 102:27
text: Thou art the same; the unchangeable God.

title: Psalms 102:28
text: The unchangeableness of God insures the fulfilment of all his promises, and will perpetuate the blessings of his people for ever.

title: Psalms 103:2
text: The benefits which God bestows are daily renewed, and should be acknowledged with daily thanksgiving.

title: Psalms 103:5
text: Is renewed like the eagle's; so that thou art made continually vigorous and active, like the eagle, even to old age.

title: Psalms 103:7
text: His ways; his ways of dealing with his people.

title: Psalms 103:10
text: Should the Lord deal with us according to our sins, and reward us according to our iniquities, all our blessings would be taken from us, and our souls be visited with indignation and wrath.

title: Psalms 103:15
text: The uncertainty and shortness of human life should lead us to place our affections on things above, and seek the durable riches and righteousness which shall never pass away.

title: Psalms 103:16
text: The wind; the scorching wind from the Arabian desert.  Genesis 41:6 Ezekiel 17:10

title: Psalms 103:17
text: We must soon disappear and be known no more among men; but God's mercy and grace to his church shall endure for ever, and through her ministrations a multitude which no man can number shall be fitted for glory everlasting.

title: Psalms 103:19
text: The government of God extends over all the works of his hands; nothing is so high as to be above his control, or so small and obscure as to escape his notice.

title: Psalms 103:22
text: Since all places of God's dominion are full of his glorious power and goodness, they ought to be fulled with his praises.

title: Psalms 104:1
text: In this psalm the majesty and goodness of God, as manifested in creation and providence, are set forth for the comfort and encouragement of his people.

title: Psalms 104:2
text: Light; the emblem of knowledge, truth, wisdom, purity, and blessedness.

title: Psalms 104:3
text: The waters; the waters above, that constitute the clouds.

title: Psalms 104:4
text: Spirits; or, winds; that is, God makes his ministering angels strong and mighty, like winds and lightning, to execute his will.  So the Greek version, which is followed by the apostle,  Hebrews 1:7 .  But many prefer to render the Hebrew, "Who maketh the winds his messengers, and the flaming fire his ministers."

title: Psalms 104:5
text: The perfections of God as displayed in the works of his hands, call for the united and unceasing praises of all intelligent creatures, and will be the theme of adoring gratitude for ever.

title: Psalms 104:6
text: The waters stood above the mountains; at the creation and at the deluge.

title: Psalms 104:8
text:
They go up--go down; or, The mountains ascend, the valleys descend. The reference will then be to the separation of the dry land from the sea, when, by God's command, the mountains and valleys took their appointed places. 
 
The sources and supply of water with which the earth abounds, are a manifestation of the wisdom, goodness, and power of God, which calls for the grateful and devout acknowledgments of all his people.

title: Psalms 104:9
text: They; the waters.

title: Psalms 104:13
text:
His chambers; his heavenly chambers in the clouds. 
 
  Satisfied; abundantly supplied, and made fruitful.

title: Psalms 104:14
text: The daily food and constant support of all creatures comes from God. he openeth his hand an supplieth the wants of every living thing.

title: Psalms 104:16
text: Trees of the Lord; of God's own planting.

title: Psalms 104:19
text: In the control and order of the elements and of the heavenly bodies, and in the instincts of animals which adapt them to the use and service of man, God shows his wisdom, power, and love, and lays men under special obligations to praise him.

title: Psalms 104:21
text: Seek their meat from God; are dependent upon him, and are supported by his care.

title: Psalms 104:24
text: Thy riches; the products of thy power and kindness.

title: Psalms 104:27
text: These wait all upon thee; look to thee for the supply of their wants.

title: Psalms 104:30
text: Thy Spirit; the author of natural and spiritual life.

title: Psalms 104:31
text: The works of the Lord are perfect and glorious, and a source of joy, not only to his people, but to himself.  All his works praise him, and his saints bless him.

title: Psalms 104:32
text:
It trembleth; before the power of God, as in volcanoes, earthquakes, and tempests. 
 
  They smoke; as mount Sinai at the giving of the law.

title: Psalms 104:35
text: The same glorious attributes of God which have furnished the world to be a residence for man, and provided so richly for the wants of all its inhabitants, will be manifested in the destruction of the wicked who oppose themselves to his righteous government.

title: Psalms 105:1
text: This psalm contains an enumeration of God's wonderful dealings in behalf of his people, from Abraham till their settlement in the land of Canaan.   Psalms 105:1-15 , occurs in the psalm sung on the removal of the ark to mount Zion.   I Chronicles 16:8-22

title: Psalms 105:3
text: The Lord is the source of all excellence and bliss, and those who seek him as their chief good have cause for perpetual gladness and joy.

title: Psalms 105:8
text: His covenant; in which he promised to give to the seed of Abraham the land of Canaan.

title: Psalms 105:10
text: Jehovah is unchangeable, and when the word hath gone out of his mouth it standeth for ever.  Heaven and earth may pass away, but his word will never pass away.

title: Psalms 105:14
text: Reproved kings;  Genesis 12:17

title: Psalms 105:15
text:
Mine anointed; set apart, endowed with special gifts to qualify them for their office. 
 
  Prophets;  Genesis 20:1

title: Psalms 105:16
text: Brake the whole staff; cut off the means of support.  The reference is to the famine which occasioned the descent of Jacob and his family into Egypt.   Genesis 41:53 , etc.

title: Psalms 105:17
text: God raises up deliverers for his people, such as from time to time they need, and sends them to fulfil his promises and accomplish his purposes of love and mercy to his chosen.

title: Psalms 105:19
text:
His word; that is, according to some, the effect of Joseph's word in interpreting the dreams of Pharoah's butler and baker.  Genesis 41:9-14   But others understand by "his word," God's word of promise to Joseph in his early dreams. 
 
  The word of the Lord tried him; God's promise to Joseph tried him by its long delay.

title: Psalms 105:23
text: The land of Ham; Egypt, which was peopled with the descendants of Ham, one of the sons of Noah.

title: Psalms 105:25
text: The condition of nations, as well as of individuals, is ordered by the Lord; he sends prosperity or adversity according to his infinitely wise and good pleasure, and as will promote his own glory and the good of his people.

title: Psalms 105:28
text: They rebelled not; according to some, Moses and Aaron rebelled not, but executed God's commands punctually.  But it is better to understand these words of the Egyptians, who when the plague came relented, as usual, and promised obedience.   Exodus 10:24

title: Psalms 105:37
text: When God would fulfil his purposes of love and mercy, it is vain for men to oppose him.  They may destroy themselves, but they cannot withstand the power of God.

title: Psalms 105:38
text:
The fear of them; the Israelites. 
 
  Fell upon them; the Egyptians.

title: Psalms 105:40
text: The bread of heaven; given miraculously from above.

title: Psalms 105:42
text: His holy promise; to give their descendants the land of Canaan.

title: Psalms 105:44
text:
The labor of the people; the riches accumulated by their labor.  Deuteronomy 6:10-11  
 
The earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof, and when he takes any part of it away from one people on account of their sins, and gives ti to another, he wrongs no one, but does what he will with his own.

title: Psalms 106:1
text: This psalm differs from  Psalms 105:1-45  in being principally occupied with an enumeration of the sins of God's people.  It is supposed to refer especially to the Babylonish captivity, when the hope of speedy restoration had begun to animate the people.

title: Psalms 106:3
text: Whatever may be the state of the wicked, it will be well with those who fear the Lord and delight themselves in his commandments.

title: Psalms 106:8
text:
His name's sake; the display of his perfections. 
 
God deals with his people not according to their deserts, but according to the greatness of his mercy in Jesus Christ.

title: Psalms 106:9
text: The depths; the depths of the sea.

title: Psalms 106:11
text: In the end men will return, and see the difference between the righteous and the wicked; between him that serveth God, and him that serveth him not.

title: Psalms 106:13
text: Waited not for his counsel; did not quietly wait for God to send them help in his own time and way; but when any trial came, as the want of water or food, were very impatient and rebellious

title: Psalms 106:14
text: Lusted; as when they desired flesh.   Exodus 16:3 Numbers 11:4

title: Psalms 106:15
text: What wicked men desire, God may give them in anger as well as in mercy; his gifts may be perverted or abused to bring leanness into the soul.

title: Psalms 106:18
text: A fire was kindled; see  Numbers 16:35 .

title: Psalms 106:20
text:
Their glory; for Jehovah, their real glory, they substituted a calf, the Egyptian idol, a shame to all who worshipped. 
 
No absurdity, wickedness, or folly is so great that wicked men, when left to themselves, may not fall into it.

title: Psalms 106:23
text: Stood--in the breach; as a soldier stands in the breach to keep back the enemy.  See Moses' intercessory prayer to prevent the destruction of Israel.   Exodus 32:30-34

title: Psalms 106:24
text: Despised the pleasant land; upon the return of the spies.  Numbers 14:1-5

title: Psalms 106:26
text: The wickedness of men is the cause of their calamities, and God in this life punishes men less than their iniquities deserve.

title: Psalms 106:28
text:
Baal-peor; one of the idol-gods of Moab. 
 
  The dead; dead idols as opposed to the living God.  See the narrative,  Numbers 25:3 , etc.

title: Psalms 106:30
text: Executed judgment; by slaying the transgressors,  Numbers 25:6-8 .

title: Psalms 106:33
text: The most meek and patient of men may be provoked to feel, speak, and act wrong, so as to bring distress upon themselves and others.

title: Psalms 106:37
text: Devils; demons, "unclean spirits," such as the idols of the heathen represented.   I Corinthians 10:20

title: Psalms 106:39
text: Men are prone to follow their own inventions, rather than the revealed will of God.

title: Psalms 106:45
text:
His covenant; which he made with Abraham, to give his posterity the land of Canaan. 
 
The covenant of God standeth sure, and though men may despise its blessings God remembers it, and in due time will fulfil all its promises.

title: Psalms 106:48
text:
Amen; so be it, or let it be.  This doxology marks the close of the fourth book into which the Psalms were anciently divided. 
 
All the hope of God's people is in him, and it is for his glory that their hope in his mercy and grace should not be disappointed.

title: Psalms 107:1
text: The theme of this psalm is God's goodness in delivering the afflicted of various classes.  It may have special reference to the restoration of God's people from captivity; but is manifestly designed for general application.

title: Psalms 107:2
text: All deliverances should be acknowledged with devout thanksgiving; but they whom the Lord has redeemed from sin and death eternal, have the most abundant cause to bless him for his goodness, and for his wonderful works to the children of men.

title: Psalms 107:3
text: Gathered them; from the lands in which they had been dispersed on account of their sins.

title: Psalms 107:10
text:
Darkness and--shadow of death; imprisoned in dark dungeons. 
 
  Bound in affliction and iron; afflicted by being bound in iron fetters; referring to men whom God has given over to imprisonment as a chastisement for their sins.

title: Psalms 107:11
text: Sin is the cause of all the troubles with which men are afflicted, and their deliverance from it is often designed by Jehovah in bringing calamities upon them.

title: Psalms 107:12
text: Labor; the original word denotes sorrowful toil.

title: Psalms 107:16
text: No calamities of men in this life are so great that the Lord cannot deliver them, even should they be like those of Manasseh in chains, or Daniel in the dungeon, or Jonah in the whale's belly.

title: Psalms 107:17
text:
Fools; in the scriptural sense;  that is, transgressors of God's law. 
 
  Are afflicted; with sickness,  Psalms 107:18 Psalms 107:20 .  The holy Scriptures regarded sickness as well as all other suffering, as the fruit of sin.

title: Psalms 107:22
text: The blessings which God bestows should be acknowledged with devout thanksgiving, and bind the soul in sweet and hearty obedience to his service.

title: Psalms 107:28
text: The deliverance of seamen and such as do business on the sea, should inspire them especially with a conviction of the goodness of God, their dependence on him, and their obligations to love and obey him.

title: Psalms 107:30
text: Men may be glad without being grateful, and rejoice in the gift without giving glory to the Giver.

title: Psalms 107:33
text: Turneth rivers into a wilderness; the psalm closes with God's providential dealings with nations.

title: Psalms 107:35
text: National, not less than individual prosperity depends upon God's blessing, which will rest only upon the people who acknowledge his supremacy and obey his word.

title: Psalms 107:38
text: The increase of worldly substance and of the comfort derived from it is of the Lord, an lays the possessor under increasing obligations to learn and do his will.

title: Psalms 107:43
text:
These things; the course of God's providence. 
 
  The loving-kindness of the Lord; towards those who truly repent of sin, and seek him with the whole heart. 
 
A careful attention to the dealings of God with men will show his loving kindness and tender mercy to all who put their trust in him.

title: Psalms 108:1
text:
This psalm is a combination, with some variations, of  Psalms 57:7-11 , and  Psalms 60:5-12 .  See the notes on these passages. 
 
This psalm is a combinatin, with some variations, of  Psalms 57:7-11 , and  Psalms 60:5-12 .  See the notes on these passages. 
 
The most exalted employment of the tongue is in singing God's praises and showing forth his wondrous works.

title: Psalms 108:7
text: The providential dealings of God in enlarging a people, call for devout acknowledgment and thanksgiving.

title: Psalms 108:11
text: Prosperity and adversity are both the servants of God.  They go and come at his bidding, and accomplish his infinitely wise and benevolent designs.

title: Psalms 109:1
text: The full application of this psalm is to Christ.  To David, as the earthly head of God's people, acting in their behalf and persecuted for their sake, it had a real but subordinate application.  The imprecations which it contains were uttered by God's Spirit.  II Samuel 23:2 Acts 2:30   They are the denunciation of God's vengeance upon the persecutors of his people, whose cause David represented in  a lower sense, and which was to be afterwards represented in the fullest sense in the person of the promised Messiah.

title: Psalms 109:4
text: The unfailing resource of God's people in trouble is prayer.  However they may be treated by men, his ears are ever open to their cry.

title: Psalms 109:5
text: The Saviour's love was rewarded with hatred and persecution, and his disciples should not be surprised or dismayed if they are called to suffer in like manner.

title: Psalms 109:6
text:
Him; probably referring to Ahithophel, whose treachery foreshadowed that of Judas, to whom the words are applied in the New Testament.  Acts 1:16-20  
 
  At his right hand; as an enemy and accuser.   Zechariah 3:1   The meaning is, that the traitor shall be given over to the power of Satan. The curses enumerated in this and the following verses, are those threatened in the law against the wicked and their posterity. 
 
The hatred and malice which men show towards Christ's faithful servants he will consider as shown towards himself, and will recompense accordingly; and as there is no sin so great as that of persecuting Christ, whether in his own person or that of his followers, so there is no sin which brings upon men such a terrible retribution.

title: Psalms 109:9
text: The rejection of Christ by one generation has often been a source of dreadful misery to many following generations.  This applies alike to families and nations.

title: Psalms 109:14
text: The iniquity of his fathers; compare  Exodus 20:5  and our Saviour's words,  Matthew 23:34-36 Luke 11:49-51 .  It is by consenting to and imitating the evil deeds of their fathers, that the children bring their iniquities upon themselves.

title: Psalms 109:16
text: Persecution of the poor and needy is highly displeasing to God, and brings down his curse on those who inflict it.

title: Psalms 109:21
text: The necessities of sinners furnish an occasion for God's glorifying himself in the display of his mercy and grace; and this may be pleaded as a reason why he should interpose in their behalf.

title: Psalms 109:23
text:
When it declineth; is stretched out at evening, and ready to vanish. 
 
  As the locust; when driven before the wind.

title: Psalms 109:26
text: All the hope of the penitent is in the mercy of God through Jesus Christ, and to him they apply for the blessings which they need.

title: Psalms 109:27
text: That this is thy hand; that this deliverance for which I pray comes from thee.

title: Psalms 109:28
text: When God blesses us the curses of the wicked can do us no harm.

title: Psalms 109:30
text: Among the multitude; when I pay my vows for thy deliverance before the great congregation.  See notes on  Psalms 22:25-29 .

title: Psalms 110:1
text:
The Lord; Jehovah. 
 
  My Lord; Jesus Christ, of whom this psalm is a remarkable prediction. 
 
  Sit thou at my right hand; to sit at God's right hand, is to be invested by God with universal dominion.   Matthew 28:18  
 
Christ is both "the root and the offspring of David."  He unites in himself a proper human with a proper divine nature, and is thus qualified to be the "one Mediator between God and men."

title: Psalms 110:2
text:
The rod of thy strength; the rod by which thou exercisest thy strength. 
 
  Out of Zion; the residence of God.  Compare  Psalms 20:2 .  When the Father invests the Son with universal dominion, he also gives him "all power in heaven and in earth." 
 
As God has invested the Messiah with universal dominion and almighty power, no opposition can prevail against him.

title: Psalms 110:3
text:
Be willing; willing to enlist under thy banner. 
 
  From the womb of the morning; like dewdrops that spring out of the womb of the morning. 
 
  Dew of thy youth; youthful vigor perpetuated from age to age like the morning dew.  The perpetual succession of his followers. 
 
The perpetuation of Christ's church from age to age, depends not on the will of man, but on the power of God, who has promised his Son that he "shall see his seed," and "shall justify many."

title: Psalms 110:4
text:
Hath sworn; see  Hebrews 7:20-22 . 
 
  The order of Melchizedek; who was both king and priest without regard to priestly genealogy, and without any one like him to precede or succeed him.  See on the priesthood of Christ, as compared with that of Aaron's family,  Hebrews 7:1-28 . 
 
In the Lord Jesus we have a Priest to make expiation for our sins, as well as a King to conquer sin within us and around us.

title: Psalms 110:5
text:
Strike through kings; destroy those who continue to oppose thee. 
 
The dominion of Christ is as terrible to his enemies as it is glorious to his friends.

title: Psalms 110:7
text:
Drink of the brook; probably, as the warrior drinks without halting and renews his strength. 
 
  Lift up the head; in immortal vigor. 
 
Since the power of Christ can never fail, they that wait upon him shall continually renew their strength.

title: Psalms 111:1
text: Ps 111.1-119.176 probably belongs to the earlier days of the restoration from the Babylonish captivity.

title: Psalms 111:2
text:
Sought out; carefully investigated and pondered, on account of the wisdom, power, faithfulness, and love displayed in them. 
 
In order duly to appreciate the works of God, their wisdom, excellence, and love must be sought out.

title: Psalms 111:5
text: The Lord will ever be mindful of and supply the wants of his people.

title: Psalms 111:7
text: Sure; trustworthy; commandments which we can obey with full confidence in their truth and equity.

title: Psalms 111:9
text: The redemption of Israel from their bondage in Egypt and in Babylon was an emblem of the deliverance of God's people from the slavery of sin, and their introduction to the liberty of the sons of God.

title: Psalms 111:10
text:
The beginning of wisdom; that which constitutes the foundation of all true wisdom. 
 
The sum and substance of true wisdom is to fear God and keep his commandments.

title: Psalms 112:2
text: The blessed effects of obeying God may descend to many and even to all generations.

title: Psalms 112:4
text:
Light in the darkness; help and deliverance in distress. 
 
Light is sown for the righteous, and gladness for the upright in heart. Weeping may endure for a night, but light cometh in the morning.

title: Psalms 112:5
text:
Discretion; in the original, judgment, that is, equity. 
 
A good man will be conscientious and faithful in the discharge of his secular as well as religious duties.

title: Psalms 112:6
text: Shall not be moved for ever; shall have prosperity that is immovable and perpetual.

title: Psalms 112:8
text:
Shall not be afraid; of the evils which threaten the wicked. 
 
Trust in God keeps the souls of his people in peace, while others are quaking with apprehension of evils that are coming upon them.

title: Psalms 112:9
text: His horn shall be exalted; his prosperity shall be increased.

title: Psalms 112:10
text:
The wicked shall see it; the salvation of the righteous. 
 
The end will show the difference between the righteous and the wicked, between him that serveth God and him that serveth him not.

title: Psalms 113:3
text:
The Lord's name; his perfections, by the displays of which he is known. 
 
The time is coming when all nations shall worship and adore the Lord for what he is, and for what he has done among the children of men.

title: Psalms 113:6
text: Who humbleth himself to behold; or, as the original seems to mean, who looketh down deep upon; that is, who, though he is exalted so high above heaven and earth, yet with his omnipotent glance beholds every thing in them.  Compare  Psalms 33:13-14 .

title: Psalms 113:7
text:
The dunghill; from the deepest depression and distress. 
 
The deliverance and enlargement which God grants to his afflicted servants in this world, are fortastes and pledges of the perfect salvation which he will bestow on them in the world to come.

title: Psalms 114:2
text:
His sanctuary; the place where God dwelt and was worshipped. 
 
  His dominion; the people over whom he ruled in a special sense.

title: Psalms 114:3
text:
Fled; became dry. 
 
All nature is under the control of Jehovah, and is obedient to his will.

title: Psalms 114:4
text: Skipped; leaped, that is, quaked.   Exodus 19:18 Psalms 29:6 .

title: Psalms 114:7
text: Creation feels the presence of Jehovah, and is dependent on him for its existence and condition.

title: Psalms 114:8
text:
Turned the rock into a standing water; as was the case in the wilderness. 
 
The miraculous provision which God made for the wants of Israel in the wilderness, is an emblem of the inexhaustible supplies of grace which he has in store for all who put their trust in him.

title: Psalms 115:1
text: Mercies are bestowed upon the people of God, not on account of their own merits, but for the sake of his own glory through Jesus Christ.

title: Psalms 115:4
text: Their idols; the idols of the heathen.

title: Psalms 115:8
text:
Like unto them; stupid and senseless as the objects of their worship. 
 
The stupidity and folly of idolatry are exceeding great, and its universality among nations unenlightened by God's word, is a terrible evidence of the desperate blindness and perverseness of the natural heart.

title: Psalms 115:13
text: Those who fear the Lord and put their trust in him will receive from him all needed good, whatever may be their condition in life.

title: Psalms 115:17
text: As the dead cannot praise the Lord on earth, we should diligently employ life and health in his service.

title: Psalms 116:1
text: The goodness of God in hearing and answering prayer lays us under special obligations to love and adore him, and to continue to call upon him as long as we live.

title: Psalms 116:2
text: Inclined his ear; heard my supplications.

title: Psalms 116:3
text: Sorrows of death--pains of hell; the anguish occasioned by deadly perils.

title: Psalms 116:6
text: Simple; those who feel their ignorance and need of divine teaching.

title: Psalms 116:7
text: Jehovah is the only sure and permanent rest of the soul, and those who reject him will remain restless for ever.

title: Psalms 116:10
text:
I believed; in the promised faithfulness of God. 
 
  Have I spoken; of the deliverance and preservation which God has vouchsafed to me.   Psalms 116:6-8  
 
Faith in God as a prayer-hearing and sin-forgiving God, affords great encouragement to continue to call upon him.

title: Psalms 116:11
text:
In my haste; in my dismay occasioned by the sorrows of death and the pains of hell.   Psalms 31:22  
 
  Liars; undeserving of my confidence.  In his trouble he turned away from all human help to God.

title: Psalms 116:13
text: The cup of salvation; which commemorated his deliverance from trouble.

title: Psalms 116:15
text: The death of God's people, as well as their life, is under his control and an object of his special care.

title: Psalms 116:16
text: Loosed my bonds; his bonds of affliction.

title: Psalms 116:18
text: Those who in time of trouble have vowed unto the Lord, shoud be careful when he delivers them to acknowledge him with praise.

title: Psalms 117:1
text: In this short psalm all the gentle nations are called upon to praise God for his goodness to his covenant people.  They all have an interest in the welfare of Israel, since it is from Israel that the knowledge of God is to go forth through all the earth.  See note to  Psalms 67:1 .

title: Psalms 117:2
text: The unchangeable goodness and truth of Jehovah are a just foundation for confidence in him; the greatness of his mercy towards those who embrace it is beyond all finite comprehension, and calls for unceasing gratitude and praise.

title: Psalms 118:1
text: This psalm was evidently composed to be sung on the occasion of some national festivity, apparently in connection with a solemn procession to the sanctuary; but the period to which it belongs cannot be certainly determined.  Many refer it to the solemnities connected with the foundation of the second temple.   Ezra 3:10-13   It might, perhaps, with still more propriety be referred to the dedication of the second temple.   Ezra 6:16-18

title: Psalms 118:5
text:
I called; the psalmist speaks here in the name of God's people, and so throughout the psalm. 
 
  Set me in a large place; delivered me from restraints and embarrassments.

title: Psalms 118:7
text: See; the destruction of my enemies.

title: Psalms 118:9
text: It is better to trust the Lord than to put confidence in men, however honorable or exalted.

title: Psalms 118:10
text: Me; the psalmist, as the representative of God's people.

title: Psalms 118:12
text:
The fire of thorns; which is soon extinguished. 
 
The assaults of the wicked upon God's people, however formidable they may appear in the beginning, will end in their own overthrow.

title: Psalms 118:13
text: Thou; the enemy of Israel.

title: Psalms 118:14
text: God is the source of defence and of joy to his people, and will not disappoint any who put their trust in him.

title: Psalms 118:18
text: God afflicts his people, not for their destruction, but for their profit; however great their sufferings, he will in the end deliver them.

title: Psalms 118:20
text: This gate of the Lord; which led into the sanctuary, the place of his worship; supposed to have been said as the solemn procession reached the sanctuary.

title: Psalms 118:21
text: My salvation; his deliverer from death.

title: Psalms 118:22
text:
The stone which the builders refused; originally applied to Israel as despised and rejected by the heathen nations, but chosen of God and exalted by him to the most honorable office: afterwards applied by Christ to himself as rejected by the Jewish builders, but exalted by God to be head over all things to his body the church.  The first application includes the second, since Christ is the head and representative of the true Israel. 
 
  The head-stone; which unites the building together. 
 
In selecting the means and instruments of establishing his kingdom in the world, God acts in a manner very contrary to human wisdom, "that no flesh should glory in his presence."

title: Psalms 118:23
text: This; which is done in the head-stone.

title: Psalms 118:24
text: This is the day; the day of salvation to Israel.

title: Psalms 118:26
text: He that cometh in the name of the Lord; applied by the multitude to Christ with his approbation, when he entered Jerusalem as the King of Israel.

title: Psalms 118:27
text: Bind the sacrifice; preparatory to offering it as a token of gratitude to God.

title: Psalms 118:28
text: My God; he not only had a God, but by the spirit of adoption could say, My God.

title: Psalms 118:29
text: The goodness of God in hearing and and answering the prayers of his people should ever be acknowledged with gratitude, thanksgiving, and praise.

title: Psalms 119:1
text:
This is an alphabetic psalm of peculiar structure.  The first eight verses begin each with the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, the next eight with the second letter, and so on.  It is wholly occupied with the commendation of God's word under various titles, expressive of the various aspects in which it may be viewed.  Thus it is called his word, as that which he has spoken to us; his law, given as the rule of our life; his commandments and precepts, laid upon us to be kept; his statutes, established as the laws of his kingdom; his judgments, as his decisions concerning our duty and destiny; his testamonies, as to his authoritative declaration of truth; and his way, in which we are to walk. 
 
  Undefiled; sincere, upright. 
 
  In the law; according to its requirements.

title: Psalms 119:3
text:
Do no iniquity; allow themselves in no known sin. 
 
The best way to be kept from all iniquity is to be diligently employed in learning and doing the whole will of God.

title: Psalms 119:6
text: They who have respect to all God's commandments have the approbation of conscience, and their hope shall never be disappointed.

title: Psalms 119:9
text:
Taking heed; regulating his life according to the Scriptures. 
 
He who takes the Bible for his guide will walk in safety, purity, and love; and will be preserved from manifold dangers to which he would otherwise be exposed.

title: Psalms 119:11
text: Hid; as a precious treasure to be carefully kept.

title: Psalms 119:15
text: Meditation upon the word and ways of God is a great safeguard to youth, and to those of riper years.

title: Psalms 119:18
text: The mind needs to be spiritually enlightened in order to behold the spiritual meaning, beauty, and excellence of the Scriptures.

title: Psalms 119:19
text: A stranger in the earth; as a stranger has no inheritance in the land of his pilgrimage, so I am as a stranger on the earth, having no inheritance but thy word.  Therefore take not away from me this precious treasure, but let it be before my eyes continually as my comforter,  Psalms 119:54 .

title: Psalms 119:24
text: Those who take counsel of the statutes of God will be likely to be made wise to salvation.

title: Psalms 119:25
text: Cleaveth unto the dust; lies prostrate; a description of deep depression.   Psalms 44:25

title: Psalms 119:26
text:
Have declared; recounted before thee. 
 
  My ways; my goings out and comings in; my whole course of life, with all its cares and sorrows.

title: Psalms 119:28
text: Melteth; pineth away.

title: Psalms 119:30
text: Men must make their duty their delight, or they will not be likely to perform it.

title: Psalms 119:37
text:
Beholding; beholding with delight. 
 
  Vanity; put here for all the vain objects of time and sense to which men look, instead of God, for happiness.

title: Psalms 119:43
text: Take not the word of truth utterly out of my mouth; deal not with me in such a way that I shall be unable to glory in thy word of truth before my enemies, as I have done heretofore.

title: Psalms 119:45
text: At liberty; literally, in a wide place, where I can walk safely and prosperously.

title: Psalms 119:46
text: Those who love God will not be afraid to speak of him before the great and honorable of the earth.

title: Psalms 119:48
text: My hands also will I lift up; as a token of affectionate desire.

title: Psalms 119:49
text: The word; the word of promise.

title: Psalms 119:50
text: This; trust in thy word of promise.

title: Psalms 119:53
text:
Horror; vehement disapprobation. 
 
Pious men are grieved when the wicked break God's law.

title: Psalms 119:55
text: Serious thought and contemplation on the works and ways of God, and on our relations to him and obligations to obey him, are essential to the hearty turning of the soul to his service.

title: Psalms 119:56
text: This I had; the comfort mentioned above,  Psalms 119:54 .  But some render the verse thus: "This I have, that I keep thy precepts;" meaning, "This I have as my heritage, or the portion of my soul, that I keep thy precepts."  Compare  Psalms 119:111 .

title: Psalms 119:59
text: My ways; comparing them with thy law.

title: Psalms 119:61
text: The bands of the wicked have robbed me; or, the snares of the wicked have encompassed me.

title: Psalms 119:64
text: Full of thy mercy: teach; do thou, whose goodness fills the earth, show thy goodness to me by teaching me thy statutes.  Compare Ps 119.58.

title: Psalms 119:67
text: Afflictions are often made the means of reclaiming the soul from backsliding, and thus promoting its highest good.s

title: Psalms 119:70
text: Fat; pampered in worldly pleasures, and insensible to spiritual goods.

title: Psalms 119:72
text: No earthly good is so precious or useful as the keeping of the divine commands.

title: Psalms 119:74
text: The deliverance of a pious soul from trouble gives great joy to the people of God.

title: Psalms 119:79
text: Turn unto me; in love and confidence.  This is the effect of the witnessing God's bountiful dealings with him.
